items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 10-12% for the whole business
items.quote: we would still stay between the guidance that we have given of 10 -12% considering the fact that we have 2 new plants that have already bee n commissioned.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 10-12% despite two good quarters
items.quote: we would like to be cautiously optimistic about the guidance that we give on EBITDA and although we have had 2 good quarters, but we still maintain, our expectations of EBITDA to stay between 10% to 12%

items.statement: Vadodara hydrogenation plant commenced production in July 2024 at ~30% capacity
items.quote: We have currently achieved approximately 30% production capacity of the planned capacity only in our third month of operation.

items.statement: Mahad Greenfield site commenced commercial production of Evermoss on 12 Nov 2024
items.quote: we commenced commercial production at our Greenfi eld site located in Mahad, Maharashtra, dedicated towards production of a speciality aroma ingredient called Evermo ss.

items.statement: Incremental revenue of 250-300 crores expected in next 2-3 years from Vadodara, Mahad and process reengineering
items.quote: I think we shouldn't be surprised to probably see an addition of anywhere between 250 to 300 crores in the next R: years to the top line.

items.statement: Destocking and reduced demand discussion has ended in H2 2024; steady demand expected for ingredients
items.quote: the whole discussion on destocking and reduced demand probably has come to an end definitely in H2 2024. Going forward, unless there are no global shocks to any of the major economies, I think we will see a steady demand for most of the products that we sell on the ingredient side

items.statement: Healthy RFQ customer demand visibility for H1 2025
items.quote: we have already had multiple rounds of conversations about H1 2025 demand from our RFQ customers and we see the numbers pretty healthy for the requirement of H1 2025.

items.statement: Camphor and terpene chemical space continues under price pressure
items.quote: the camphor and the terpene chemical sp ace continues to be under a price pressure, multiple reasons, point number one

items.statement: Raw material inventory, availability and pricing broadly stable across fragrance, flavor and aroma ingredients
items.quote: it is safe to say that everything looks stable in terms of inventory, in terms of availability and in terms of pricing on the raw material side.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin improved to 12.08% vs 10.29% QoQ and 4.8% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter has shown a substantial improvement and res ulted in 12.08% as compared to 10.29% on quarter -to-quarter and 4.8% on year -on-year.

items.statement: Depreciation expected to increase to 6.5-7 crores per quarter in FY26
items.quote: Parag, it will be 6.5 to 7 crores a quarter.

items.statement: Existing fragrance/flavor business expected to grow 5-10% in H2; camphor seasonal, off-season uncertain
items.quote: We are seeing that it's going to be a healthy growth of anywhere between 5 to 10 percent. On the camphor side, since it's a cyclical product, we need to kind of wait and watch what happens in the off-season.

items.statement: Cautious on camphor due to price pressures and seasonality; EBITDA guidance kept at 10-12%
items.quote: We are still a bit cautious on the camphor and the terpene chemical side, where we still have some price pressures and we will see how it evolves going forward.

items.statement: Board approved brownfield expansion of 53,000 MTPA Phthalic Anhydride plant at Taloja instead of 80,000 MTPA greenfield in Gujarat
items.quote: Substantial savings in project set-up cost i.e. Rs. 345 crores (brownfield) v/s Rs. 550 crores (greenfield)

items.statement: Project to be funded by ECB/Rupee Term Loans of Rs. 220 crores and Internal Accruals of Rs. 110 crores
items.quote: To be funded by a mix of: ECB/Rupee Term Loans - Rs. 220 crores Internal Accruals - Rs. 110 crores

items.statement: Project IRR expected at 15% for PA5 based on Gross Margin of ~US$200/tonne with payback period of 5.5 years from commissioning
items.quote: Project IRR is expected to be 15% for PA5 based on Gross Margin of ~ US$ 200/ tonnes The payback period of the project is expected to be 5½ years from the date of commissioning

items.statement: Executive Committee authorized additional investment up to GBP 1,000,000 in equity capital of wholly owned subsidiary IGPL International Limited

items.statement: Targeting stable EBITDA margin around 13-14% while pursuing aggressive growth across segments
items.quote: I would say that we are aiming to keep the EBITDA level in a similar range what we have today, because we are still aimin g for a very high and aggressive growth

items.statement: Expecting single-digit order intake growth of 8-10% over last year 9 months
items.quote: order int ake, it would be maybe a single -digit growth, 8% to 10% over last year

items.quote: Our orders on han d is almost ₹2,400 crores. Half of it is the normal business, and half of it is nuclear, ₹1,200 crores and ₹1,200 crores

items.statement: Solar business revenue expected at ₹120 crores this year with receivables of ₹80-85 crores
items.quote: About the business this year, we will do a revenue of maybe ₹120 crores out of solar this year.

items.statement: Export outlook optimistic despite Bangladesh crisis and geopolitical issues; strong pipeline in US energy and Middle East petrochemical
items.quote: But the outlook, I wouldn't say is we are pessimistic on that. I think the outlook is good. We have introduced products which are solely manufactured in our factories. And we are expecting good orders in the project business, in the energy segments from countries like U.S.

items.statement: Capacity increases through lean manufacturing, contract manufacturing, and long-term investments in new locations under 5-10 year planning
items.quote: Capacity increases happens by maybe adding space, adding machinery, and of course with internal improvement measures . So the internal improvement measures by lean manufacturi ng, by all those theories and practical things, this continuously happens

items.quote: I feel a bit awkward to answer or give a co mmitment when it will happen, because it takes two hands to clap . And, today, we are ready and that ’s why you see the things are

items.quote: Solar business, which we do today would not have the same EBITDA m argins as our product business. If I go for, let ’s say, firefighting pump sets, it wouldn ’t give me the same EBITDA level for like my product

items.statement: Domestic standard pump outlook mixed: wastewater and distillery positive, chemical/paper weak, real estate uncertain; overall optimistic for next year
items.quote: We are s eeing a good amount of optimism in the wastewater market, those investments are coming in industry. The distillery segment is again coming back , though, there are bit of a downturn in the chemical , and paper , and other industries

items.statement: New product launches: B pump for wastewater, firefighting products, vertical turbine pumps, non-metallic pumps for chemical, reciprocating pumps for BP&CL
items.quote: We recently launched the B pump, which is not the vertical turbine pump, which is not per se a dealer product. But we are going to launch the – we will come out with fire fighting products, which we already have.

items.statement: Green hydrogen small orders received; plan to localize and participate more as demand picks up in 2-3 years
items.quote: We already have some orders, small business, but we have been successful in this because the product range is available. But we intend to participate more and more as the demand picks up locally, which would happen in the next 2, 3 years.

items.statement: Dealer network at 1,100 (mix of exclusive and non-exclusive); win-win model with dealers holding inventory and doing customization
items.quote: In our terminology, dealers are one who keep the inventory themselves. For us, and I said win -win is because we give them a standard product a nd they do the customization

items.statement: KSB Guard IoT monitoring deployed on all engineered pumps from Shirwal factory; central monitoring from Pune
items.quote: All our pumps which go from our engineered factory in Shirwal, they will have a KSB Guard.

items.statement: Raised INR200 crores via QIP in August 2024 from global investors including Bank of America, Samsung, Citigroup, Societe Generale, Nomura, BNP Paribas, Morgan Stanley; well subscribed with 6.71% dilution at INR53-54 per share
items.quote: we had INR200 crores raised through QIP. And all the global eminent investors, marquee investors like Bank of America, Samsung, Citigroup, Society General, Namura, BNP Paribas, Morgan Stanley, everybody had participated and of course, it was well subscribed.

items.statement: QIP capex allocation INR123 crores for capacity expansion; INR8.5 crores spent so far; civil work in full swing, machinery ordered, medical device erection started; project completion targeted in 18-24 months by end of FY26
items.quote: Out of INR123 crores, only INR8.5 crores has been used for the capex. The rest of the money would be spent as the supplies of machineries and advances start going.

items.statement: Targeting INR5,000 crores revenue by 2030 at ~20% CAGR; medical devices to grow 25-26%, other businesses 15-20%; EBITDA margin target 15% in 3 years, 17-18% in 5 years; medical devices revenue share to reach 40% by 2030
items.quote: conservatively, if medical devices keep on growing at between 25% to 26% and other businesses between 15% to 20%. So we still have around 20% and based upon the overall plan and the EBITDA margins, we are looking for a INR5,000 crores top line by 2030

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin 11.55% vs 10.13% FY24 and 6% FY23; trailing 12-month EBITDA INR211 crores with four consecutive quarters at ~INR50 crores; targeting 15% EBITDA in 3 years, 17-18% in 5 years
items.quote: Last year EBITDA was 10.13%. So now this year EBITDA is 11.55% for the first six months. So 11.55% looks very promising as far as our recovery from the previous numbers is concerned. But as I said, miles to go way ahead. So we are targeting 15% EBITDA in the next three years and going up to 17%, 18% in the next five years.

items.statement: Medical devices installed base grew from 10.5 crore to 13 crore meters; strips sold per meter increased from 150 to 165; H1 strips sales up 10% to 22.1 crore; Bluetooth meter and app launching next quarter
items.quote: Now we have installed basis, 13 crores meters. So basically 25 lakh more meters have been added in one year. So this is a growth in the installed base of our customers. So we had 10.57 million, now we have 13 million customer base.

items.statement: Medical devices 30% of H1 revenue (INR271 crores), targeting 40% in 5 years; pharma exports up 21% in H1 (Europe +60%, US +5%); domestic API exposure reduced 9% strategically; new molecules contribution up from 10% to 13.6%
items.quote: Medical devices business is around 30% of the total. And as I was sharing earlier as a part of the strategy that this 30% share of medical devices will go up to 40% in next five years because the rate of growth of medical device business is much higher than the other typical pharma businesses.

items.statement: API capacity expansion from 400 KL to 600 KL (50 KL done this quarter); formulation capacity 1.2 billion dosages (720M tablets, 300M capsules); new medical device facility 120,000 sq ft (5x current) completing this quarter; nebulizer produc
items.quote: In the API, we have to expand our capacity from 400 KL to 600 KL. So out of the 200 KL, 50 KL has already been implemented. So this quarter it should be complete and next quarter onwards, we will see upside in the quantities also.

items.statement: USFDA and Health Canada registration obtained for Class 1 medical devices; team at MEDICA Germany exploring bulk orders and contract manufacturing; glucometer launched in Qatar; 80 new regulated market customers added in H1
items.quote: we have got our product registration done with USFDA and Health Canada and we have got the registration certificate so that we can start export of products in US and Canada. Of course, we had to work on with the customers in getting the orders and everything.

items.statement: Strategically reduced low-yield domestic API sales (India -9%, South America -22%) to protect margins; maintaining price discipline despite China price fluctuations; export focus improving profitability
items.quote: we are trying to reduce our exposure to the non-yielding or low-yielding markets wherein, for example, markets like India, Bangladesh, Pakistan, where we do not get good profit margins. So we are trying to reduce our exposure and focus on the high value drugs

items.statement: FY25 medical devices revenue target INR540-545 crores (H1 at INR271 crores); H2 growth expected better than H1 with API stronger in Q4; margins to be maintained or improved vs H1 11.55% EBITDA
items.quote: Meghna, we had projected around INR540 crores, INR545 crores. So I would say INR540 crores is the number. So we are already at INR271 crores.

items.statement: Medical device subsidiary spin-off planned by Q1 FY26 subject to regulatory approvals; further fundraising likely for INR5,000 crore target; tariff impact on US exports not yet evaluated
items.quote: as far as a medical device business to be put up in a separate subsidiary, so we have already talked about in our annual AGM also and last quarter also. Of course, that is subject to all regulatory approvals and other things. So between this quarter and the next quarter, we will finish the regulatory process.

items.statement: BP monitors now 100% in-house manufactured with SMT lines; backward integration improved margins and removed China dependence; nebulizer license obtained after 3-4 years, expecting INR25-30 crores revenue; ortho supports manufacturing start
items.quote: Now we have the SMT machine installed, everything is in-house, and it has taken some time to establish those lines. And because of the good backward integration, we have been able to get good margins also till the time some components were imported.

items.statement: Jan Aushadhi business at ~30% gross margin, stable volumes growing with finished dosage capacity expansion; government pushing for increased supply; weight loss product launch delayed to New Year with Farah Khan as brand ambassador
items.quote: Of course, the margins are not very great in the Jan Aushadhi business. We just get around 30% gross margin as we talked last time. But what we are seeing is as a good stable business and regular business coming up.

items.statement: H2 FY25 expected better growth than H1; API stronger in Q4, medical devices lower in Q4; margins to be maintained or improved vs H1; trailing 12-month EPS INR2.53
items.quote: That's right. We are looking for better growth in H2. Medical devices at least is low in the Q4, but API is higher in Q4.

items.statement: QIP funds: INR46 crores used for working capital (inventories); INR137 crores balance as of Sept 30, 2024; further disbursements in Oct-Nov; zero-debt company with improving ROCE, ROE, fixed asset turnover
items.quote: On the working capital front, we have spent INR46 crores for the inventories particularly and we still have INR137 crores balance lying for the QIP as in 30th September '24.

items.statement: Birla Opus on track to exit FY25 with high single-digit market share in Indian decorative paints
items.quote: We are on track to exit this year with high single-digit market share in the Indian decorative paints market.

items.statement: Birla Pivot targets $1 billion revenue in 3 years from FY24 and aims to be profitable at that scale
items.quote: Revenue of our B2B e-commerce business, Birla Pivot is gradually ramping up and remains on track to achieve $1 billion revenue in 3 years' timeframe as announced in FY '24.

items.statement: Board approved second and final call of rights issue to raise balance ₹2,000 crore; record date 13 December 2024

Out of this, ₹2,000 crores is already raised, and now the Board has approved for second and final call raising balance ₹2,000 crores. The record date has been fixed on 13th December '24.

items.statement: Chemicals EBITDA up 16% YoY in Q2 FY25 led by chlorine derivatives and speciality chemicals
items.quote: Chemicals business EBITDA for Q2 FY '25 was up 16% Y-o-Y, mainly led by chlorine derivatives and speciality chemicals.

items.statement: Caustic prices improved for fifth consecutive quarter; ECU lower due to chlorine oversupply
items.quote: CFR- Southeast Asia caustic prices marked fifth consecutive quarter of improvement. Domestic prices of caustic also showed improvement during the quarter. However, ECU is lower due to oversupply of chlorine, leading to higher negative realization.

items.statement: Net debt-to-EBITDA guided at 3-3.5x; on track with pending capex and rights issue proceeds in Q4
items.quote: we have guided earlier also that we will be having net debt -to-EBITDA of about 3-3.5x. So, I think we are on track to that. And the pending capex, etc., which is to be done in H2, we have already announced the second and final call of the rights issue, which we will be getting in Q4.

items.statement: Birla Opus portfolio at 83-85% of planned 145 products and 1,200 SKUs by September; remaining entering in Nov-Dec

We have talked about 1,200 SKUs. If you take some of those multiple sizes of enamels and shapes, then the SKUs go a bit more. But I would say that more or less about 83% to 85% of our portfolio is there. Other elements, which need to comp

items.quote: what I can tell you is that our sellout is very high. At any given time, none of our dealers is holding more than a certain couple of weeks or 3 weeks of stock. So, we are very confident that more than 55% - 70% of stock is already sold out.

items.quote: The renewable business capacity has surpassed milestone of 1 gigawatt . items.statement: Epoxy sales dip in Q2 due to monsoon slowdown in construction and windmill installations; no structural slowdown or market share loss
items.quote: generally, monsoon is a slower period for construction and a lot of epoxies go into the construction sector. So that is primarily the driver. items.quote: Additionally, the company continues to see consistent interest for the balance space expected to be vacated by Morgan Stanley

items.quote: EBITDA margins were about 80.55% Profit after tax for the quarter stood at about INR 57 crores, which also grew by 8% year-on-year, while profit after tax margins reported at 34.77%

items.quote: The issue is still playing out in the courts, right. So whereas the initial judgment that we have seen has been largely positive and that has been welcomed by most in the industry, we will just let it play out

items.statement: Average occupancy stable at 99.8% for Q2 FY25; only 7,600 sq ft vacant across NKP and Nirlon House as of Sep 30, 2024
items.quote: the average occupancy rate for the company as a whole, that is NKP and Nirlon House combined, was stable at 99.8% for the 2nd Quarter of the Financial Year 2025

items.statement: Revenue growth of 15-16% YoY expected to be sustained going forward
items.quote: Yes, definitely. We have a plan. Rohit Ohri: Ok. Nitin Tulyani: As I mentioned we are getting export orders and we are also adding new customers as well as new products in our

items.statement: No expansion capex planned; only routine maintenance capex until demand outlook shifts
items.quote: So, given the current environment, we are approaching future capital expenditures very cautiously, so have to revisit our expansion plan once there is a shift in the demand outlook. So, we are not exploring any CapEx other than the routine maintenance CapEx.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement targeted via cost optimization and inventory reduction; no numeric range given
items.quote: Ok. Like I talked about optimization of the cost and second what we are doing is we are focusing on reducing the finished goods stock level. So that it will have a direct impact on our finance cost.

items.statement: Denim (fabric) division profitable in Q2 FY25; expected to remain profitable in Q3 and Q4 FY25 with improving profitability
items.quote: OK, so the fabric division primarily includes our denim business and we have been able to reform this business now and it is expected to deliver profit in Q3 FY25 as well as Q4 FY25. It has given profit in Q2 FY25 also and in Q3 FY25 and Q4 FY25 also the profitability is going to improve.

items.statement: Cotton prices stabilizing; Bangladesh market recovery expected to revive yarn demand
items.quote: See, the price realization is still the challenge we are expecting the Bangladesh market to improve upon and then hopefully there are chances of business being revived.

items.statement: Revenue growth driven by new Kapas unit at Lodha and Chhata (Ginni Filament) acquisition
items.quote: Ok, so when we are talking about the revenue increase, it has primarily increased because of the new unit which went live last year, that is the Kapaa s unit at our Lodha location plus the new acquisition we did at Chhata that has also added the increase in the revenue

items.statement: Off-balance-sheet financing via vendor supply-chain and TReDS platforms approved by RBI to reduce borrowings and working-capital stress
items.quote: Ok, so what we are doing is we are working on the off -balance sheet financing, primarily the vendor supply chain financing as well as the TReDS financing, which has been approved by RBI. So, we are planning to shift some of our vendors to off-balance sheet debt financing so that our borrowings will be shown as reduced and our working capital stress will be reduced a little bit.

items.statement: Yarn spindles (630,000) running at full capacity; no shutdowns
items.quote: So, we are working at full capacity, we have not shut down any spindles. This is what I am saying. We have 6,30,000 spindles for the yarn business and they are running at the full capacity.

items.statement: No headcount reduction planned; AI/Industry 4.0 aimed at augmenting employee bandwidth, not cutting jobs
items.quote: We are focusing on increasing the bandwidth of the employees to handle a particular task by bringing in the technology like I mentioned earlier, one area is cotton forecasting and cotton trading where artificial intelligence is going to be very fruitful be cause it has a direct impact on the cost of raw material procurement

items.statement: Current maturities of long-term debt ~₹157 cr for next 12 months (Oct 2024-Sep 2025)
items.quote: Our current maturities are around ₹157 crores for the next 12 months, from 1 October 2024 t o 30 September 2025

items.statement: AI-driven cotton forecasting tool under evaluation to optimize raw-material procurement cost and improve EBITDA margins
items.quote: Ok. So, on the artificial intelligence, I would like to elaborate, let's say cotton is the primary raw material for the yarn industry and we are implementing a cotton forecasting tool that will help us to be more accurate in terms of, at what level and at what price and what quantity of cotton needs to be purchased so the tool is yet under evaluation phase and we will be sharing an update later on

items.statement: Forex EBIT margin guidance remains steady at about 45% for Q3 FY25
items.quote: our guidance to the EBIT margin on this business remains steady at about 45%.

items.statement: Forex revenue growth expected at 8%-10% and EBIT growth at 12%-15% for Q3 FY25
items.quote: We believe that the business is poised to that 8% - 10% growth in terms of revenue and about 12% to 15% growth in EBIT

items.statement: Sterling expects demand to grow at CAGR of approximately 10% over next few years driven by 20% domestic demand growth
items.quote: We expect the demand to continue to grow at a CAGR of approximately 10% over the next few years and driven primarily by a strong domestic demand growth of 20%

items.statement: Sterling added 5 new resorts in previous 90 days, total now 54 resorts and 3000 rooms; pipeline of 23 resorts to open in next 18 months
items.quote: During this quarter we also took the opportunity to ramp up our inventory supply, and we have added and opened five new resorts in the previous 90 days. This brings a total resort count now t o 54 resorts across 47 destinations in India, and with over 3000 rooms

items.statement: Consolidated operating EBITDA margin increased from 7.04% to 8.05% YoY in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Our operating EBITDA margin increased from 7.04% to 8.05%.

items.statement: Forex EBIT margin expanded from 37% to 48% YoY in Q2 FY25
items.quote: If you look at the EBIT margins, they have expanded from about 37% to 48%

items.statement: Sterling EBITDA margin improved to 32.7% from 31.9% YoY in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Sterling has delivered a respectable EBITDA margin of 32.7% up from 31.9% in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Travel vertical EBIT margin at 4.9% in Q2 FY25, near full-year guidance of close to 5%
items.quote: I am happy to report that in the current quarter our margin stacks at about 4.9%

items.statement: Sustained consumer demand in leisure business across short-haul and domestic markets; forex card billings grew YoY
items.quote: In terms of consumer appetite from the Indian market, we continue to see su stained demand, especially if I look at the leisure business, both in the short-haul as well as in the domestic markets

items.statement: Forex card loads increased 6% QoQ to $250 million in Q2 FY25, inching closer to $1 billion annual run rate
items.quote: If you look at our card loads, they increase by about 6% in the current quarter as compared to the previous quarter. So, we are talking about $250 milli on of loads that we did in the current quarter

items.statement: Short-haul business grew ~30% and domestic business grew ~10% in Q2 FY25; domestic portfolio at FY20 full-year levels in H1 FY25
items.quote: we actually saw the short haul business growing by close to 30% and the domestic business actually growing by about 10% during the current quarter

items.statement: DEI revenue dropped from Rs 235 cr to Rs 209 cr YoY due to US operations closure and Middle East geopolitical tensions impacting Maldives
items.quote: Our revenue has dropped from Rs 235 crores in the previous year's quarter to this year to Rs 209 crores. This drop has been largely due to one of the US operations closure.

items.statement: DMS and inbound India business grew ~25% YoY in Q2 FY25; forward bookings indicate very good season for most DMS entities except South Africa and Allied T-pro
items.quote: the DMS business as well as the inbound in India grew by about 25% during the quarter

items.statement: Group holds over Rs 1800 cr cash on balance sheet, of which ~Rs 1500 cr is forex float; balance is unrestricted
items.value: Rs 1800 cr total, Rs 1500 cr float
items.quote: we have over Rs 1800 crores of cash on our balance sheet on which about close to about Rs 1500 crores is on account of the float. So, the balance can be considered to be unrestricted.

items.statement: Sterling sunset acquisition of new members for 10-year vacation ownership product from September 2024, focusing solely on hospitality business

items.statement: M3 metallized compostable packaging priced 30-40% higher than petroleum-based substrates
items.quote: That's about 30 to 40% higher than the current petroleum-based substrates.

items.statement: M1 metallized compostable packaging priced almost double current substrates
items.quote: M1 is a little bit of a glossy substance with a different structure. That's almost double of the current substrates in terms of pricing.

items.statement: Jagriti project public hearing completed and papers moved to MOEF for final clearance
items.quote: So we have done that open hearing, which is public hearing by the Pollution Board and by the administration, which has been okayed by both of the communities and the papers have been moved to MOEF for the final letter movement.

items.statement: Kawok project equity raise delayed due to investor risk concerns on engineering, offtake contracts, and IP structure
items.quote: The investors have raised some concerns on the risk side of the project. So we are securing that, and it's mainly around more detailed engineering, ordering of equipment, or finalizing of the ac tual costs, and on offtakes

items.statement: UP government capital incentive of about 100 crore over 12 years for Jagriti project
items.quote: capital incentive we are going to get in this Jagriti project. So it's over the period of 12 years, but lump sum, according to the current policy, it is about a 100 crore benefit

items.statement: Kawok project land acquisition of $1.7 million expected to close within 10-14 days
items.quote: The land itself is about $1.7 million. We haven't paid anything yet, but next week is when we expect to pay ideally the entire amount to transfer the land to our name.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY25 recalibrated to INR 5,000 crores +/- 5% from earlier +/- 10%
items.quote: To stay aligned with the market conditions, we have recalibrated our capex estimates by FY'25. We are now estimating to spend INR 5,000 crores +/- 5% versus the earlier guidance of INR 5,000 crores +/- 10%.

items.statement: Automotive order book stands at USD 88 billion lifetime sales to be executed over 5-6 years
items.quote: As of September 2024, we have a large automotive book business of $88 billion providing visibility over the future revenues, which is to be executed over the average of next 5 years to 6 years.

items.statement: Normalised EBITDA INR 2,463 crores and normalised PAT INR 747 crores for Q2 FY25
items.quote: The normalised EBITDA is INR 2,463 crores and the normalised PAT concern share is INR 747 crores.

items.statement: 5 of 19 greenfield facilities operationalised; 8 more expected in H2 FY25
items.quote: As an update on greenfields, we now have 5 out of 19 operationalised and in ramp-up phase. We expect another 8 to come on line in the second-half of this fiscal year.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR 10,500 crores including INR 1,500 crores CCDs; net leverage at 1x
items.quote: We closed the quarter with a net debt of approximately INR10,500 crores versus INR13,500 crores in June 2024. The net debt in the quarter currently includes INR 1,500 crores of CCDs, which were issued in September as a part of the capital raise.

items.statement: Net leverage expected between 0.5x to 0.75x by March 2025
items.quote: So from a leverage of around about 1x right now, we anticipate that by March '25, we should look somewhere between 0.5 to 0.75x depending upon how the production schedules and deleveraging takes place.

items.statement: H2 FY25 expected to be better than H1 due to seasonality and cost recovery from customers
items.quote: We do anticipate that even in H2 at an aggregate level, we should be better than what we did last year-plus better than what we have done in H1 right now.

items.statement: Consumer electronics plant delivered first batch; main plant construction started, full ramp-up in 1.5 years
items.quote: I think we have said that our bigger plant is already starting construction this month and that will take a year and a half for it to be fully up and that's when you will see the full impa ct of the

items.statement: Working capital elevated due to inventory build-up from production uncertainty and supply chain challenges
items.quote: There are multiple reasons why the business took a conservative stance across the globe to load on some amount of inventory in order to prevent any disruption to the customer in this uncertain environment.

items.statement: ROCE improved to 17.3% on LTM basis from 16.9% in FY24
items.quote: I would like to rep ort that the consolidated ROCE based on H1 FY'25 last 12 months basis has improved to 17.3% from 16.9% reported for FY 2024

items.statement: Organic business outpacing industry growth by 4-5% using light vehicles as proxy
items.quote: The organic business continues to outpace the industry growth and deliver consistent increase in content as a result which we have registered a 4% to 5% growth over the market using the light vehicles numbers as a proxy.

items.statement: Targeting 18% to 20% consolidated revenue growth for full year FY25
items.quote: We have been saying that on a full year basis, we are targeting to have something in the range of 18% to 20% growth on a consolidated revenue basis.

items.statement: Targeting 10% to 11% consolidated EBITDA margin for full year FY25
items.quote: Similarly, on an EBITDA level, we are targeting to have between 10% to 11% EBITDA for the full year.

items.statement: Targeting INR130 crores consolidated EBITDA for full year FY25
items.quote: Yes. For the full year basis, we are targeting something in the range of about INR130 crores.

items.statement: Order book increased to INR1,772 crores as of 30th September 2024
items.quote: Next, on the order book front, it has increased to INR1,772 crores as of 30th September 2024, with new contract wins from domestic BTS customers for defense and space.

items.statement: Strong pipeline for domestic defense and space with opportunities in line systems and military radars
items.quote: I'm happy to say that I think we are progressing in those lines in the last quarter, we announced a substantial order for a space program again. And we continue to see a few more significant opportunities coming in for the rest of the year. These are broadly in the domain of line systems and military radars, basically.

items.statement: EMS pipeline strong with export order intake increase due to geopolitical situation and new industrial equipment customers
items.quote: In addition to this, even on the EMS side, our pipeline remains strong. One from the existing customers, again, for defense is quite strong. We've seen the order intake increase from our export customers as a result of the global geopolitical situation today. And apart from that, we've also seen some new customers that we've just added into our portfolio in the last quarter, which will grow substa

items.statement: Capex of INR100 crores over next two years (FY25 and FY26)
items.quote: Capex, as I said, there will be an additional requirement than the normal operating capex that we used to have because of the growth. So for the next couple of years, it will be in the range of about INR100 crores.

items.statement: Fundraise up to INR250 crores via equity for working capital and capex over next 2 years
items.quote: So predominantly, it will be for the increase in working capital, and also the capital expenditure that we need to incur to ensure that growth happens. Since we already have a debt on our balance sheet, we thought it would be better to look at the opportun ity of raising it to equity and that is what we are looking at

items.statement: MOU with Indra Systems delayed awaiting government budget allocations and commercial bid decision
items.quote: We are still waiting on budget allocations from the government, I think the RFP has already been submitted. It's the decision from the government to go ahead with the commercial bid opening, which is being delayed for various reasons on their side.

items.statement: Targeting 14% to 15% consolidated EBITDA margin over next 2-3 years driven by subsidiary improvement
items.quote: And I think the second part in terms of us getting to that 13% to 15% level, a key factor in that will be improving the subsidiaries EBITDA margins up to that level, which will take that 2-year timeframe that we've been mentioning.

items.statement: FY25 revenue mix expected at roughly 25% BTS, 30% engineering services, 45% EMS
items.quote: It will be again, not too far from where we've been at. So roughly about 25% or so would be BTS. And then maybe around 30% or so will be on engineering services and then the rest of it, which is probably about 45% odd will be EMS.

items.statement: Employee cost expected at INR88-90 crores per quarter for H2 FY25
items.quote: It may not go up significantly. It may be in the range of INR88 to INR90 crores per quarter. Because in the subsidiary also, the utilization levels and the revenue will g row. So in absolute terms, it will be about INR90 crores, I would say, for the two quarters

items.statement: No plans to enter OSAT; focus on moving up value chain with system design and development
items.quote: As of now, we have no plans to get into OSAT. I think we want to continue to develop already. We believe we already have a reasonably well diversified portfolio, both in terms of engagement models and in terms of segments that we address. So we're not looking at OSAT again as a new thing now. In fact, I would say our point there is more in terms of moving up the value chain rather than down the va

items.statement: Subsidiary expected to turn profitable in Q3 and Q4 FY25, meaningful profitability in FY26
items.quote: Yes. So we expect to have a positive contribution for the subsidiary in the next two quarters, Q3 and Q4. It's important to remember that even in the subsidiary that it's a bit seasonal in nature. Q2 is always the slowest quarter over there because the number of working days are the least. And Q4 also is the highest in the year also because of the number of working days being high.

items.statement: Standalone tax rate 25%, consolidated tax rate below 25% due to subsidiary losses
items.quote: And on the tax rate, the standalone will stay at that 25 %, and in the subsidiary, we may not have tax at all because we are having a simulated loss which should be offset against the future profits

items.statement: Awarded single largest export order worth $15 million (₹126 crores) from Jessa for rotary dryers at OCP Morocco, to be completed over 12 months
items.quote: Kilburn has recently been awarded an export order by Jessa for supply of rotary dryers to be installed at OCP Morocco, the largest producer of rock phosphate. This is the single largest order ever awarded to Kilburn.

items.statement: Group order book at ₹354 crores as of 30th September; order intake in current quarter till date approximately ₹130 crores including the Morocco order
items.quote: The closing order book on the 30th September for Kilburn and M.E. Energy stood at approximately ₹299 crores and ₹55 crores respectively, which at the group level is around ₹354 crores and a well-diversified one. Furthermore, we have had order intake in the current quarter till date, which is approximately ₹130 crores.

items.statement: Targeting group revenue of ₹500 crores plus for FY25 with EBITDA margin of 20% plus
items.quote: At group level, we still continue to target an aggregate order intake of ₹500 crores plus for the current financial year. With the current pace of execution and the orders in hand we are confident of achieving ₹500 crores revenue for the current year at the group level. On the profitability front, we continue our target of 20% plus and we are sure of achieving it.

items.statement: Targeting group revenue of ₹700-750 crores for FY26 with 20% plus EBITDA margin after consolidation of M.E. Energy and Monga Strayfield
items.quote: If you look at the consolidation of M.E. Energy and Monga Strayfield, both these together will definitely add over ₹200 crores of revenue in FY26 and Kilburn should continue to look at growing at 25%, 30% CAGR. So all that put together I think we are going to target a ₹700 crore kind of number for FY26.

items.statement: Group EBITDA margin target maintained at 20% plus; standalone Q2 margin at 26%, consolidated at 22.28%
items.quote: We will still maintain 20% plus at group level.

items.statement: Ambernath factory acquired for ₹22 crores; M.E. Energy Pune expansion phase one by December end, phase two by March 2025 with total CapEx of ₹10-12 crores; Monga Strayfield CapEx to be evaluated post-acquisition
items.quote: CapEx, we have recently acquired a factory in Ambernath. So that's what we have invested ₹22 crores. We will continue to invest in expansion of M.E. Energy at Pune. Phase one would get completed by December end. And then we look at phase two. The total CapEx should be in the range of ₹10 crores to ₹12 crores.

items.statement: Monga Strayfield acquisition adds radio frequency drying technology for textiles, food, spices, baking, ceramics, foam, latex, fibreglass, packaging, leather, cellulose, wood; 30-40% export revenue
items.quote: So as far as Monga Strayfield is concerned, they have been global leaders in drying and heating solutions using the RF, or the radio frequency technology. Their biggest application is in the textiles, yarn drying and then food and spices and the baking industry.

items.statement: Enquiry pipeline at ₹2,000 crores plus across diverse sectors; strong activity in carbon black (7-8% industry growth), nuclear, chemical, cement, petrochemicals, offshore platforms
items.quote: We are still sitting on a strong enquiry pipeline of ₹2000 crores plus, right. So that has not got diluted so far in last three quarters in spite of us booking orders.

items.statement: Biggest risk identified as geopolitical situation impacting project schedules and commodity prices; mitigated by diversification across 15-20 sectors
items.quote: On the risk part of it, I think the biggest challenge which I see is the geopolitical situation and that can impact the project business. So if the situation worsens in the Middle East and other parts of the world, then there can be some challenges.

items.statement: Fundraise of ~₹280 crores to be completed in current/next week; will recapitalise company and enable Monga Strayfield transaction closure
items.quote: Our fundraise also should be completed in the current week, in the next one week, which will recapitalise the company and also enable us to close the Monga Strayfield transaction.

items.statement: M.E. Energy targeting ₹125-130 crores revenue in FY25 (near double prior year); entering cement waste heat recovery boiler market (₹5,000 crore industry)
items.quote: This year we must be close to ₹125 crores, ₹130 crores of turnover this year. So this is a major jump for M.E. Energy. As far as the new business is concerned, we are working on getting into the cement industry.

items.statement: Ambernath facility handover by end of November; capable of generating ₹100 crores revenue; no further expansion possible at site
items.quote: We have already accounted for that. Ambernath facility by itself is in a position to generate revenue of ₹100 crores. This is what we have mentioned in the previous course as well.

items.statement: Monga Strayfield annual revenue run rate ~₹70-80 crores with over 20% EBITDA margins; four family members to continue in management; deal expected to close in December
items.quote: could be the Monga's annual revenue run rate? Amritanshu Khaitan: Around ₹70 crores, ₹80 crores

items.statement: Tax losses fully utilised; company to pay tax from next quarter onwards
items.quote: All the tax losses have been wiped off. Next quarter onwards we will pay our taxed income.

items.statement: Moroccan order won against Chinese competition; technically qualified as T1 in closely held tender; export strategy combines proactive project tracking and brand-driven inbound inquiries
items.quote: But definitely there was competition from China also. But technically we were qualified as T1. I think that should answer your question how we have placed.

items.statement: M.E. Energy phase two CapEx completion by March 2025 to enable larger project execution; aiming to enter large waste heat recovery boiler market for cement
items.quote: Mr. Kartha is working on the CapEx plan which will allow higher capacity and obviously this will allow us to take larger jobs. As stated in earlier calls, the aim for M.E. Energy is to enter the waste heat recovery boiler market for cement, which is a ₹5,000 crore industry annually.

items.statement: Target double-digit growth, aiming for 20% in coming 1-2 years; higher growth after capex becomes productive
items.quote: We would certainly like to grow in double digits and towards -- more towards 20% game play for sure in coming 1 or 2 years.

items.statement: Capex of INR10 crores spent in H1 FY25; greenfield plant timeline ~1 year; roadmap by January-February
items.quote: We have done a capex of about INR10 crores, including Q1 and Q2.

items.statement: Greenfield plant takes about a year to reach full output; full benefit expected from FY27
items.quote: Yes, about a year's time that from greenfield for a greenfield projects to get into full output status.

items.statement: Institutional business restrained to INR100-150 crores range; Q2 volume down 67% YoY; H2 better than H1 but not targeting last year's levels
items.quote: we'll be very careful. will definitely see second half better than first half, but we are not looking to numbers what we had hit last year in terms of Institutional

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA INR5 crores, down 186 bps YoY; H1 EBITDA INR29 crores, up 138 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA of your company stood about INR5 crores. There is a dip by 186 basis points on Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: PVC prices fell from INR92.50 to INR76.50 (17-18%) in Q2; substantial inventory loss; prices stabilizing at lower end
items.quote: During the last quarter, there were two challenges. One, the prices were continuously falling. As you must be aware, the PVC prices from INR92.50 which we were on 1st July came down to INR76.50 on 30th of September, which is a sharp decline in a short period.

items.statement: Building Products volume grew 25% YoY in Q2; Agri volume grew 18% YoY; Q3/Q4 outlook positive as prices stabilize and supply chain rebuilds stocks
items.quote: Q3 and Q4, we are certainly looking with more -- I mean, surety because, one, prices are now towards the lower end of the curve. And they are stabilizing.

items.statement: Column pipes target premium Agri market; current capacity can reach 600-700 tons/month (INR10-12 crores/month) over time
items.quote: We clearly see going forward, we can definitely build up volumes in excess to 600 to 700 tons a month. So current going basis, it would be more than INR10 crores to INR12 crores a month possibility.

items.statement: QIP raised INR150 crores; 25% (INR37 crores) received, used for working capital and capex; remaining 75% allocation to be finalized by January
items.quote: We have only taken, first 25% of money has come in, which is amounting to about INR37 crores. And most of it is getting utilized either in working capital or capex.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty notification issued; final decision after 30-day comment period; global PVC markets depressed due to wars and economic sluggishness
items.quote: Government has already notified in press, and they have a procedure. They have to go through that procedure before they take a final view and decide and announce.

items.statement: Management confident of achieving ROC target of 18-20% by FY26
items.quote: We are confident that by FY '26, we should be able to achieve the ROC target that we have given earlier.

items.statement: Margins expected to improve year-on-year after Q2 seasonal dip
items.quote: Whatever margins insignificant dip was there, that will be made good going forward and we are very confident that year-on-year basis, we will be giving positive increment on our margins.

items.statement: Three vessel contracts up for repricing in H2 FY25
items.quote: In 2025, we have three vessels where we are expecting repricing. The tenders will come and once the tenders come, we will be able to know once they are allotted.

items.statement: Seamec-3 and Seamec Princess contract renewals with L&T EPC nearing finalization
items.quote: As we talk, the talks are going on. To complete the formalities for that, there has been a significant discussion with the EPC contractor with whom we are going to contract it.

items.statement: Company actively looking to acquire vessels in overseas markets
items.quote: We are looking for those opportunities but along with that, we are also looking for some suitable asset in the form of vessel and all these things.

items.statement: Charter hire rates have increased but vary by contract structure
items.quote: The charter hire rates have increa sed. That is definitely there. But again, each contract is structured in a different way. So some are pure charter hire contracts, some are pure lump sum ® SEAMEC LIMITED A Member of ~~~ contracts and different-different scopes

items.statement: Fuel cost borne by customer in most contracts except lump sum jobs
items.quote: Fuel cost is in most of the cases, it is borne by the customer, except in the cases where we have taken a lump sum job. So, majority of our fleet is on the contract where client is bearing the fuel cost.

items.statement: East Coast opportunities emerging as fields develop
items.quote: East Coast, as we have conveyed even in that earlier call also that there are opportunities which are coming up sinc e the field is developing. So, definitely there will be opportunities coming

items.statement: UK subsidiary liquidation process ongoing, update to come via exchange filings
items.quote: Yes. So, that is an ongoing process. So, that is going on. So, on that also, we will be coming back to the exchanges as and when this is decided.

items.statement: Strong demand for subsea inspection, maintenance and construction services
items.quote: The demand for subsea inspection, maintenance and construction services remains robust and we are well positioned to continue executing on our strategic priorities.

items.statement: Optimistic about H2 FY25 prospects with strong project pipeline
items.quote: Overall, we are pleased with the performance thus far and are optimistic about the prospects for the second half of FY25.

items.statement: Confirmed FY25 sales guidance of over INR500 crores
items.quote: I'm happy to confirm that we will achieve the earnings guidance given at the beginning of the year of over INR500 crores of sales in FY25.

items.statement: Spent INR33 crores of INR48 crores planned capex; expect INR4-5 crores more on committed works
items.quote: Out of INR48 crores of capex plan, which we have shared with you earlier in the year, we have already spent INR33 crores, and the work is progressing as per plan. We expect another INR4 crores to INR5 crores to be spent on ongoing works, which are committed.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia plant capex expected at INR125 crores, operational by H1 FY26
items.quote: We expect the capex in Saudi Arabia to be INR125 crores. This will be done in a phased manner, and we expect that we will be operational by the first half of next year.

items.statement: Varle plant contributed INR16 crores in H1, expected to contribute INR75-100 crores in FY25
items.quote: In H1 FY25, our Varle plant has contributed about INR16 crores in revenue, and it is expected to contribute about INR75 c rores to INR100 crores in this financial year

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin improved 186 bps to 17.29%; Q2 EBITDA margin at 16.3%
items.quote: Despite these challenges, EBITDA grew to INR44 crores, up 77% and EBITDA margin increased by 186 bps to 17.29% compared to 15.43% in H1 FY24.

items.statement: TP Buildtech operating at ~22% EBITDA margin, expected sustainable at least till year-end
items.quote: We are very pleased with the progress of TP Buildtech business that is operating at around 22% EBITDA margin and it is delivering an ROE of over 40%. We fully expect these margins to be sustainable at least till the end of the year.

items.statement: Expect margin revival without EPR in 1-2 quarters as one-time costs normalize and price increase resistance settles
items.quote: We expect a revival of our margins even without EPR over next 1 to 2 quarters, and that's for multiple reasons. One is that there have been some onetime costs which we have incurred in H1 of this year, which has impacted us.

items.statement: H1 tire processing volume up 25% YoY; infrastructure segment volume up 52%, industrial exports up 75%
items.quote: On a half yearly basis, the volume of tires processed in H1 FY25 has increased by 25% year-on-year basis. And on a quarterly basis, the volume has increased by 19% year-on-year.

items.statement: MRP contributes ~10-15% of H1 sales; Gummidipoondi MRP capacity doubled to 10,000 TPA, targeting 75-80% utilization
items.quote: Also to -- just to give you a specific answer to your question, approximately 10% to 15% of our total sale in H1 is of MRP.

items.statement: EPR credits booked on accrual basis (INR11 crores in Q2); no cash realization yet, monetization expected from Q3/Q4
items.quote: In this quarter, we have not sold any. This is all on accrual basis. And our CFO, Mr. Chhabra, would like to add.

items.statement: Planning fundraise of ~INR150 crores primarily for capex and acquisitions, not working capital
items.quote: So we expect the fundraise amount to be largely used for capex and acquisitions essentially, not really for working capital. That's not our purpose.

items.statement: Integrated tire recycling plant of ~24,000 TPA capacity costs INR30-40 crores
items.quote: And a plant like that, which is kind of integrated in nature could cost anywhere between INR30 crores to INR40 crores.

items.statement: Vision 2027 targets: 10 plants, 25%+ revenue CAGR, 18% EBITDA margin, 33% profit growth, 30% ROCE, 250,000+ MT crushing capacity
items.quote: Tinna Rubber is making significant progress towards its vision 2027, which includes expanding recycling plants from the current 6 to 10 locations, achieving a revenue CAGR of 25% plus, EBITDA margin of 18%, profitability growth of 33% and a ROCE of 30%.

items.statement: India recycled rubber penetration at 2-2.5% of tire production; tire companies targeting 10% by 2030
items.quote: of now around 2% to 2.5% of the total tire production i n the recycled rubber material, but each and each and every tire company is now -- have carbon neutralization mission. So wherein by 2030, they want to achieve a level of 10% of the recycled rubber material addition to their systems

items.statement: Current capacity can generate ~INR600 crores revenue; full fungibility across segments from tire crushing
items.quote: we believe that we can get to ab out INR600-odd crores with the capacity that we already have now and the capex, which is under -- which has been undertaken in FY '24. And there is fungibility for sure

items.statement: Consumer segment Q2 degrowth due to heavy monsoon impacting sports surfacing demand; H1 YoY volume up 85%
items.quote: There might be like Q-on-Q basis, if you are looking at the numbers, there might be because of the heavy monsoon and all, most of the consumer segment, what we service is the sports sturfing field so there is a possibility on Q-on-Q basis, but if you see the overall Y-o-Y basis numbers, we have grown.

items.statement: Management confident of achieving 15-20% growth for FY25 despite Q2 headwinds
items.quote: 15 to 20% growth in our conservative target for time to come, however, in Q2, the geopolitical situation, we disrupted the exports and slowing the boosting demand.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA improvement of 5-10% year-on-year if volatility subsides
items.quote: If it subsides, then we expect EBITDA improvement anything between 5 to 10% EBITDA improvement on a Year-to-Year basis.

items.statement: Hydraulic tube plant commissioned with Rs 200 crore investment for 15,000 MT capacity
items.quote: The facility has been installed with the investment of 200 crore in the capacity of 15,000 metric ton.

items.statement: Bullet train order of 22,000 MT, 65% produced, completion in 8-12 months
items.quote: We have got an order of 22,000 metric tons and out of that we have produced almost 65% order and in next 8 to 9 months, maximum to 12 months, it will be completed.

items.statement: Solar support structure has good order books with visibility for at least next one year
items.quote: We have the good order books there and we almost everybody we are supplying, almost everybody we are servicing solar support structure and we see good visibility for at least next one year.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton approximately Rs 8,100 in Q2 FY25, expected to maintain or improve
items.quote: It is almost 8,100 approximate.

items.statement: Management confident EBITDA per ton will not go down and will improve year after year
items.quote: It will be maintained it has to improve year after year. There is no reason. I don't see any reason for it to go down.

items.statement: Hydraulic tube demand excellent, replacing seamless pipes, market needs exceed production capacity
items.quote: This market is excellent. Demand is excellent. Interior replacement of seamless crew.

items.statement: Defense sector demand strong, MIL placed order for 250,000+ requirement for 2027
items.quote: They have placed the order of almost 2,50,000 plus requirement for 2027.

items.statement: Hydraulic tube plant to reach 50,000 MT capacity in 12-18 months, then double capacity
items.quote: We have done a capacity of 50,000 metric ton and we hope to achieve it in 12 to 18 months and as soon as we get 80-90%, then again we will have to do a certain CapEx to double its capacity.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions, Red Sea issues, US elections disrupted exports in H1 FY25
items.quote: However, geopolitical tensions have disrupted our export. US elections have thrown uncertainty in the business.

items.statement: Heavy monsoon, Indian elections, US elections affected domestic demand in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Heavy monsoon all over the country. Elections, Indian elections, US election, we are export thrust company, disruption in export definitely affected the demand.

items.statement: Government capex expected to improve in H2 FY25 as projects announced post-elections
items.quote: Now they have started coming up from the month of October I see there is a demand in the government projects because now March is coming and all the funds have to be spent.

items.statement: No plans to demerge or expand CR coil business, considered low margin but services committed customers
items.quote: We don't plan to do this. It is a business running for last 25 years at the same capacity as which it was installed.

items.statement: Fundraising for defense vertical to be considered after plant stabilization, no amount decided yet
items.quote: So right now, it has not been decided so far because now our total focus is on the reaction of the plant, to start the plant once it gets started, then we will start working on it.

items.statement: Order book as of 30th September is around INR17,260 crores with 64% hydro, 21% irrigation, 10% tunnelling, 5% other sectors
items.quote: Our order book as on 30th September is around INR17,260 crores. Out of that 64% is from hydro sector, 21% from irrigation, 10% from tunnelling and remaining 5% from other sectors.

items.statement: Received letter of award for Jigaon Water Lifting project valued at INR317.6 crores, company share around INR111 crores
items.quote: In Q2, we received the letter of award for the Jigaon Water Lifting project valued at INR317.6 crores for which we earlier declared lowest bidder. Our share in this project is around INR111 crores.

items.statement: Declared L1 for Teesta-V hydropower project in Sikkim with contract value around INR240 crores from NHPC
items.quote: We have also been declared L1 for the Teesta-V hydropower project in Sikkim with a contract value of around INR240 crores from NHPC Limited.

items.statement: Bid pipeline of approximately INR10,000 crores under evaluation and INR40,000 crores identified for bidding soon
items.quote: As regards upcoming projects and bidding pipeline, we have a bid for projects worth approximately INR10,000 crores that are currently under evaluation. Additionally, projects worth around INR40,000 crores have been identified and are expected to be available for bidding soon.
