items.quote: We typically, as far as what is reported on ou r balance sheets, have spent anywhere between 1.2 -1.3 odd percent of turnover in R&D. But that really doesn't capture the full number because most of our R&D projects are end up getting sold.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated revenue target raised to INR13,000 crores with PAT margin 6-7%
items.quote: We're going to achieve the top line around INR13,000 crores on consol. Bottom line, it will be already we have achieved INR232 crores PAT. So it will be more than that, whatever we have targeted, we're going to achieve more.

items.statement: Consolidated order book INR84,400 crores with 55% PMC/EPC and 45% redevelopment
items.quote: Total order book in consolidated level, INR84,400 crores, out of which NBCC around INR70,403 crores, HSCL INR8,093 crores, HSCL INR5,915 crores and NSL INR200 crores. So this is our consolidated order book INR84,400 crores, so out of which P MC/EPC around 55% and 45% in redevelopment

items.statement: Target to reach INR1 lakh crore consolidated order book by FY25 end
items.quote: During this year, we are going to achieve INR l lakh crore order book, that is our target. So that will be easily , I think it is

items.statement: INR15,000 crores contract awards targeted for FY25, INR10,000-15,000 crores for FY26
items.quote: Already awarded around INR3,600 crore. But targets for this year -end, around INR14,000 crores, we're going to award. INR8,600 crores of Amrapali is on sale and another INR2,000 crores, INR3,000 crores work also in pipeline only. S o during this year around INR15,000 crore work we're going to award

items.statement: PAT margin target 6-7% and EBITDA margin 5.5-6% for FY25
items.quote: Currently, our PAT margin is around 6%, 6.6%. So whatever we have committed 6% to 7%, definitely, we're going to reach out that margin. And EBITDA, 5.5% to 6%.

items.statement: Expect at least 20% execution growth in FY26 driven by Amrapali Phase 2 and 7 GPRA projects
items.quote: Yes definitely, at least 20%, we can because Amrapali work Phase 2 will be awarded by next month. So from next year 1st quarter, we're going to get the revenue from Amrapali. And 7 GPRA also, we'll go into start our commercial activities. So definitely.

items.statement: Ghitorni land project GDV INR4,000 crores with phased launch starting FY26
items.quote: It will be built and after built we're going to sell the FAR. So that around INR4,000 crores. This will be INR4,000 crores. And the profit will be more because it is our own land.

items.statement: Supertech project INR10,000-15,000 crores opportunity pending NCLT order
items.quote: Supertech is a stalled project, and it is having 50,000 units. Amrapali, has 38,000 units, whereas Supertech around 50,000 units yet to be handed over by the builder. It is also costing about around INR10,000 crores to INR15,000 crores construction work.

items.statement: INR18,000 crores of NBCC standalone order book currently under execution
items.quote: Currently only INR18,000 crores in execution at the NBCC level. Consolidated level, around INR22,000 crores.

items.statement: Seed money INR400 crores invested in Amrapali with INR190 crores interest receivable from ministry
items.quote: So seed money, we received from MoHUA. We have infused the seed money in Amrapali, around INR400 crores we have invested in Amrapali and interest, INR190 crores we have to receive from ministry.

items.statement: Standalone cash INR723 crores and consolidated cash INR1,600 crores as of 30/09/2024
items.quote: Stand-alone cash flow is INR723 crores as far as NBCC is concerned. And in consol level, it is INR1,600 crores as of 30/09/2024.

items.statement: Border fencing INR440 crores awarded for Indo-Bangladesh with more orders expected
items.quote: Recently, we got around INR440 crores worth from Indo-Bangla border fencing. So future also, there will be a scope for us.

items.statement: Sarojini Nagar commercial property sales INR1,400 crores completed
items.quote: In Sarojini, we have sold downtown. Commercial property we have sold in INR1,400 crores.

items.statement: Disbursement guidance maintained at INR3,600-3,800 crores for FY25
items.quote: We have told between INR3,600 to INR3,800 crores. We still maintain that number as far as disbursement is concerned.

items.statement: AUM guidance may fall short by INR100-200 crores from INR15,000 crores target for FY25
items.quote: Maybe instead of INR15,000 crores, we may be around INR14,800 or something. This is our expectation.

items.statement: GNPA target maintained at INR450 crores for FY25
items.quote: GNPA, we have total INR450 crores as a GNPA number, we'll still maintain that.

items.statement: Outlet guidance of 250 by March 2025 maintained
items.quote: As far as number of outlets are concerned, we have given a guidance of INR250 crores. I think we have already have 227 outlets.

items.statement: INR27 crores spent on new software implementation so far
items.quote: A total of approximately INR27 crores have been spent so far on the new software.

items.statement: NIM at 5.1% in Q2 FY25 with spread maintained at 3.4%
items.quote: Our NIM for Q2 FY '25 was at 5.1% against 5.4% in Q2 FY '24. The company has been able to maintain a spread of 3.4% by raising yields to 12%.

items.statement: MLR increased by 20 bps in current year (10 bps in May, 10 bps this month)
items.quote: In fact, we have increased our MLR by 10 bps from this month. So already one increase we have done in the month of May. So 20 bps, we have already increased in the current year.

items.statement: Second half disbursements expected around INR2,000 crores, historically stronger than first half
items.quote: based on th at and based on the new initiatives that the management has taken, we are quite confident that we will be able to do around INR2000-odd crores of disbursement in the second half

items.statement: Repayment rate increased to ~INR200 crores/month from INR150 crores, driven by balance transfer outs to banks
items.quote: We are now getting a repayment of around INR200 crores approximately per month. I t was around INR150 crores one year back something per month

items.statement: Stage 2 assets at ~10-11% of AUM, focus on reduction with enhanced collection team
items.quote: So Stage 2 is our focus area. Whatever reduction has happened, in fact, personally, we want to do -- the team wants to do still better. So we a re focused. And the 10%, we are confident that we will be able to achieve this 10% of AUM

items.statement: NHB loan proposal in pipeline, NCD approvals in place, no fixed securitization plans
items.quote: Maybe as of now, liability, we are also approaching NHB. So the NHB proposal is in the pipeline. So maybe we may get some NHB loans during this current year. We are also – we are tapping the market as to our NCD routes and all. We have got approvals from AGM as well as our

items.statement: Non-housing (home equity) at 26% of loan book, housing at 74%
items.quote: The share of non-housing loan that is home equity stood at about 26% of the loan book and housing loans contributed about 74% of the book.

items.statement: Credit cost expected to be marginal/negligible with estimated INR50 crores write-back for FY25
items.quote: Credit cost will be marginal or almost nil. It will be very much negligible because of the recoveries we are making. In fact, write-backs will be more this time because we have already estimated a write-back of INR50 crores for the current year.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 slippages INR37 crores, recoveries INR67 crores
items.quote: For the current quarter, I can tell INR37 crores was the slippage, INR67crores was the recovery.

items.statement: Incremental lending rates: home loan 11.2%, home equity 13.8%, average 11.8% in September
items.quote: Home loan is 11.2% in September, home equity 13.8%. Average is 11.8%.

items.statement: DSA/Connector share in disbursements increased to ~40% from ~30% last year
items.quote: month, it was 40%. But overall, I think it's -- but we may end up around 40% by year-end... Rajiv Mehta: For the whole year. K. Swaminathan: Yes. For the current year, we may have because that percentage is going up because Connectors we have added in the current

items.statement: Won U.S. export order for commercial vehicle emission components with $7M annual and $40M+ lifetime revenue, SOP January 2026
items.quote: I'm also very happy to announce that we have won an export order for emission components to the U.S. market with annual business of approximately $7 million and lifetime business of $40 million plus. The SOP for the order is expected by January 2026.

items.statement: Will continue to outperform industry; gross profit is the right barometer rather than sales due to catalyst accounting
items.quote: So we have just guided that we will continue to outperform the industry and gross profit is the right barometer rather than sales in our case, the way catalyst accounting is done.

items.statement: EBITDA margins benefit from catalyst accounting removal and FOC model mix; hard to guide specific number
items.quote: So definitely, that is -- and in fact also when you see in terms of the improving EBITDA margins, the way they're calculated, so it's hard to guide on a number.

items.statement: INR 50 crore capex for new suspension plant with SOP mid-December to early January, 280,000 controls capacity
items.quote: We have indicated a capex of INR50 crores. Some is already done and some will be done over this quarter. We have a capacity of 280,000 controls on site.

items.statement: New suspension plant for control arms on platform usable for EV and ICE; new customer business small initially but hopeful for larger wallet share
items.quote: The current volumes that we have, there will be a gradual ramp-up. Hence, at least for Q4 of this year, there will only be marginal revenues for this plant.

items.statement: Construction equipment emission norms from Jan 2025; won temperature control tube business, mature volumes from June 2025, not significant initially
items.quote: We have received good business and we expect some revenues to be coming, starting next year and we expect maybe mature volumes to start more towards June '25 onwards.

items.statement: TREM 5 timeline intact on development readiness; any delay would be government-driven, no communication of delay so far
items.quote: So it is hard to predict in terms of any government delay. However, in terms of development and in terms of readiness, it's fully there and if there is any delay, it should be in due to government, delays in norms.

items.statement: JV with Purem awarded localization program for international customer, expected to kick in mid-2026, will boost JV above breakeven
items.quote: And once that's added, that's going to give some boost to the JV and we're expecting somewhere around the middle of 2026 for that to kick in, but that's a good program that the JV has won.

items.statement: CV 3-4 liter segment: competitor has 90% share, Sharda has product ready but no platform awarded yet, targeting niche profitable segment
items.quote: As of now, we've not been awarded any platform in that segment. That's one of our target segments where we have ready with the product and we are in the business development cycle for that.

items.statement: Export margins generally better but working capital higher; net ROCE similar to domestic business
items.quote: However, what we've guided in general about exports, that generally margins are better in exports, however working capital is also more in exports. So on a net ROCbasis, it generally works out to be the same as our domestic business

items.statement: Core emission capacity augmentation incremental only; similar capex trajectory as last 2 years; light-weighting vertical will require additional capital
items.quote: It will all be incremental capex only. It is not going to be some substantial capex, right? And we would continue on a very similar capex trajectory that we've had last 2 years.

items.statement: Substantially increasing shareholder payback via buyback and established dividend policy; will become more efficient in surplus cash usage
items.quote: At the same time, we are also substantially increasing our payback to shareholders. So I think the buyback was the first part of the journey. At the same time, we also now have a dividend policy that is established and we will continue to do that.

items.statement: Filed ~10 IPs in last couple years focused on emission competitive advantage and exportable adjacencies; too early for licensing or business results
items.quote: Regarding the IPs, we have focused on 2 areas. One is which strengthens our competitive advantage within emissions and especially, there are a few technologies that we anticipate in the next emission norms.

items.statement: Export focus on 4 core areas: CV emission components, temperature control tubes, stationary engine gensets, sub-100HP tractors; light-weighting exports later
items.quote: So these are 4 core areas where we want to focus our export business. However, in the future, definitely, these products are also exportable.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin 14.4% (+258 bps YoY); Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 14.8% (+178 bps YoY)
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for the half year grew by 258 basis points from 11.8% in H1 FY '24 to 14.4% in H1 FY '25.

items.statement: AUM guidance of INR 1,300 crores for FY26 maintained; may reach INR 1,250-1,275 crores depending on environment
items.quote: So to all the banks in this year starting from day one we gave guidance to them in terms of AUM of INR1,300 crores. So it depends also on how the environment if the environment gets better and better we can still reach that number of 1250, 1275 kind of number.

items.statement: Target minimum doubling of net worth and tripling of AUM over 18 months from last equity raise
items.quote: So what, from an investor perspective, we are saying a minimum doubling of net worth and tripling of AUM over an 18-month period from the last equity raise.

items.statement: Secured loan book increased to 32% of AUM; target over 40% by end of 2025; incremental secured disbursements at 47%
items.quote: The secured loan represented only 12% of our AUM, while this has now increased to 32% as of September 24. By the end of 2025, we maintain our outlook that we will have over 40% of our loan book in the secured segment.

items.statement: Branch network expanded to 141 branches (up 36% QoQ); 37 branches added last quarter including 28 in September alone
items.quote: Our branch network continues to expand, now totalling 141 branches up from 104 last quarter. We are now active in 12 states with new branches recently opened in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana which has strengthened our diversification.

items.statement: Yield stable at 29%, spread stable at 15.5%, NIM stable at 16.5%; opex at 13% of AUM vs 12.7% in FY24
items.quote: Evidently, the yield and spread continue to remain stable at 29% and 15.5% respectively for the quarter, which you have noticed in our investor presentation as well. So despite low yield on secured book our spreads remain stable and NIM has remained stable as well.

items.statement: Collection efficiency dipped to 93.2% in Q2 (vs 97.6% YoY); 30+ DPD at 5.45%; credit cost at 3.85% (highest since inception); gross NPA 2.78%, net NPA 1.41%
items.quote: For September quarter, the collection efficiency was at 93.2% comparing with 97.6% in second quarter last year and 30 plus DPD stood at 5.45%. We have mentioned in our presentation that collection efficiency in secured loans is significantly higher at around 97%. While the credit cost stood at3.85% for the quarter, which is – we agree that it has been highest since inception.

items.statement: Internal target: 30+ PAR should not exceed 3%; expect improvement in current quarter and further next quarter
items.quote: Exactly at this point of time if you ask me in terms of guidelines, I feel anything more than 3% PAR in a 30% is not acceptable to us. That is what we will say should be the highest number. Having said that, it is high, looking high in this quarter which we really feel will settle down. We will see some improvement in this quarter and definitely next quarter again should see the improvement.

items.statement: Equity raise of INR 176 crores completed (INR 63 cr equity + INR 113 cr warrants); INR 91 cr received in Q2, balance INR 85 cr receivable by March 2026
items.quote: We also reached equity of INR176 crores which is more than double our net worth in Q1, out of which INR63 crores equity and 113 was warrants and INR91 crores is already received in second quarter and balance INR85 crores is receivable before March 26.

items.statement: Secured loan pricing 100-150 bps below peers in up to INR 5 lakh ticket; incremental borrowing cost at 11-12% (HDFC at 11%); average borrowing cost 13.5%
items.quote: So while the incremental has been 12% the last loan we got from HDFC bank was at 11% in this kind of market. What I believe is there is absolutely no reason that in coming years we will have borrowing cost which is more than our peers.

items.statement: Dedicated collection team built from zero (Aug 31) to 40 people (Sep 30); three large collection agencies engaged; cash collections down from 40% to 20%
items.quote: 31st of August we just had zero collection, dedicated collection team because in all our presentations, we have said that it is a sale and collect model. End of September, we had 40 people internal. And we have also started with agencies and we can already see the change which is coming

items.statement: ROE target of 12% for FY25 uncertain; aim to at least maintain last year's ROE; first target 15% ROE as soon as possible
items.quote: For this year I would not say I am not sure for this year we will be able to do 12% let's see how times shape up. We at least we should maintain what we did last year maybe improve upon it let's see so time will tell.

items.statement: Provision policy: 50% at 90 days, 100% write-off at 360 days; only 9 legal cases filed in 5.5 years; new strategy to pursue maximum recovery
items.quote: I think we are never less on provisions. See we have a policy that for all 90 day cases we make a 50% provision so this is without any exception and in a 360 day 1 year period we take a complete write off. There are many players who keep the book for 3 years before writing it off.

items.statement: Targeting 12% EBITDA margin with consistent delivery; confident of double-digit sales growth
items.quote: So yes, we are going to achieve towards 12%, but most important for us is consistency and which is what we are delivering. So in the process of building our core, I am very confident that achieving the double-digit sales growth number is just for us a very easy.

items.statement: Capex of INR 300-350 crores per annum for next 2-3 years, funded through internal accruals
items.quote: we feel that we should be doing capex of about INR 300 crores INR 350 crores per annum. And given our internal accrual and cash flow generation, largely this should be funded through internal accruals only.

items.statement: H1 FY25 lifetime order book INR 4,750 crores; EV platforms 25% of Q2 wins; annual peak revenue ~INR 1,100 crores from 18-24 months
items.quote: In the first six months of FY25, the company's order book exceeded INR 4,750 crores, reflecting our expanding product portfolio, product premiumization and rising demand for ICE and EV products across segments and geographies.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 11.4%, up 38 bps YoY; fifth straight quarter above 11%; targeting 12%
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 11.4%, increased by 38 basis points. Total lifetime order book won was INR 2,400 crores with EV constituting to about 25% of the total order book.

items.statement: EV products ~10% of revenue; wiring harness 32%, lockset 23%, die casting 18%, instrument cluster 17%; 2W/3W 46-47%, CV 26%, PV 15%, aftermarket 11-12%
items.quote: wiring harness continues to be about 30% to 35% and this quarter is 32%. Lockset and vehicle access is about 23%, die casting division, which is DCD stands for about 18% as this segment is growing as well as our instrument cluster business is also continuing to grow, which is now contributing to about 17% and other new products, which is the EV products and other products such as the sensors are a

items.statement: 2-wheeler demand strong with premiumization; PV slightly declined but UV robust; CV challenged by high base and monsoon; tractor recovery expected
items.quote: In Q2 FY25, industry growth has been moderate with the 2-wheeler segment leading in demand. The passenger vehicle segment experienced a slight decline, reflecting softer market demand. While the utility vehicle category showed robust performance, underscoring strong consumer interest in the SUVs and multifunctional vehicles. The commercial vehicle segment faced challenges due to a high base effect

items.statement: Sanco TLA addresses high-voltage connectors, charging guns, bus bars, cell contact systems, PDU, BDU; localization roadmap aligned with customers; target >10% export revenue share mid-term
items.quote: This partnership will deliver comprehensive and customized electrical distribution systems for the electric vehicle market and there will be various new products, w hich will bring into the portfolio of Minda Corporation such as the connectors, charging gun assemblies, sockets, bus bars, cell contact systems for batteries, power distribution systems and Battery Distribution Unit

items.statement: Export demand subdued in Europe; US election uncertainty; CV recovery dependent on government infra spend; some EV OEM orders not yet in production
items.quote: Of course, the order intake continues. However, we do not see a hig her uptake in the next six months when it comes to the exports, primarily in Europe region, various macroeconomic factors. And now with the new elections in the US, we have to really see on how this market pans

items.statement: Four new facilities: two diecasting, one instrument cluster, one wiring harness component; 24-acre land acquired in UP for future expansion
items.quote: To meet this growing demand, the company is coming up with four new facilities, two in diecasting, one in the instrument cluster division and one in the wiring harness component division. In line with our strategic vision, Minda Corporation has also acquired a 24 -acre land in Uttar Pradesh for future expansion.

items.statement: Export revenue target 10-15% of total (from ~7% currently) in mid to long term; order book already in place
items.quote: in the midterm to long term from current about 7% in our growth on the exports, we expect it to be,and our target rather is to be about 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Sanco TLA potential >INR 1,000 crores immediate TAM for phase 1 products; RFQs received, nearing nomination
items.quote: this can increase our business potential to more than INR 1,000 crores in the current products that are offered in the first phase.

items.statement: ROCE floor 20% for any inorganic acquisition; capital allocation policy board-approved
items.quote: Absolutely. Parag ji, we have very strong financial footings metrics internally approved by Board of Directors on capital allocation, and any kind of inorganic or capital allocation cannot dilute our ROCE. So ROCE above 20% is our prime capital allocation financial prudence.

items.statement: Sunroof/closure JV with HCMF: plant commissioning Q1 FY26 (possible 1-2 month delay); advanced discussions with OEMs for SOP in 2 years
items.quote: So yes, we are in line with the Q1. Of course, there could be maybe a month or two delay, but yes, we are in line in order to move forward and set up the facility.

items.statement: Order book mix: 2W/3W ~40%, 4W ~20%, rest CV and offroad; 60% new business, 40% replacement
items.quote: So it is in line with our current revenues. So again, 2-wheelers and 3-wheeler continues to be, I think, about 40% of the total order book, and 4 -wheelers is over about 20%, and the rest is the commercial vehicles and offroad.

items.statement: Smart key penetration on track; SOP started for Japanese OEMs in Q2; new segments launching soon
items.quote: Smart key orders continue to get deeper penetration. And depending on the SOPs of the customers that are there. Of course, in Q1 we had sales to the 2-wheeler OEMs, but in Q2, our sales to Japanese OEMs have also started.

items.statement: Net debt INR 160 crores, net debt/net worth 0.08x; ROCE 21%, targeting 25%; long-term borrowing reduced to INR 170 crores
items.quote: Our gross debt has come down by about INR 14 crores, making our total net debt to INR 160 crores and net-debt to net-worth is about 0.08x. Capital employed at INR 1,873 crores and our ROCE is about 21% with our focus to increase this to about 25%.

items.statement: Implemented freight rate hikes across all sectors and geographies; realization per ton increased ~8% YoY to INR7,241
items.quote: As communicated during the last call about the increase in freight rates, we have successfully implemented the freight rate hikes across all the sectors and geography.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 17% from 14% YoY, driven by rate hikes, fuel cost control, and lower hired vehicle dependency
items.quote: The EBITDA has increased by 39% from INR98 crores to INR135 crores, and percentage to revenues increased from 14% to 17%.

items.statement: Expect 4-5% tonnage growth in H2 FY25 at current realizations; better tonnage growth in FY26; EBITDA margin of 16%+ sustainable
items.quote: Going forward, also in next half year, we're expecting at least around 4% to 5% growth in the tonnage with the current realizations what we are having.

items.statement: H2 FY25 capex ~INR350 cr including INR240-250 cr for Bangalore facility, INR20-22 cr for Mysore, INR30-40 cr/quarter for vehicles, plus INR44 cr dividend
items.quote: With that, the total investment in next half year, if these projects are going to be invested, then total investment will be around INR350 crores.

items.statement: Industry demand muted; VRL grew volumes 4% YoY via 82 new branches added YoY (2.5% contribution) and existing customer share gains
items.quote: Even though we saw muted growth in quarter 2 by most of the companies across the sectors, we are still in a position to show growth in volumes.

items.statement: LTL ~90%, FTL ~10%; textiles 16-18%, agri commodities 9-10%, others 5-6% each; door-to-door 35-38% of business
items.quote: Yes, LTL is around 90%. FTL is around 10%.

items.statement: Cautious on fleet addition; will add own vehicles only if sustained demand, else use hired vehicles; branch expansion focused on East/North/Northeast
items.quote: No, basically, it will be a cautious decision. See always what we do, we add the vehicle only if the vehicles are required for our operations.

items.statement: Fuel procurement from refineries at 35% of consumption (optimum); saving INR2-2.5/litre vs retail; bulk purchase increased from 30% to 35%
items.quote: The refinery is now we can say it is at the optimum level. There are 1% or 2% changes will be there.

items.statement: FY26 capex predominantly for vehicles; capacity addition ~3-4% per year matching 4-5% tonnage growth
items.quote: In 2016, again, predominantly, the capex will be towards vehicle itself. Based on the quantity improvements, we will decide on the investment into the vehicles.

items.statement: Fixed costs ~30-35% of revenue (employee, rent, insurance, taxes); grow ~8% annually; operating leverage to improve margins with volume growth
items.quote: See, almost around 30%, 35% of our costs are fixed in nature, especially the employee cost is fixed in nature.

items.statement: Added 12 branches in Q2; plan 80-100 branches/year for next 5 months adding 40-45; 250+ branches added in last 2 years contributing 8-10% of tonnage
items.quote: On a full year basis, we are planning to add at least around 80 to 100 branches even going forward.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR259 cr; H2 FY25 net debt increase ~INR100-120 cr after INR350 cr capex+dividend vs INR240-250 cr operating cash flow
items.quote: So the net debt addition will be around INR100 crores by end of 31st March.

items.statement: Interim dividend INR5/share approved; receivable days ~12; 85% LTL on paid/to-pay basis; 9 lakh customer base
items.quote: Considering the improvement in turnaround time of the vehicles and control on usage of hired vehicles, we moved slower on the vehicle capex during the quarter and invested around INR18 crores in the current quarter.

items.statement: Order book stands at about 2 GW valued at INR3,350 crores, to be executed over the next 12-18 months.
items.quote: Our order book stands at about 2 gigawatt inching us closer to our ambitious target of 10 gigawatt on the group level.

items.statement: Bid pipeline of 1.57 GW expected to materialize in 3-6 months.
items.quote: So we have about 1.57 gigawatts of orders already in bid. And we expect them to materialize in about coming 3 months to 6 months.

items.statement: 30 MW IPP plant capex is INR240 crores, partially funded through equity and debt; work already started for commissioning by end of January 2025.
items.quote: Coming to your first question on what is the capex cost of the entire 30 megawatt plant it is INR240 crores.

items.statement: Expect better performance in H2 FY25 and maintain same growth perspective.
items.quote: I would feel you should expect better coming up and we will maintain the same growth perspective as well further.

items.statement: EPC EBITDA margin at 20-23%; blended EBITDA depends on mix of EPC, IPP and O&M.
items.quote: So right now at the current level, if you see, about 20% to 23% of margin is being there on the EPC contract at the EBITDA level and balance is being contributed by the IPP and the O&M factors.

items.statement: KPI Green hybrid order (ex-turbine) EBITDA margin expected at 22-23%.
items.quote: Other than the turbine, it would come to about 22% to 23% as has been maintained in the earlier orders.

items.statement: IPP average gross selling price INR7.5-8/unit; net price INR6-6.5/unit for private PPAs; GUVNL PPA at INR2.43/unit with lower transmission costs/losses.
items.quote: So the price which we have agreed with GUVNL as per PPA is INR2.43 per unit.

items.statement: IPP portfolio at 20 MW, plus 30 MW under commissioning expected by January 2025, targeting 50 MW by FY25 and 100 MW by FY26.
items.quote: Our IPP, which is the independent power producer portfolio stands at about 20 megawatt with another 30 megawatt under commissioning and which is expected to be energised in the financial year 25.

items.statement: 100 MW IPP expected to generate ~INR100 crores revenue with 75-80% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: So, again, as I told before it depends upon the mix, but roughly you can expect about INR100 crores of top line at 100 megawatt.

items.statement: No visible listed competitor offering full-scope wind/solar hybrid BOP; confident margins will be maintained.

items.quote: As far as our opalware capacity is concerned, I would say that we have at least 2 years to go before we fully utilize the capacity. We have some debottlenecking waiting this year.

items.quote: As far as gross margins are concerned, it's a product mix issue. It's not -- I mean lunch boxes is definitely compared to selling a mixing bowl, a lunch box has definitely got a lower gross margin.

items.statement: Strong H1 FY25 revenue growth of 19.4% YoY to INR490.7 crores; confident in medium-term outlook despite cautious consumer sentiment
items.quote: I'm happy to share that Borosil Limited had a strong performance in H1 FY '25 with revenue from operations reaching INR490.7 crores compared to INR410.9 crores in the same period last year. This impressive year-over-year growth of 19.4% places us among the top performers in the

items.statement: BIS implementation transition expected to be seamless with adequate imported inventory and domestic sourcing; no plans for Gujarat capex currently
items.quote: I believe that we have imported enough inventories and we have domestic sourcing also, which will help us let's say, transition away from imports to domestic sourcing in adequate time, and therefore, it should be relatively seamless, this whole transition.

items.statement: Raised INR150 crores via QIP in Q1 FY25; utilized INR105 crores for working capital loan repayment, INR39 crores for long-term project loan repayment; net debt INR88.6 crores
items.quote: During the quarter ended June 30, 2024, the company successfully raised INR 150 crores through a QIP to facilitate the repayments /prepayment of long -term project loans, working capital loans and for general corporate purposes.

items.statement: ICRA upgraded long-term rating to AA- stable, short-term reaffirmed at A1+; reflects healthy credit profile improvement
items.quote: We are pleased to update you that the external rating agency, ICRA, has upgraded Borosil Limited's long-term rating to AA - stable, while the short -term rating has been reaffirmed to A1+.

items.statement: Pressware capacity utilization close to 65%; target to reach 100% in 2 years (this year plus next year) vs original 3-year plan
items.quote: We would be close to 65%.

items.statement: Opalware capacity utilization 100% in Q2 FY25, ~85% in H1 FY25; able to meet all orders

items.statement: No extra discounts observed from e-commerce platforms during big billion day sales; channel strategy differentiated by product categories to reduce friction
items.quote: No. In our category, there was no -- I mean nothing majorly noticeable.

items.statement: A&SP expenses higher by INR12-13 crores in H1 FY25 and INR7.4 crores in Q2 FY25 due to Diwali preponement; annual A&SP expected consistent with previous year
items.quote: The higher A&SP expenses is attributed to the preponement of the Diwali festival this year compared to last year, with the benefits expected to reflect in the subsequent quarter. However, the annual A&SP expenditure is expected to remain consistent with the previous year.

items.statement: Other income includes INR8.42 crores shared service support income in H1 FY25 (~INR4.5 crores in Q2); associated expenses captured under total expenses
items.quote: Notably, other income includes INR 8.42 crores from shared service support income with associated expenses captured under total expenses.

items.statement: No price cuts taken; selling more lunch boxes priced lower than mixing bowls causing product mix impact on gross margin
items.quote: There's been no price cuts.

items.statement: Presales guidance of 5,000 crores for FY25
items.quote: The first half of the fiscal has been very exciting for TARC with our presales number totaling to 1,322 crores, a 6x growth in the first half of fiscal over previous year which gives us enough arsenal to reach our guidance of 5,000 crores for the fiscal.

items.statement: Full-year collection guidance of close to 700 crores additional for FY25
items.quote: As far as our collection is concerned for the whole year, we should be getting close to 700 crores additional apart from whatever we have done in this financial year.

items.statement: Construction spend of roughly 2,000 crores for three launched projects
items.quote: We will be spending roughly 2,000 crores on construction now for the three projects put together.

items.quote: We have done roughly 3,000 crores of sales till now, between the three projects.

items.quote: 4,500 crores is the balance . The total is 7,500 crores from these 3 projects roughly . So, 3,000 offered and 4,500 is to be sold.

items.quote: You know, we are doing good 60%, 65% EBITDA margins. Amar Sarin: Yes

items.quote: I think 10 % to 15% year -on-year growth in terms of price is something which a good development and a good product will keep seeing over the next three to four years.

items.statement: Focus on luxury residential only, no mid-market entry for next 18-24 months
items.quote: We don't see ourselves going in any other real estate vertical or even mid -income or premium, at least for the next 18 months to 24 months. The idea is to stay here.

items.statement: Target to become debt-free within next two years from project cash flows and monetization

items.statement: Total debt currently around 1,650 crores plus redemption premium

items.statement: Expect Tripundra OC within 4-6 months, targeting March for part OC to start revenue recognition

We will try and do it by March. Maybe one phase, if not the whole project , and get a part OC and start booking the revenue at least for Tripundra.

items.statement: Plan to launch new project in next 3-4 months if needed to meet 5,000 crore presales guidance
items.quote: We have given a number of 5,000 crores. We are very confident of achieving it from our existing projects. And if need be, we will launch another project so to say in the next three to four months.

items.statement: Expect compensation receipts of ~300 crores within next one year, to be used for debt repayment
items.quote: The compensation that has to be received by the company is in various stages of, I would say , acquisition that has been done of the properties of the company. And we are expecting these compositions to come within the next one year, I would say , from now. This money is predominantly going to be used for paying off our debt.

items.statement: Second half FY25 top line growth of 15% to 16% and 14% to 18% growth in second half itself
items.quote: For the second half of the year, we are looking at, at least 15% to 16% top line growth, which includes ramp-up of operation at the bio mining of the C&T project, ramp up of operations at our waste to energy entity, which will see an improved PLF post the maintenance shutdown, and the sale from my construction and demolition waste. items.quote: We exited the June quarter with an order book of around Rs.8,300 crores to be spread over the next 12 to 14 years. So that kind of has a fixed revenue visibility for us without the escalation kicking in.

items.quote: The core EBITDA during the quarter was around Rs.48.9 crores, and the core EBITDA margin is around 20.1%.

items.quote: So we should be in low to mid-teens going forward because our denominator is going to be much higher than what it was historically. So anywhere between 11% to 14% over the next project rollouts should be our comfort zone, I would say.

items.statement: EBITDA margin was 28% and PAT margin was 17.9% in Q2 FY2025.
items.quote: EBITDA for Q2 stood at INR 42 crores with a healthy EBITDA margin of 28% and PAT stood at INR 26 crores with a PAT margin of 17.9%.

items.statement: Second half of the year historically performs much better than the first half for a travel company.
items.quote: So historically, half -- second half of the year is always performing much better than the first half of a travel company. Yes, I will agree on that.

items.statement: Hotel and Holiday Packages segment grew 178% year-on-year with gross booking revenue of INR 241 crores.
items.quote: Our strategy to expand beyond air services continues to yield strong results, particularly in Hotel and Holiday Packages segment, which achieved an impressive 178% year-on-year growth with gross booking revenue reaching INR 241 crores.

items.quote: However, that number, I believe, for this particular quarter is 9.5%. And earlier that number was somewhere around with similar around 9.8% for the last year. So it hasn't really changed so much.

items.statement: Signed exclusive agreement with PhonePe to power Hotel segment for 560 million users.
items.quote: has also forged an impactful partnership, including an exclusive agreement with PhonePe to power Hotel segment on their platform, enhancing convenience for 560 million users of PhonePe to offering them seamless access of millions of domestic and international hotels

items.statement: Dubai operations breaking even and making money; international margins expected to exceed India margins due to cost arbitrage.
items.quote: In fact, even the services, the operations, everything is run by Indian team, which is why it is able to create a very good alpha as the entire technology, entire operations runs out of India, while we are competing and earning in dirhams and dollars.

items.quote: Hotel business does not require as much capex. The hotel in Ayodhya, which we have announced about a year ago does not also require capex because it's an equity deal. There is another partner who is basically putting in the capital. We have basically offered them the equity in return.

items.statement: YoloBus subsidiary breaking even; EV bus manufacturing to serve YoloBus and external orders from government and private companies.
items.quote: Yolo in the last few months has started breaking even. Our Dubai business has started breaking even and started actually even making some money.

items.statement: Target 80 Kalyan and 50 Candere showrooms in FY25; 49 Kalyan and 34 Candere opened so far

items.statement: Expect INR 50 crore additional customs duty loss in Q3 FY25, total INR 120+ crore for FY25
items.quote: INR 120-odd crores, out of which INR 70 crores has come. So, we will have to expect INR 50-odd crores more in Q3.

items.statement: Debt reduction target INR 300 crore for FY25, INR 350-400 crore for FY26
items.quote: So, debt reduction this year, our plan was INR 300 crores. Next year should be in the range of what? INR 350 crores to INR 400 crores.

items.quote: In this quarter just ended, we opened 26 stores net, 14 in the Kalyan Jewellers brand and 12 in Candere.

items.quote: If you look at gross margins will be only 8% for franchisee stores. Owned store will be always in between 15.5%, 16%.

items.statement: PBT growth marginally higher than revenue growth after adjusting for INR 70 crore customs duty write-off
items.quote: If you are adjusting the INR 70 crores write-off, PBT growth is actually marginally higher than our revenue growth, even this year.

items.statement: Gold price up 10-11% YoY; SSG 23% implies volume growth plus studded mix shift
items.quote: About 10% to 11% is where the gold price have gone up, but the revenue has gone up by what SSG said, was 23%.

items.statement: SSG excess of 20% for Diwali minus 30 days period; momentum strong into wedding season
items.quote: We have witnessed SSG in the excess of 20% for Diwali minus 30 days period when compared to the base year.

items.quote: Studded share was higher, and we saw a marginal improvement in gross margin at the showroom level, but not major improvement in the showroom level gross margin.

items.quote: There is one thing, which has come this quarter is the onetime write-off of around INR 70 crores for customs duty.

items.quote: There has been a de lay in the launch of the first showroom in the U.S., and we expect to open the showroom by the end of the current quarter

items.statement: International TAM estimated at 25-30 showrooms across US, UK, Canada, Australia, Singapore; Middle East has more potential
items.quote: U.S., U.K., Canada, Australi a, Singapore, everything put together can be maybe what, 25, 30 showrooms

items.statement: Candere at 46 showrooms, targeting 50 in FY25; campaigns delayed post-Diwali, focus on footprint first
items.quote: This year itself, we opened 34. Our plan for this financial year was to open 50 out of which 46 is already done.

items.statement: Non-GML working capital loan reduced by INR 143 crore in India YTD; GML stable, focus on non-GML repayment
items.quote: Non-GML working capital loan in India has been reduced by around INR 143 crores.

items.statement: Target to add 100 new restaurants to reach 325 by FY27
items.quote: For the medium term, we will target to add 100 new restaurants to reach 325 restaurants by FY27.

items.statement: 100 stores expansion requires approximately Rs.300 crores over next 2.5-3 years
items.quote: From now on, 100 stores would require approximately Rs.300 crores. And in the next 2.5 to 3 years, just based on the last year's operating cash that we generated, it is enough to deliver that.

items.statement: On track to add 25 new restaurants in FY25 with 8 added in H1 and 3 in October
items.quote: We added 8 new restaurants in H1 and are on track to add 25 new restaurants for FY25.

items.statement: Pre-IND AS operating EBITDA grew 23.1% to Rs.16.6 crores with margin at 5.4%, up 96 bps YoY
items.quote: Pre-IND AS operating EBITDA grew by 23.1% to Rs.16.6 crores. Adjusted operating EBITDA margin for the quarter was 5.4%, an improvement of 96 basis point compared to same period last year.

items.statement: Restaurant operating margin improved from 11.2% to 12.4% YoY
items.quote: Restaurant operating margin grew year-on-year by 12.5%. That is an increase from 11.2% in quarter Q2FY24 to 12.4% in quarter Q2FY25.

items.statement: Mature store restaurant-level margins at 14% in Q2, potential 17-18% with SSSG recovery
items.quote: Mature store margins are around 14% right now. This is for the Q2.

items.statement: Average pricing growth flat at 0.2% YoY; no portfolio-level price hikes taken
items.quote: And the average pricing growth over last year, it's flattish. We have not taken any price hikes at a portfolio level. It's just marginal 0.2% increase in overall APC, if you look at the entire 222 store portfolio.

items.quote: We reported negative same-store sales growth of 2.5% during the quarter. Despite the prevailing slowdown in consumption across mass category discretionary spend, we've been able to improve our SSSG trend on a gradual basis.

items.quote: And out of 100 stores that we're targeting, we will have around 35 to 40 restaurants coming from Premium CDR, around 15 will come from international markets and the balance will come from Barbeque India.

items.statement: Flow-through from top line to bottom line around 50%; 5% SSSG improves margins 2-3%
items.quote: Our flow-through from top line to bottom line is around 50%. So any SSSG increase of, say, 5% will help us to improve our margins by 2% to 3%.

items.statement: Sri Lanka entry: first restaurant under construction, expected to start trading January next year
items.quote: We have incorporated a company and starting our first restaurant there. That site is under construction now and should start trading in, hopefully, January next year.

items.statement: Gross margin target 68% for full year; delivered in H1 with 80 bps from reclassification
items.quote: 68% is what we're targeting, We have delivered that in H1. And we expect to close the year also at 68%.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of not less than 25-30% annually, targeting 30% top-line growth for FY25
items.quote: We maintain this not less than this, this growth is very sustainable and not less than 25% to 30% growth is there every year. We hope it will continue and then even better than.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 21-22% for FY25
items.quote: Yes, that is around 21%-22%.

items.statement: CCS facility of 1,800 MTPA in Dahej scheduled for commercialization by FY26, requiring 18 months to commission after environmental clearance
items.quote: We are also progressing with the establishment of 1,800 metric tons per annum CCS facility in Dahej, scheduled for commercialization by FY26.

items.statement: API capacity expansion from 100 KL to 250 KL, with additional 150 KL commencing January 2025 and operational by January 2026

items.statement: Planning additional MCC capacity expansion within 2-3 years as current expanded capacity utilization reaches 50% by end of March 2025
items.quote: I believe that very soon we should be at the drawing board to look at an additional capacity for MCC because our consumption of the new capacity is going on track and going at a good speed.

items.statement: Gross margin declined to 47% in Q2 FY25 from 57% in Q1 FY25 due to market penetration pricing in expanded MCC capacity and API segment losses

Once we start exporting this to the regulated markets, I am very confident of having 20% EBIT positive.

items.statement: Wood pulp prices on increasing trend; 70% procured via annual contracts, 30% spot purchases; cost increases passed to customers

items.statement: MCC demand strong with 75% capacity utilization currently, targeting 95-100% utilization by mid-FY26; growing 15-20% vs global market growth of 10%

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guidance of 35%-40% remains on track

items.statement: Working capital days target of 60-65 days by March 2025
items.quote: Alok Dalal: And then, what can we expect the working capital days for March 2025? Prabhat Agrawal: Our target will be somewhere between 60-65 days.

items.statement: Internal organic growth target of 1.5-2x market growth rate
items.quote: Prabhat Agrawal: So, Gautam, we have always guided that our internal target for organic growth is 1.5-2 times of market growth rate.

items.statement: Similar acquisition pace of Rs. 1,000 crores targeted for FY26

items.statement: Operating cash flow expected to turn positive by next year (FY26)
items.quote: C. V. Ram: Yes. I think with the margin improvement and then optimization on the net working capital days that we are continuously targeting, I think by next year, this should be positive.

items.statement: 9 acquisitions completed in FY25 with Rs. 750 crores annualized FY24 revenue, Rs. 128 crores recorded in Q2

items.statement: Two binding MoUs signed in Kerala and Haryana, on track for Rs. 1,000 crores annualized revenue target

items.statement: Non-medicine portfolio at ~10% of revenue, includes devices, surgical, diagnostics; first Pan India device acquisition completed
items.quote: Prabhat Agrawal: Yes, today, if I look at the product level cut, almost 10% of our revenues are coming from non-pharmaceutical products which are non-medicines.

items.statement: Hospital business ~24% of revenue, growing at ~15% organic rate similar to overall
items.quote: Prabhat Agrawal: Around 24% is our hospital business today. Romil Jain: And what were the growth rates in the first half? Prabhat Agrawal: Similar to what, our overall organic growth rate is 15%, right, so more or less in that vicinity.

items.statement: Acquisition valuation multiples remain at 5-8x EBITDA, not expanded; market not more competitive
items.quote: We are still buying acquisition in, as I told before , 5-8 times of EBITDA multiple, not more than that. None of our acquisitions have exceeded that kind of multiple threshold and it is not difficult to buy targets

items.quote: Prabhat Agrawal: So, in first half, we sold to 80,000 retailers around, retail pharmacy. Nitin Agarwal: And where do you see this number really reaching over the next - what are the plans you have in mind over the next year and a year and a half? Prabhat Agrawal: Nitin, it is difficult to give the exact number because again you will hold me accountable for it. So, what we are saying, we are pursui

items.statement: Management anticipates upside potential to the FY25 guidance of 30% revenue growth and 1.5pp margin improvement on iGAAP basis
items.quote: With respect to the guidance, the one thing what I can only say is that we anticipate upside potential to the guidance which we have shared at the beginning of the financial year.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 revenue growth expected at 30%+ including Design & Build segment
items.quote: our total guidance is about 30%-odd. So, you can expect the overall D&B business to also on a whole year grow a t 30%-plus kind of a scenario

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY25 is Rs 140 crores; will exceed guidance based on growth needs
items.quote: Rs.140 crores was the guidance what we had given at the beginning of the year and keeping the CAPEX in line with our growth we will keep evaluating our capex expenses.

items.statement: Design & Build order book of Rs 175 crores in H1 FY25; portion to be booked in H2
items.quote: we have kind of received orders with about Rs. 175 crores in the first half. So, I just wanted to understand , of this Rs. 175 crores, what part would be executable in the second half

items.statement: Signed LOIs for 19 centers adding ~20,000 seats and 1 million sq ft chargeable area
items.quote: We have a strong pipeline with signed letter of intents for 19 centers, adding almost 20,000 seats and 1 million square feet of chargeable area.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 iGAAP EBITDA margin at 14.9% (+690 bps YoY); expect similar margin profile for rest of year
items.quote: The margins stood at 14.9% as against 8.1% in Q2 of FY'24, which is a growth of 690 bps.

items.statement: Blended occupancy benchmark of 70% for full year FY25 despite Q2 at 73%
items.quote: I think the 70% benchmark is a good benchmark for the whole year. This quarter, obviously, we have done much better than that.

items.statement: Seat pricing up due to micro-market rental growth; enterprise escalations 4-5%, smaller cohorts 5-7%
items.quote: For larger enterprises , it ranges from about 4% to 5% for companies with smaller cohorts, about 5 % to 7%, and this is how even our new sales are happening for this segment of customers.

items.statement: Elite brand seat realization expected 40-45% higher than base Awfis product; capex 20-25% higher
items.quote: From Elite we are expecting the seat realization, which will be about 40% to 45% higher than the Awfis product. In terms of the overall CAPEX, we are expecting the CAPEX to be about 20%, 25% higher

items.statement: H1 FY25 sold 25,000 new seats vs 37,000 in full FY24; Q2 sold 14,000 seats
items.quote: we have signed demand contracts for 14,000 new seats in Q2 FY '25 and 25,000 new seats in H1 of FY '25. To give you a perspective, we sold a total of 37,000 seats in the whole of financial year 2024.

items.statement: NSE mandate for 1.65 lakh sq ft at Adani Inspire BKC; partial revenue Q4 FY25, full from Q1 FY26
items.quote: Partial revenue for this transaction is expected to flow in Q4 of FY'25 and full revenue will start from Q1 of FY'26.

items.statement: Elite brand launch targeting GCCs; 5 centers planned (700-1,300 seats each) in key micro-markets
items.quote: the current plan is we will have these five centers, that we have selected across key micro markets where we see a strong GCC interest

items.statement: Managed aggregation model at 76% of seats including fit-outs; asset-light, risk-averse supply strategy
items.quote: We continue to expand our managed aggregation share with 76% of seats, including additions and those under fit-out signed under this model.

items.statement: No plans to launch SM REIT for fundraising
items.quote: So, as of now there is no plan.

items.statement: New Anjar Facility II to be commissioned in Q3 FY25, boosting capacity from 6,000 to 15,000 metric tons, total capacity to 112,500 metric tons
items.quote: We are establishing the new Anjar Facility II, which will be commissioned in Q3 of FY '25, and this will boost our capacity from 6,000 metric tons to 15,000 metric tons, bringing the total capacity to 1,12,500 metric tons.

items.statement: Board approved seamless pipe plant with 7,000 tons annual capacity, 900 million capex, 225 million internal, operational by Q4 FY26
items.quote: We have obtained approval from our Board of Directors to establish a plant for manufacturing fold seamless pipes with an annual capacity of 7,000 tons, involving a capital outlay of 900 million, out of which 225 million will be from the internal approvals.

items.statement: Seamless pipe plant expected to yield 4,500 million annual revenue at peak with 30-35% IRR
items.quote: At the optimum level, this plant will yield an annual revenue of 4,500 million at its peak, while the internal rate of return for the investment is expected to be around 30% to 35%.

items.statement: Order book at 11,921 million as of 30 September 2024, up from 8,001 million as of 30 June 2024
items.quote: As of 30th September 2024, our order book stood at 11,921 million, up from 8,001 million as of 30th June 2024.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 operating EBITDA margin expanded 196 bps QoQ and 195 bps YoY to 15.4%
items.quote: Operating EBITDA in Q2 FY '25 saw quarter -on-quarter increase of 20.2% and year on year increase of 24.5%, reaching 298 million with an operating EBITDA margin expans ion of 196 basis points quarter-on-quarter and 195 basis points year-on-year to 15.4%.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 PAT margin expanded 891 bps QoQ and 529 bps YoY to 10.6%
items.quote: Profit after tax for the quarter stood at 223 million, up by 598.8% quarter-on-quarter and 125.2% year-on-year with PAT margin expanding by 891 basis points quarter on quarter and 529 basis points year-on-year to 10.6%.

items.statement: New Anjar facility expected to bring 1-2% logistics cost savings and operational efficiency boosting EBITDA margins
items.quote: So, it will bring at least 1 % to 2% of logistics cost savings in overall revenue scheme. So, that will give us a good amount of boost, not only in terms of enhancing our EBITDA margins, but also this plant will bring a lot of operational efficiency.

items.statement: Seamless pipe plant expected to have around 20% EBITDA margin
items.quote: So, the EBITDA margin would be around 20% in this product line.

items.statement: Oil and gas order pipeline expected to remain extremely strong for next 3-4 years with 50% domestic, 50% export mix
items.quote: And, we expect at least coming three to four years an extremely good order book from oil and gas itself.

items.statement: Seamless pipe plant is 100% import substitute for P91/P92 grade pipes used in 660+ MW thermal plants and subsea projects
items.quote: So, it's basically 100% import substitute only because at present nobody in India is manufacturing these pipes. As a matter of fact, in India, even now normal seamless pipes are not manufactured in P91 and P92 grades for which we are establishing this plant.

items.statement: Medium-term guidance delayed due to new seamless pipe project; will provide on or before next earnings call
items.quote: However, since we have very recently initiated the seamless pipe projects, we have not been able to finalize the revised business plan incorporating the new project and we will surely get back to you with the detailed medium -term guidance on/ or before the next earnings call.

items.statement: IPO proceeds of 3,250 million, 2,769.25 crores utilized so far for working capital and debt repayment
items.quote: Of the total gross IPO proceeds of 3 ,250 million, we have utilized INR2,769.25 crores so far.

items.statement: Gross margin range historically 30-40%, sometimes above 40%, depends on job mix
items.quote: So, I would always say that the gross margin range would be ranging from 30 % to 40% and sometimes it is more than 40% and sometimes, many times it remains between 35 % to 40%.

items.statement: Steel price volatility does not impact margins due to back-to-back procurement contracts
items.quote: Therefore, I would say we have seen four to five cycles where there was a lot of volatility in the steel prices, but we have never got any impact in terms of the profitability of those volatility in the past.

items.statement: Management reaffirms target of INR 900-1,000 crores revenue in next 3 to 3.5 years
items.quote: So there is no correction as far as our forecast of reaching a INR 1,000 crores in the next 3 years to 3.5 years is very much there in place.

items.statement: Targeting PAT margin of more than 12% by end of 3 to 4 years
items.quote: we believe that our margins and profitability we are targeting to arrive at anything more than 12% of PAT by the end of 3 years to 4 years t hat is the vision

items.statement: Plan to roll out 11 stores in FY25 and reach 100 stores in next 3 years from current 64
items.quote: So, basically, in terms of our store rollout plan, there will be no stopping us and we will continue to roll out these 11 stores for this year.

items.statement: Order book at start of H2 FY25 better than previous year; B2B forecasts for Q3/Q4 awaited from Toyota and IKEA
items.quote: With a better-than-previous-year order book at the start of H2 FY25, we remain positive to have better business in the remaining quarters of this year.

items.statement: Gross margin run-rate at 56% from Q4 FY24; Q1 FY25 dip was one-off; localization and efficiency driving structural improvement
items.quote: We are at about 56% of gross margin run rate from quarter 4 onwards last year. And quarter 1 was an exception where it dipped because it was a one-off transaction.

items.statement: Pricing headroom exists vs European brands due to their rising costs; price increases expected in Level Next format
items.quote: So we do always continue to have a headroom to increase our pricing because the acceptance level in India also is constantly increasing.

items.statement: B2C retail grew 5% YoY in Q2; H2 typically contributes 55-56% of annual revenue; new store maturation and property handovers expected to drive growth
items.quote: We remain very positive in terms of B2C sales and we think we will definitely continue growing there.

items.quote: From 2025 onwards, Stanley is going to be positioned more as a luxury full home custom furniture manufacturing company and moving away from the typical Sofa only kind of company.

items.statement: B2B segment weak; awaiting H2 forecasts from key accounts Toyota and IKEA; B2B2C cash-and-carry transition caused 60% decline but normalizing
items.quote: B2B is still looking a bit weak. We have not yet got our what they call as forecast for Q3 as well as Q4. So we are hoping that will pick up.

items.statement: Net cash balance of INR 2,112 million as of Sep 30, 2024 supports growth plans
items.quote: As of September 30, 2024, Stanley Lifestyles holds a strong financial position with net cash balance of INR 2,112 million.

items.quote: Accordingly, we will be able to grow our adjusted EBITDA margins for FY25 versus FY24 in our core business.

items.statement: Post-acquisition objective is to reach breakeven quickly for Shipway through accelerated sales growth and cost synergies
items.quote: Our objective post transaction is to reach a breakeven point quickly, primarily through accelerated sales growth and realizing synergies across both direct and indirect costs.

items.statement: Initial 43% equity stake in Shipway acquired for INR 684 million cash; remaining stake via non-cash merger or stock swap within 12 months

items.statement: Shipway gross margin approximately 20% with courier aggregation contributing 85% of FY24 revenue; core Unicommerce Q2 FY25 adjusted EBITDA margin near 21%
items.quote: Gross margin for the company stands at approximately 20% with courier aggregation contributing around 85% of the total revenue in FY24.

items.statement: Shipway loss after tax reduced to INR 22.3 million (5.2% of revenue) in FY24 from INR 42.8 million (42.1%) in FY23
items.quote: The loss in the company is steadily reducing over the years and our objective post transaction is to reach a breakeven point quickly, primarily through accelerated sales growth and realizing synergies across both direct and indirect costs.

items.quote: Although the percentage-wise gross margin for this product is lower than that of Unicommerce's core business, the much higher revenue per transaction significantly enhances the gross margin potential in absolute terms and makes this business an attractive proposition for us.

items.statement: Courier aggregation 85% of Shipway revenue; shipping automation and ConvertWay make up remainder; aggregation expected to remain primary contributor
items.quote: Courier aggregation will remain a primary revenue contributor going forward as well.

items.statement: Integration risk acknowledged; Shipway to operate independently initially with thoughtful integration plan for cross-sell and cost synergies
items.quote: Shipway will continue to operate like an independent company and we will try to figure out whatever synergies are possible for the betterment of the combined entity.

items.statement: Acquisition funded through internal accruals; second tranche valuation expected slightly higher than first within 12 months
items.quote: So, on the funding of the transaction, we are funding this through our internal accruals.

items.statement: Combined client base of 6,500+ e-commerce businesses after acquisition with low overlap; significant cross-sell potential
items.quote: When combined with Unicom merce's existing network of over 3 ,550 clients, we will serve a robust collective customer base of around 6,500+ e-commerce businesses

items.statement: Targets double-digit EBITDA margin soon from current 9.2%
items.quote: We are expecting that the double digit margin should come by the, very soon because we are at 9.2% average margin which is there currently.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin to reach 12-13% in three years from current 9.12%
items.quote: In next three years considering the revenue growth and operational efficiency with the product mix changes, I expect around 30% EBITDA growth. So, we will move from 9.12% to around 12% to 13% of our EBITDA.

items.statement: Current order book of Rs.165.51 crore billable in H2 FY25
items.quote: Rs. 165 crore is the quantum of the order book which I am right now having it, which will be all billable in H2.

items.statement: IPO proceeds used for property purchase; security operating center CAPEX in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Majority of our CAPEX investment will get into building our own stock for which we have taken a property in market, and that payment has been made from the IPO proceed, as per our RHP.

items.statement: PSB Alliance empanelment with 12 public sector banks seen as minimum Rs.100 crore opportunity over three years
items.quote: Over a period of three years, it will be a minimum 100 crore kind of an opportunity for partner like Orient.

items.statement: Data center solutions to contribute ~25% of revenue annually; managed services to grow from 15% to 25% in three years
items.quote: Data center solutions will contribute to approximately 25% of our overall revenue, is what I can promise every year.

items.statement: Managed services to increase from 15% to 25% of revenue in three years
items.quote: From the manage services we were trying to move from 15% to 25%. In next three years, we will be moving managed services from 15% to 25%.

items.quote: So margin profile ranges between gross margin I can talk about, so that depends on product to product and LOB-to-LOB, but typically it ranges from 12% to 17% as my gross margin.

items.statement: Cyber security currently <10% of revenue; planning to increase year-on-year
items.quote: So, currently it is less than 10%. And we are planning to increase it year-on-year.

items.statement: Recurring revenue estimated at 35-37% of quarterly revenue from cloud and ITeS
items.quote: This quarter recurring revenue will be slightly difficult to tell right now, but it should be in the range of around 35% to 37% because any recurring revenue is between cloud and ITeS revenue is recurring revenue.

items.statement: Top 10 customers contribute 24.83% of revenue; customer retention 80-90% annually
items.quote: So current top 10 customers contributes to around 25% of our overall revenue, to be precise, 24.83%.

items.statement: Attrition rate 15-17%; revenue per employee ~Rs.50 lakh per year
items.quote: So current attrition rate in Orient is around 15% to 17%.

items.statement: PSB Alliance revenue expected to start from Q4 FY25
items.quote: I expect from 4th Quarter.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit sales growth for FY25
items.quote: If we look into the overall year of FY'25, we would be surely targeting to close FY'25 with a double-digit sales growth.

items.statement: Expect H2 FY25 to be significantly better than H1 FY25
items.quote: We for sure are seeing a better momentum in both the component and the trailer axle and suspension business from September itself and therefore we expect H2 of FY'25 to be significantly better than H1 FY'25.

items.statement: Axle beam extrusion facility to be installed by Q4 FY25, raising monthly capacity to 7,500 axles
items.quote: Our plant is already ready. The machine for it is already ready and we will be undertaking certain trials in the month of November. We plan to install this facility at our plant by Q4 of this financial year.

items.statement: Targeting 4,000-4,500 axles per month by Q4 FY25
items.quote: We are targeting to reach to approximately 4,000 to 4,500 axles per month by quarter four of this financial year.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin improved 64 bps to 12.2%
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for the half year improved by 64 basis points from 11.5% last year in H1FY24 to 12.2% in H1-FY'25.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin improved 58 bps to 13.1%
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for the quarter improved by 58 basis points from 12.5% in Q2-FY'24 to 13.1% in Q2-FY'25.

items.statement: Extrusion line expected to deliver ~5% cost saving vs existing design
items.quote: In fact, the cost saving of this would be at approximately 5% than the existing design.

items.statement: M&HCV demand recovering from September; October-November indications positive
items.quote: We have seen that from the month of September and continue to October and November, this has gradually increased as far as the major OEM's and Tata Motors and Leyland are shifting a lot to the prime mover segment.

items.statement: Government infrastructure spending supporting H2 FY25 demand outlook
items.quote: And now we see that the government spending has increased towards road building and various other infrastructural projects, which require a lot of vehicles. So that's why we see that H2 will be far better than H1.

items.statement: Export revenue grew 8x to INR8.9 cr in H1 FY25 (3.1% of revenue); bulk supplies of validated components to start in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Our export revenue in H1-FY25 stood at INR8.9 crores as compared to INR 1 crore in H1-FY'24, an increase of nearly eight-folds to H1-FY'24.

items.statement: Validated export components to commence bulk supplies in Q3 FY25
items.quote: The other components have also finished their validation stage, and we would be commencing the bulk supplies of those components in Q3 of this financial year.

items.statement: Trailer axle revenue share rose to 45.2% in H1 FY25 from 44%
items.quote: We have increased our contribution from 44% to 45.2% on the trailer axle segment, mainly because the M&HCV segment has performed quite weak, especially in Q2.

items.statement: No plan to forward integrate into trailer fabrication
items.quote: We do not plan to get into the trailer fabrication part of it.

items.statement: Deployed INR90 cr from IPO proceeds for debt reduction in FY25
items.quote: Out of the net proceeds, we have already deployed INR90 crores towards debt reduction for the company as planned in FY'25.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio at 0.1x after deleveraging
items.quote: The debt-to-equity ratio for the period stood at 0.1x.

items.statement: Pre-sales for Q2 FY25 were INR 215 crores, up 12% year-on-year.
items.quote: The pre-sales for Q2 FY '25 was INR 215 crores, which is up by 12% and collections grew by 43% to INR 179 crores.

items.statement: Arkade Rare project accumulated 50+ bookings worth INR 80 crores on launch day.
items.quote: We have accumulated 50 plus pre-sales and the consideration for that would be around INR 80 crores on the day of booking.

items.statement: Arkade Rare received close to 60 bookings in the first weekend after launch.
items.quote: week of booking, we got close to 60 bookings, which is... Devang Shah: How much, sir? Amit Jain: Close to 60 on the first weekend itself and the bookings are still ongoing very well

items.statement: Three new projects (Arkade Vistas, Arkade Rare, Arkade Views) expected to reach 25% construction threshold next year for revenue recognition.
items.quote: Arkade Vistas and Arkade Rare and Arkade Views, these three projects should be up for offering next year onwards, 25%.

items.statement: Healthy second half expected driven by Arkade Rare velocity, ready inventory in Aspire and Crown, and nearing completion projects Aura and Prime.
items.quote: So, ready inventory in two projects -- ready inventory in two nearing completion projects, and plus the velocity of recently launched Arkade Rare. So, that should give us a healthy second half of this financial year.

items.statement: Demand is very healthy for mid-segment value premium projects with built-in amenities.
items.quote: Demand is very good, as we've always seen. Demand is very healthy. For all these projects with built-in amenities, layouts that you see, the demand is very healthy in the mid-segment value premium projects.

items.statement: Pricing positioned in top 2-3 projects in micro-markets; highest in Borivali and Santa Cruz, second highest in Goregaon.
items.quote: We are almost always in the top two, three projects available in terms of pricing in the micro-markets. In Goregaon, Baring, Oberoi, our rates are second highest. In Borivali and Santa Cruz, we are first highest.

items.statement: Redevelopment projects PAT margin 10-15%; outright land projects PAT margin 25%+.
items.quote: So, though we do not have separate accounts on project-wise basis, but normally PAT for a redevelopment project is in the range of, say, 10% to 15% currently. We have had, we have seen better margins in the past. And the PAT for outright projects can be double of that, say, 25% PAT on outright projects

items.statement: EBITDA margin maintained at 28-30% range with nil long-term debt.
items.quote: So, we maintain a EBITDA margin of about 28% to 30%. I mean, that's the range. We don't have any debt as such, or nil longer term debt.

items.statement: Two land parcels identified for acquisition in Thane and Mumbai; process underway.
items.quote: We have identified a couple of land passes, and we are in the process of acquisition of them. One is in Thane and the other one is in Mumbai and they are in the process of acquisition, and you will hear from us soon.

items.statement: No Pan-India expansion planned; focus remains on MMR with study of Thane market.
items.quote: No, no, not Pan India currently. Currently, we are focusing only on MMR. That's a mature market and healthy market. And we see immense potential within the MMR region.

items.statement: IPO raised INR 410 crores; INR 380 crores in fixed deposits as of September 30, 2024.
items.quote: Out of INR 400 crores, about INR380 crores are in fixed deposit. As of 30th September.

items.statement: Construction cost ranges INR 3,500-4,500 per sq ft; cost as % of sales varies by micro-market (10% in Santa Cruz vs 20% in Thane).
items.quote: But broadly, it ranges between INR3,500 to INR4,500 per square feet, based on the details of the product.

items.statement: Marketing spend at 2% of top line plus separate 2% brokerage; consistent allocation.
items.quote: Our spend on marketing budget is 2% of our top line plus brokerage, which is separate. So, marketing is 2% and 2% may be the brokerage.

items.statement: Approval timeline from acquisition to launch averages one year for larger projects, six months for standalone buildings.
items.quote: So, from acquisition to launch normally a year is more than enough. If the projects are smaller ones, say, standalone building, it can be in six months also.

items.statement: Industry expected to see low single-digit growth this year on high base of last year's 8.5% growth
items.quote: we have been maintaining that this year the industry would see a low single digit growth on a very high base of last year, which of course came up with the growth of 8.5%

items.statement: Creta EV launch planned for last quarter of this financial year
items.quote: In the last quarter o f this financial year, we will be launching our Creta EV for mass market

items.statement: Pune plant construction progressing; start of vehicle production expected by Q3 FY26
items.quote: The construction activity at our Pune plant is progressing in full swing and the plan t is expected to have start of vehicle production by third quarter of financial year 2026

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 12.8% vs 13.1% YoY; H1 FY25 EBITDA margin improved 50 bps to 13.1%
items.quote: EBITDA margin was at 12.8% as compared to 13.1% in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Domestic discounts at 1.5% in Q1 and 1.9% in Q2 FY25

items.statement: Expect modest growth for full year FY25, exiting H2 at enhanced levels with positive margin impact

items.statement: Flashlight revenue grew 16% in Q2 and 7% in H1; rechargeable segment now 50% of mix
items.quote: Backed by these tailwinds, the category had a decent 16% revenue growth during the quarter and 7% for the half year.

items.statement: Alkaline battery manufacturing facility to be multi-product; may include carbon zinc and flashlights

items.statement: KKR arbitration status unchanged; matter moved to InCred and now NBFC companies, awaiting next hearing

items.statement: Lighting business targets INR 400 crore revenue for sustained break-even; 5% EBITDA margin at INR 500-600 crore
items.quote: We have maintained the annual level. We said that INR400 crore is a very good number to become a break-even for our organization, seeing the past trend.

items.quote: I have already told that from the Q3 onwards, the benefit will start reaping on and of course, Q3 starts showing that and Q4 will have the full scale here. So, H2 will have the benefit and what intended objective of the RTM exercise.

items.quote: So, segment wise revenue for H1. Batteries for us is a INR 456 crore, flashlight INR108 crore and lighting is INR166 crore.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance of INR300 crores may be delayed to FY26, with a potential shortfall of INR50 crores plus or minus

items.statement: H2 FY25 capex expected to be INR40-50 crores

items.quote: the guidance that what we gave perhaps may be impacted in totalit y by about, you know, maybe about INR5 -6 crores
