items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 17.9%. On H1FY25 basis EBITDA showed a growth of 42.5% standing at Rs. 88.9 crores with margin at 19%.

items.statement: Management expects present margin levels for at least 3-4 quarters due to market penetration and manpower investments
items.quote: So, for at least three to 4 Quarter we can expect the same level of margin which we have right now, or we look forward for the better margin.

items.statement: Realization dip of 5% versus March 2024 and 8-10% versus internal budget due to steel price correction
items.quote: We are in 8% to 10% then the internal budget which is primarily due to realization dip of 5% versus March 2024 and also 8% to 10% versus our internal budgets.

items.statement: Export revenue grew 2.7x YoY, now 33% of total revenue; expect export share to remain above 25% in coming quarters
items.quote: Venus has delivered impressive export performance this quarter with export revenue growing by 2.7X despite high freight rates, export now make up one third of our total revenue, which is a strong milestone for us.

items.statement: Domestic demand remains solid with healthy order inflow from oil & gas, engineering, chemicals and power sectors
items.quote: We see a major opportunity in sectors such as oil and gas , engineering, chemicals and power with the healthy inflow of orders.

items.statement: Seamless pipes grew 21% YoY in Q2 and H1; welded pipes declined 2% in Q2 but grew 13% in H1; both segments achieved over 30% volume growth in H1
items.quote: Sales from seamless pipes showed strong growth increasing by 21% year-on-year for both the quarter and the first half of FY25 . Welded pipe however show ed a slight dip of the 2% in Q2 though for H1FY25 sales grew by 13

items.statement: Targeting low double-digit market share in coming years driven by fittings and value-added pipes
items.quote: We are confident of increasing our market share to low double digits in coming years given our foray into fittings and value-added pipe and tubes.

items.statement: Ocean freight rates increased significantly in Q2, softening margins; expect rates to subsidize going forward
items.quote: there had been good export growth but in the last quarter there was a hefty increase on the side of ocean freights being paid on while you export the goods to various part of the world. That has rose by quite significant number. So, that is slightly soft en the margins

items.statement: Aramco and other major oil & gas approvals under process; expect most approvals within 6-9 months
items.quote: Hopefully every month or every quarter we are getting some of the approval from the some of the new company. So, I believe that most of the oil and gas companies, or particular what segment we are operating, what sizes we are manufacturing right now will able to get in the period of 6 to 9 months with most of the oil and gas companies.

items.statement: Capacity utilization: seamless >85%, welded ~60%; targeting 85-90% seamless and 70% welded by year-end
items.quote: It's more than 85% on the front of seamless and around 60% on the side of welded.

items.statement: Inventory days around 120 days; intend to maintain similar levels
items.quote: Inventory days are around 120 days sort of.

items.statement: Oil & gas sector currently not double-digit in mix; expect to touch double digits in coming year with approvals
items.quote: it's not currently double digit for oil and gas. But we believe going forward with many of the approvals coming in and again supplying to the larger pla yer in the country also we should be touching double digit in coming year to come

items.statement: Aim to produce in excess of 20,000 metric tons of bromine for the year including captive use
items.quote: We aim to produce in excess of 20,000 metric tons for the year of bromine, including requirements for our own use.

items.statement: Expect more than 1 million ton volume run rate for industrial salt in coming quarters
items.quote: H2 is generally better for our business, and we expect more than a million ton volume run rate in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Expect meaningful contributions from SOP next year
items.quote: At present, there's a work-in-progress, and we expect meaningful contributions in the next year.

items.statement: Expect healthy contribution from Clear Brine Fluids in coming quarters
items.quote: We have seen some favorable progress in these products and expect a healthy contribution in coming quarters.

items.statement: Expect two Oren Hydrocarbons plants fully operational within next few weeks with meaningful business contributions from Q4 FY25
items.quote: We expect two plants to be fully operational within the next few weeks with meaningful business contributions than anticipated from the Q4 of this financial year.

items.statement: Investing GBP 15 million for 21.33% equity in Clas-SIC Wafer Fab Limited UK
items.quote: Our company will be investing to the tune of GBP 15 million for a 21.33% equity share capital with a primary subscription of GBP 10 million and secondary purchase of GBP 5 million.

items.statement: Investing nearly USD 12 million in Offgrid Energy Labs for 21% stake
items.quote: We will invest nearly USD12 million in series A fund for the subscription of 21% stake.

items.statement: Capex of INR 50-75 crores over next 6 months for existing initiatives including Oren Hydrocarbons and derivatives
items.quote: I think our initial year after this outflow of investment on the equity side, for the next 6 months, we don't see too much of capex apart from what we're doing with Oren, I think maybe I would broadly put with existing initiatives, probably we will probably be between INR50 crores to INR75 crores over the next 6 months at the very most.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 standalone EBITDA margin at 36%
items.quote: EBITDA for the company stood at around INR898 million for this quarter, Q2, with a margin of 36% and net profit stood at around INR219 million.

items.statement: H1 FY25 standalone EBITDA margin at 37%
items.quote: EBITDA for the company stood at around INR1,747 million for the 6 months period with a margin at 37%.

items.statement: Bromine demand recovering domestically, export market soft; China stimulus expected to gradually improve demand
items.quote: We expect steady demand in the bromine business with end-use applications either stable or recovering. With the recent stimulus in the Chinese market, we foresee China economy to pick up gradually and the demand for our key products recover as well.

items.statement: Producing second grade of Sulphate of Potash with encouraging inquiries from global and domestic markets
items.quote: We have also taken steps to produce a second grade of Sulphate of Potash, which we're seeing encouraging inquiries from both global and domestic markets.

items.statement: Cyclone Asna caused loss of 472,000 metric tons of industrial salt worth INR 40.18 crores; insurance claim initiated
items.quote: We reported an exceptional item due to the impact of Asna cyclone in Gujarat that occurred in the month of August and in the beginning of September. So almost it prevailed for more than a week or so, which resulted in a loss of 472,000 metric tons of Industrial Salt, which amounts to around INR40.18 crores. We have initiated a necessary claim process with respective insurance companies.

items.statement: Flame retardants project delayed but not derailed; taking measured approach focusing on current initiatives first
items.quote: I think it's a commercial call. It's not derailed for sure. I think it's delayed, as I mentioned, I think on the previous calls as well. It's easy to always put capital, but I think we want to take a measured approach.

items.statement: Secured technology exclusivity in India for silicon carbide MOSFETs via Clas-SIC investment; roadmap 2-3 years to commercialization
items.quote: The road map from concept to commercialization will take between 2 to 3 years as a part of the first phase of this new initiative.

items.statement: Urban discretionary demand slowdown seen as temporary blip; cautiously optimistic for H2 with structural tailwinds
items.quote: Looking ahead now, we believe that the current slowdown in the urban discretionary demand is, we believe and hope that it's more of a temporary blip and not structural. We remain cautiously optimistic for the second half of the year and should benefit from some specific structural tailwinds in H2.

items.statement: Expect return to healthy growth from Q4 FY25, particularly from December onwards
items.quote: So, in summary, we expect these expansions, along with the upcoming SulaFest, to provide a boost to our wine tourism business and contribute positively to H2 performance. And in particular, we are looking to return to healthy growth from Q4, in fact, from December onwards.

items.statement: Elite and premium portfolio grew 7% YoY; share reached all-time high of 78.5% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Our elite and premium portfolio grew 7% year-on-year for the quarter, while economy and popular was down 18%. Share of elite and premium in our own brands improved 500 basis points, reaching an all-time high of 78.5% in quarter two.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 78 bps to 74% in Q2 FY25 driven by premium mix; EBITDA fell 24% to Rs 34 cr due to higher marketing spend
items.quote: Our gross margins stood at 74%, 78 basis points better versus last year, supported by higher share of elite and premium. Gross profit stood flat at Rs. 104 crores. Our expenses increased by around 21%, primarily due to the higher selling and distribution and marketing costs.

items.statement: Domaine Sula expansion near Bangalore to complete in Q3 FY25; 30-key resort at York Winery in FY26 to raise room capacity 30% to 134 keys
items.quote: Furthermore, the ongoing expansion of our wine tourism facilities at Domaine Sula near Bangalore is slated to complete in Q3. So, we have a beautiful new tasting room there with a beautiful vineyard view, a bit akin to our facility in Nashik, which was a bit lacking until now.

items.statement: Telangana grew 59% in Q2; revenue ex-Maharashtra and Karnataka grew 6% YoY
items.quote: Telangana stood out with a growth of 59% during quarter two. Success of second force strategy, as Rajeev alluded to, also helped Sula's sales force to focus better and drive premium portfolio in Maharashtra.

items.statement: Unsustainable competitor discounting in Maharashtra impacting net sales; wine tourism hit by poor road infrastructure and outbound travel surge
items.quote: There have also been, I would say, some kind of unsustainable discounting by some of our competitors. Unfortunately, the market does not have the kind of depth to allow it to easily withstand this. So, there is a fair amount of wine that has been produced, which is unfortunately being discounted in the market.

items.statement: Reopening Andhra Pradesh after 5-year hiatus; targeting first shipment in Q3 FY25
items.quote: These include the reopening of Andhra Pradesh, which would be after a hiatus of five years for us. We had voluntarily withdrawn from the state five years ago, and we are quite pleased that it is reopening with a more progressive excise policy. So, we hope to be getting back in there pretty shortly.

items.statement: Adding four new brands to CSD, nearly doubling portfolio; CSD showed strong growth over last 18 months
items.quote: We will be seeing the introduction of four more brands in CSD. CSD, I should point out, has shown very strong growth over the last 18 months or so. And we will be introducing four new brands, including our Dindori Reserve Shiraz and also our Source Grenach e Rose, our Sula Vineyards Riesling, and our RASA Syrah

items.statement: Resuming BSF shipments after 8-month gap; BSF performed well in H1 FY24
items.quote: We are also resuming shipments to BSF after eight months. And BSF did incredibly well for us in the first half of FY '24. So, it was a shame that due to some administrative issues we were not able to be present. We are now getting back in there, and we will get the benefit of that in H2.

items.statement: SulaFest returning in February 2025 after 5 years as wine and beer festival; likely biennial event
items.quote: A word on SulaFest. We come back after five long years due to overwhelming popular demand. This was a festival that was much loved and had grown into being one of India's iconic festivals. We had to shut down due to COVID. And for various reasons, after that, we decided not to restart. But now we do believe the time is right.

items.statement: Evaluating third state for new winery; decision likely within next year
items.quote: In terms of new wineries, you are absolutely right that the time has come for us to look at other states. And in fact, we are taking a close look. And I believe that more likely than not, within the next one year or so you would see some action on that front.

items.statement: Wine tourism spend per head up 9% YoY in Q2; tastings up 6% to over 50,000, an all-time high for Q2
items.quote: Spend per head and tastings, these will be the two key metrics for us. On both fronts, we did pretty well in Q2. Spends per head, as I just said, grew 9% Y-o-Y. And pan-India tastings are up 6% in Q2 to over 50,000, so an all-time high for Q2.

items.statement: Delhi excise portal migration disrupted September shipments; portal now mostly restored
items.quote: In Delhi, the excise portal was offline for much of the second half of September as they migrated from external management to in-house management of the portal, and which impacted sales during this transition. We were, in fact, unable to ship goods for most of the second half of September in this very important market.

items.statement: Karnataka excise policy changes caused temporary stocking hesitation; situation mostly stabilized with sales recovery underway
items.quote: In Karnataka, retailers were initially hesitant to stock up due to recent changes in the exercise policy, which introduced pricing uncertainty. This situation has since mostly stabilized after clarity came in from the state authorities, and we have started seeing already a recovery in sales there.

items.statement: Revenue less service cost margin target of ~20% by summer next year (next three quarters)
items.period: next three quarters / summer next year
items.quote: So by summer of next year, we should be looking at this number getting to about 20%.

items.statement: Current adjusted EBITDA margin on revenue less service cost is ~15%
items.quote: This INR13.6 crores of adjusted EBITDA margin is on INR93 crores of revenue less service cost, which is almost a 15% margin.

items.statement: Hotel & packages gross margin expected to rationalize to ~10% long-term (9-10% range over next 3 years)
items.quote: Over the next three years, given that the business would be largely focused on corporate and mice, I would expect this number to be range bound between nin e and 10

items.statement: Synergies from Globe acquisition expected slightly ahead of initial INR60M/year target
items.quote: As part of the combination of Yatra and Globe, we had identified synergies of approximately INR60 million per year. And as we move forward, we expect that we should be able to realize synergies slightly ahead of this initial target.

items.statement: Onboarded 29 new corporate clients in Q2 FY25 with INR1.2B annual billing potential
items.quote: In the second quarter of FY25, we onboarded 29 new corporate clients, collectively adding an annual billing potential of INR1.2 billion.

items.statement: Corporate air volumes show healthy double-digit growth; B2C air volumes stabilized and gradually increasing
items.quote: We continue to see healthy double-digit plus kind of volume growth on the air ticketing side on the corporate front. On the B2C front as well, as I mentioned, we've reached a point where we've been able to stabilize the volumes and the last couple of months we've started seeing a

items.statement: B2B now ~60% of gross bookings; hotels & packages ~65% B2B; Globe adds 360 corporate clients
items.quote: So in terms of gross bookings, now almost 60% of our gross bookings are coming from the corporate travel business, from the B2B business.

items.statement: International air ticket prices easing, expected to soften further in Q4
items.quote: The part which is getting a bit impacted on that, and this is not a negative thing, is just that the international air ticket prices are finally beginning to ease off a little bit and we would expect them to soften a bit more in the fourth quarter of the year.

items.statement: Globe acquisition: INR1.28B cash; Globe FY24 adj revenue ~INR470M, adj EBITDA margin >30%; 60% air / 40% hotels gross bookings split
items.quote: Globe Travels last year reporting adjusted revenue of approximately INR470 million and adjusted EBITDA margins exceeding 30%.

items.statement: Q3 underlying earnings expected to remain range-bound vs Q2 reported levels
items.quote: As of now, the trending seems to indicate that they shouldn't come off. They should remain range bound to what we had just reported.

items.statement: Management expects recovery to be gradual over next few quarters, not sudden, with focus on offline scale-up and Mamaearth experiments
items.quote: So, our entire focus is on that. That's said we expect the recovery to be gradual and not sudden when it comes to sort of getting back on the growth path that you talked about.

items.statement: Medium-term target of high double-digit EBITDA margin remains unchanged despite short-term investment skew
items.quote: But our view on being able to get to a high double -digit in the medium term for ME continues to hold strongly.

items.statement: Investing in R&D capabilities and partnerships to make hero products beat competition in blind testing across focus categories
items.quote: Our objective here would be that we build capabilities that in all our focus categories, our hero products actually beat the competition in blind testing and that's an area where a few of our products are already ther e but it's a constant journey through dedicated investment that we are going to continue to be on from an organization perspective

items.statement: Focus categories (face cleansing, serum, sunscreen) grew 28% in H1; aim to extend to 5-6 categories over next 3-4 quarters
items.quote: Our three strongest categories where we have the best shares and ambition also is the strongest in those 2-3 categories which is face cleansing, serum, and sunscreen have actually demonstrated 28% growth in half one and we want to make sure that this focus category approach we are able to extend that to five to six categories over the next three to four quarters

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin impacted ~10.7% YoY due to Rs. 63 cr inventory returns, gross margin loss, inventory and trade provisions
items.quote: So, there's a loss of gross margin, there's an inventory provision and also, we provided certain, trade loss related provision on top of it, which is impacting this close to 10.7% impact from a year-on-year perspective on our EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Urban consumption patterns changing; structural shift recognized but not yet fully understood
items.quote: There clearly seems to be some form or change in terms of consumer buying in patterns which are visible, but we genuinely want to see that and understand that as a structural change.

items.statement: Mamaearth top 10 SKUs contribute 40-45% vs 75-80% for mature offline brands; need to narrow focus to hero SKUs
items.quote: For most others, top 10 SKUs would probably, especially in the offline kind of environment, contribute to 75%, 80%, while for Mamaearth, it will be about 40% to 45%.

items.statement: Dubai distribution case ongoing; favorable India High Court judgment but unfavorable first appeal in Dubai; appeal filed in Dubai High Court
items.quote: We have a favorable judgment in Indian High Court, but in the first appeal in Dubai, the judgment has not been as favorable. That said, our lawyers are very confident on the construct of our case.

items.statement: Offline GTM overhaul (Project Neev): 70% ward cells have distributors deployed; remaining 30% to be covered in 3-4 months
items.quote: Currently, in about 70% of them, we have been able to deploy distributors but there are at least 30% of the ward cells where we are still deploying distributors and that will happen over the next three to four months

items.statement: Young brands (ex-Mamaearth) grew 30%+ in H1; Derma Co. doing phenomenally well with face wash entry scaling
items.quote: The young brands continue to demonstrate very healthy growth. And each one of them at H1 and quarter two level also have grown at 30% +, which is a great sign for the company as they scale and become much larger.

items.statement: Staze (color cosmetics) at Rs. 25 cr+ ARR run rate; early days in new category and mass-plus price point
items.quote: And it actually is already at a Rs. 25 crores plus run rate ARR. And we believe we will continue to learn on it and get our basics even stronger to win that category in early days, but yes, good signs.

items.statement: Inventory correction impact higher than estimated (Rs. 63 cr vs Rs. 40-50 cr guided) due to sub-stockist and trade inventory not initially accounted for
items.quote: But during the same period when we have actually executed this, they've also taken inventory from sub-stockists which owed them money, as well as to some extent in certain cases trade. And all of that has resulted in a higher net inventory take back compared to what we had estimated it to be.

items.statement: Offline ASPs 20-25% higher than mass market; offers retailers higher bill value and margins to drive adoption
items.quote: One, of course, as you premiumize a category in our ASPs, in almost all categories are higher by 20% to 25%. And that gives the retailer higher bill value per transaction and if your margins are higher compared to what they've been selling in the past, for the retailer, there is a much higher opportunity to sort of, make better money.

items.statement: Online consumer proclivity shifting toward actives/derma vs naturals; naturals seen as long-term consistent proposition
items.quote: in a ch annel like online, the proclivity towards actives and derma brands is far higher compared to naturals and we have different brands to play on to those different propositions and we need to invest accordingly to win in the category

items.statement: Media strategy overhaul: shifting from impulse/seasonality to always-on deployment; media mix modeling with internal and external data science teams
items.quote: The changes are not only towards the type of media, but also how we deploy media, where we were very impulse and seasonality-focused, instead of which we need to be far more always-on, in terms of our spread of media on these focus categories.

items.statement: Mamaearth pilots for new playbook starting in Q4 FY25 across 8-10 test cells (state/subcategory) with Bain partnership
items.quote: Now, what we are trying to do as part of pilots is taking cells like, a one state and or one subcategory and implementing a very different kind of a playbook on the same, getting into all of that is work is planned, starting now in Q4 and then seeing if it generates disproportionate results in that cell. And there are 8 to 10 such pieces which we want to activate in action

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 50%+ for FY25 with EBITDA margin around 8%
items.quote: In terms of overall current financial spending, as we have been mentioning in the past also, is to maintain the same spend that the company will be growing at 50% plus for the current year as compared to the previous year.

items.statement: Target ROE/ROCE of minimum 15% within 2-3 years and 17% in next 3 years
items.quote: So, first of all, the company is extremely confident and positive that we will achieve ROE, ROCE of minimum 15% in time to come, very shortly, within a span of two to three years, for sure.

items.statement: INR 240 crores capex over 3 years for Hisense AC facility (1.5M units capacity)
items.quote: And the estimated capex over next three years for AC business is around INR 240-odd crores. So we said $30 million, so that's almost INR 240 crores is what we are estimating in investment to create a capacity of 1.5 million air conditions over next 3 years.

items.statement: INR 40-50 crores capex for existing facilities over next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: So a max of INR 40-odd crores, INR 50 odd crores is what we're looking at in terms of investment in the existing facilities.

items.statement: Hisense partnership targets $1B revenue over 5 years across AC, washing machines, refrigerators
items.quote: This alliance aims to generate $1 billion revenue over next five years serv ing both India and global markets and leveraging our manufacturing expertise to drive innovation in home appliances

items.statement: Gross margin decline in Q2 due to AC mix shift (70% vs traditional 40%); H1 margins stable YoY
items.quote: So like, although we are not reporting on a segmented basis, but at the same time, the margins in small home appliances is comparatively better, or slightly more as compared to AC. So when the overall revenue mix has changed, this has led to the decline in margins on a quarterly basis.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at ~8% for FY25 (vs 8.12% last year)
items.quote: The guidance on margin remains the same. We have been maintaining that last year we achieved a margin of 8.12% the EBITDA margins and we are targeting to achieve similar kind of margins around 8% for the current year as well.

items.statement: AC 70%+ of Q2 revenue (vs 40% traditionally); small home appliances lines starting Q4; washing machine pilot done in Q2
items.quote: So Bhoomika, the mix for the current quarter is, AC contributing almost again, it's 70% plus in this quarter and non-AC, nearly 30%.

items.statement: Sricity plant capacity utilization target: 30% by FY25 end, 60%+ in FY26
items.quote: So, by end of this year, the overall capitalization what we are targeting should be a minimum of 30 percent from Sri City in this year. And next year onwards, we definitely look to further improve it to at least 60% onwards.

items.statement: Industry AC growth expected at 35-40%; company to outpace market; 17-18% CAGR over 3-4 years
items.quote: Even industry we can see is now talking about a growth of minimum 35% to 40%. So definitely that's one area.

items.statement: Commodity and forex fluctuations fully passed through to key customers (95% revenue) with ~1 quarter lag
items.quote: So, any change in commodity forex is a complete pass-through to most of the larger brands. So, all the key customers, if we talk about who contribute on the 95% of overall revenue, we have an arrangement whereby all the commodity fluctuations and forex fluctuations are passed on.

items.statement: Plain copper BIS certification (effective Oct 17) creates short-term supply challenge; domestic production expected from December
items.quote: Especially, I think the industry is talking about BIS on plain copper, which has become effective as of 17th of October this year. So, definitely, to certain extent, because the current capacities in India are not enoug h to meet the industry requirement, there is definitely a challenge

items.statement: INR 230 crores IPO proceeds in fixed deposits to fund Hisense capex and growth
items.quote: So actually, Mr. Amarnath, in terms of funding the upcoming new projects that the company is planning, the company already has a kitty from the IPO proceeds, which currently lies unutilized. Hence, we have a fixed deposit of INR 230 crores with us lying in the bank, which will be used towards funding the new upcoming projects.

items.statement: Exports grew 300% YoY; targeting US/other markets pending certifications by end of Q3
items.quote: So, there is almost 300% growth in our exports last year, but still the overall contribution is small. So, exports needs a lot of new products, I'll say additional product development.

items.statement: Asset turnover target: 4.5x consolidated, 5-6x for Hisense JV (current 3.25-3.5x)
items.quote: With the way we are diversifying into new product segments, we are targeting an asset turn of minimum 4.5. And this new company, because this will not be investing into a lot of backward integration, which will be catered by our existing investment. And the new company's asset turn would be anywhere between 5 to 6.

items.statement: Cost of capital 8.75-9%; working capital debt increase due to intentional non-discounting of invoices
items.quote: Cost of capital is 8.75% to 9%.

items.statement: Expect sustained double-digit growth in business in quarters ahead
items.quote: We expect sustained double-digit growth in our business in the quarters ahead.

items.statement: Expect ARR growth in excess of 10% and double-digit ARR growth in H2 FY25
items.quote: So, based on these statistics, we strongly feel that our growth rate will be in excess of 10% in terms of ARRs. Another very significant point is that we are now entering the festive and wedding season . This will also help in terms of the business and in terms of the ARRs going up. Last year, the ARR during H2 actually increased by close to 15%. And this year also , we expect that the ARRs would

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY25 remains Rs. 150 crore to Rs. 160 crore
items.quote: We have said the CAPEX will remain in the range of Rs. 150 crore to Rs. 160 crore. That will remain the same.

items.statement: Well booked on all wedding dates in hotels for season through March
items.quote: We are well booked on all the wedding dates in our hotel.

items.statement: Tea room EBITDA margin around 35%, cafe above 20%, kiosk about 10%
items.quote: In case of tearoom, as we opened in Mumbai, near the Gateway of India; so overall, the margin is 20% and for that tearoom margin will be around 35%. The cafe margin is also higher. Kiosk margin is on the lower side.

items.statement: Plan to add 250 new Flurys outlets over next five years, targeting 350 total
items.quote: Over the next five years, we aim to approximately add 250 new Flurys outlets, significantly enhancing our presence and market share in the fast-growing bakery and confectionery sector.

items.statement: Shift Flurys mix toward cafes and tea rooms from kiosks; plan 40-50 new outlets per year
items.quote: We are going to be more focused on opening more cafes and tea rooms. Our earlier strategy was to have a blend of kiosk cafes and tea rooms. There is a slight change in strategy. We are going to be opening more cafes and more tea rooms.

items.statement: Expect hospitality super cycle to last over a decade driven by connectivity, business travel, FTA recovery, middle-income expansion, spiritual tourism, weddings, MICE, wildlife, de-leisure
items.quote: We are in the starting phase of the hospitality sector super cycle and expect this cycle to last for over a decade, if not more. The industry's growth will be driven by improved connectivity, increased business travel, recovery of FTAs and the expansion of the middle-income segment. Spiritual tourism, weddings, MICE, events and wildlife tourism and a new segment of de-leisure are also expected to

items.statement: Plan to more than double keys from 2,410 to 5,048 over next five years including 830 owned keys
items.quote: Currently, we operate 34 hotels totaling 2,410 keys and over the next five years, we plan to more than double the number of keys, taking the total number of keys to 5,048. This inventory of 5,048 rooms will include 830 keys, which we will build on our own and will be owned by us.

items.statement: The Park Pune to open April 2027, Park Vizag additional 100 rooms by October 2027, Park EM Bypass Kolkata by April 2028
items.quote: The 200-room, The Park Pune, is now on course to open in April 2027. The Park Vizag additional 100 rooms by October 2027 and the Park EM Bypass Kolkata by April 2028.

items.statement: Expect ROCE to rise from 12.5% to over 20% in coming years
items.quote: We expect ROC E to go up from the present level of 12.5% to over 20% in the years to come.

items.statement: Lotus Palace Chettinad opening rates Rs. 12,000-20,000; Ran Baas Patiala Rs. 35,000-40,000, expected to reach Rs. 40,000-50,000+ by year end
items.value: Rs. 12,000 to Rs. 20,000 and at Ran Baas The Palace at Patiala in the range of Rs. 35,000 to Rs. 40,000
items.quote: Opening rates and bookings at the Lotus Palace Chettinad are in the range of Rs. 12,000 to Rs. 20,000 and at Ran Baas The Palace at Patiala in the range of Rs. 35,000 to Rs. 40,000. During this season between October and March, we feel that this range is expected to go up further.

items.statement: Exploring inorganic acquisition and lease opportunities; Ranthambore 50-room lease concluded for Dec/Jan opening
items.quote: We are exploring inorganic opportunities, which are acquisition including lease. One lease we have just specified, 50 room on lease, which has been concluded at the stage, which is the Ranthambore property. So, ready-made rooms now will be available from December or early January . We are trying additional lease properties also and, acquisition opportunities. But they are under discussion.

items.statement: Target waste neutrality by 2025, water neutrality by 2028, carbon neutrality by 2032
items.quote: We plan to achieve waste management neutrality by '25, water neutrality by '28 and carbon neutrality by '32.

items.statement: Jharsuguda plant 70-75% installed; tube mills and slitting line ready, awaiting power connection expected within one month
items.quote: The plant is I would say is 70%-75% already installed in Jharsuguda. Once the power line which is also very close government contractors are working at it.

items.statement: Total capex plan of INR 14,000 crore till 2027-28, with INR 7,000 crore committed including the INR 5,000 crore polycarbonate project and earlier INR 2,000 crore
items.quote: So around INR 7,000 crore, we have committed, including this INR 5,000 crore plus earlier INR 2,000 crore what we have just shared about nitric acid and all. And balance INR 7,000 crore is there as part of MOU where the Phase 2 will commence

items.statement: Nitric acid, photochlorination, hydrogenation and nitration blocks expected to commission in H2 FY25; MIBK/MIBC and acetophenone projects in H1 FY26; R&D center near Vadodara in H2 FY25
items.quote: nitric acid project is expected to be commissioned in H2 FY25. • Our other projects, including photochlorination, hydrogenation and nitration block are also commissioning together in H2 FY25. If you remember, fluorination block was already commissioned in Q4 FY24. • In the MIBK/ MIBC project, we expect commissioning in H1 FY26. • The acetophenone project is on track and expected to be commissioned

items.statement: Q2 FY25 consolidated EBITDA flat at INR 319 crore YoY, margin moderated to 16% due to higher raw material costs and lower recovery for few products
items.quote: In Q2 FY25, on a consolidated basis, revenue were up 14% to INR 2,053 crore as compared to INR 1,795 crore in Q2 FY 24. EBITDA at INR 319 crore was flat on a year -on-year basis. Margins moderated at 16% on the base of higher raw material costs and other utilities along with lower recovery for a few products.

items.statement: H1 FY25 consolidated EBITDA grew 15% YoY to INR 647 crore with 15% margin driven by Phenolics segment performance
items.quote: In H1 FY25 consolidated basis, the revenue grew at 18% to INR 4,239 crore versus INR 3,595 crore in H1 FY24, driven by performance of the Phenolics segment. EBITDA grew at 15% at INR 647 crore compared to INR 561 crore in H1 FY24. Margins came in at 15% in H 1 FY25.

items.statement: Advanced Intermediates segment EBIT margin at 8% in Q2 FY25 and 9% in H1 FY25 due to soft realizations and weak agrochemical demand
items.quote: In the Advanced Intermediates segment, revenue stood at INR 606 crore in Q2 FY25 versus INR 670 crore in Q2 FY24. While EBIT stood at INR 47 crore translating to 8% margin during the quarter under review. In H1 FY 25, revenue came at INR 1,322 crore and EBIT came in at INR 114 crore, translating into a margin of 9% due to current environment as explained earlier.

items.statement: Phenolics segment maintained 15% EBIT margin in Q2 FY25 with 29% revenue growth YoY; H1 FY25 revenue grew 33% and EBIT grew 64% YoY at 15% margin
items.quote: The Phenolics segment delivered an encouraging performance with revenue growth at 29% year-on-year to INR 1,443 crore in Q2 FY25 versus INR 1,120 crore in Q2 FY24. EBIT was INR 215 crore at an EBIT margin of 15% in the quarter. In H1 FY25, revenue grew at 33% to INR 2,907 crore and EBIT was higher by 64% year-on-year at INR 422 crore, translating into a margin of 15%.

items.statement: Agrochemical customers revising volume guidance down through the year, now communicating confidence in significant improvement in volume pickup from end of Q3 or Q4 onwards; CY25 expected more positive than CY24
items.quote: So just to clarify, agrochemicals, as a segment, a lot of customers have been constantly down revising their volume guidance over the year in anticipation of the end of this destocking cycle and are now also communicating back to us their confidence about significant improvement in volume pickup compared to the current and Q1, starting from towar ds the end of Q3 or Q4 onwards. So we can anticipat

items.statement: India polycarbonate resin demand ~240,000 MTPA in 2023, projected to grow faster than India GDP; currently 100% import dependent
items.quote: India's demand for polycarbonate resins was approximately 240,000 MTPA in 2023, and it is projected to grow at a rate exceeding that of India's GDP. Currently, the entire demand is met through imports.

items.statement: Domestic revenue share increased to 84% in Q2 FY25 from 80% YoY, exports 16%; reflects shift of volumes from Europe to Asia and wallet share retention
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, our domestic to export mix stood at 84:16 in Q2 FY25 as against 80:20 same period last year.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties, high interest rates, limited operating rates in Europe and China, low price destocking, volatile crude prices, and logistical challenges from increasing freight rates and sailing times creating mixed business sen
items.quote: Business sentiment in the quarter remained mixed due to geopolitical uncertainties linked with high interest, limited operating rates in Europe and China, low price destocking and volatile crude oil prices. While there are segments where we witnessed positive sentiment, a short-term challenge from persistently underpriced product availability from China has prevented a broader recovery so far. Thi

items.statement: No immediate cash flow pressure for polycarbonate project; company has INR 800 crore liquid surplus, Trinseo payments phased, and doable limits available; funding plans to be detailed later
items.quote: As regards to funding of the project, there is no pressure on the cash flow as of now, as we have liquid surplus of around INR 800 crore and payment to Trinseo is also in the phased manner. Over and above that, we have doable limits also available. We shall come back to the market regarding funding plans in detail in due course once we have evaluated various options in detail.

items.statement: Invested INR 34.5 crore in OXO Chemical Limited for polycarbonate compounding business to support forward integration strategy
items.quote: Additionally, we have invested INR 34.5 crore in OXOC Chemical Limited, which has ventured into business of polycarbonate compounding based products and derivatives. This should help Deepak Group with strategic objective of forward integration, but particularly when we have our polycarbonate plant now going ahead with the announcement phase.

items.statement: Company maintains zero net debt position with consolidated net worth of INR 5,125 crore; ROCE at 23%
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, our ROCE is reported at 23%, continuing our track record of consistently delivering value in the current challenging macro-economic landscape. You all may appreciate that with projects approaching commissioning gradually as stated by Maulik earlier, some of which are bottom-line accretive and some are top-line, we are gradually getting into a high level of integration, as

items.statement: Tax rate expected to be around 28% going forward
items.quote: The tax rate would be in the range of about 28% going forward.

items.statement: 90% of capex amount to be capitalized by end of FY25
items.quote: I think towards the end of this financial year, we're going to capitalize almost 90% of the amount, which is there in the period.

items.statement: Hassan plant has blueprint for higher capacity with space for future expansion
items.quote: The Hassan plant was not designed as a fixed capacity. It had a blueprint of capacity, which is much higher than the existing capacity. So yes, there is space there for future capacity expansion because we have constructed it in a way that we have sufficient space for future expansion.

items.statement: Actively evaluating greenfield, brownfield, whitefield opportunities in new states like West Bengal or UP
items.quote: Yes, we are continuously looking at new opportunities. And these opportunities are of greenfield, brownfield, whitefield, all three in nature. So as and when it matures, I mean, we will notify the required exchanges. But looking at our consumption story and looking at our capacity utilization, it's prudent that we look at a new state to set up manufacturing.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 40% in Q2 FY25 due to stable raw material prices and higher usage of old bottles
items.quote: The Q2 was characterized by stable raw material impacting material prices and higher usage of old bottles in our overall bottle mix led to an improved gross margin of 40% for the quarter.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 12.1% for Q2 FY25, up 28% year-on-year
items.quote: We achieved an EBITDA of INR35.2 crores to 28% increase year-on-year with an EBITDA margin of 12.1%, underscoring our ability to manage costs effectively.

items.statement: Power Cool beer price increased over 30% from INR100 to INR130 MRP in Karnataka
items.quote: There has been a price increase of over 30% on the Power Pool. And still, it remains the second most popular beer in Karnataka, even after a price increase of 30% on the MRP.

items.statement: Raw material and bottle prices remain stable; new glass manufacturing units opening to offset demand; sugar prices expected stable mid-term due to ethanol surplus
items.quote: As I briefly covered in my address, the raw material and bottle prices continue to remain stable. Also, there are a couple of more new glass manufacturing units opening up in the country. This is again to offset the growing demand in the country. And sugar prices are cyclical in nature. So if you notice every 3 to 5 years, there is a spike and then it comes down. On an average basis, thanks to the

items.statement: Industry growing at 9% CAGR; company growing at 29% (3x industry) with excess growth from market share gains
items.quote: Also, the other important thing is the industry itself is also growing at a CAGR of 9%-odd. And we are growing at 29%. So it's roughly 3x the industry. And the base is also getting bigger. So we look forward to this growth because we look at also activatin g other levers which are like more visibility about our products, more products from our shelves, a couple of more liquor products, some ready-

items.statement: Launched Woodpecker premium beer (India's first twist-cap) in Karnataka with positive consumer response; Legend brand gaining traction in South
items.quote: We have also recently launched 2 brands, namely Legend and Woodpecker, where Legend also has contributed significant volumes for the quarter as well as the half year. I would also like to mention that we have had a fantastic response to our beer named Wood pecker in the state of Karnataka, where we are experiencing positive tertiary from the consumer, which is a first step in premiumization of our

items.statement: Hunter became single largest beer brand in neutral market of Delhi in H1 FY25
items.quote: Hunter, which is our pr emium offering emerged as a single largest beer brand in the neutral market of Delhi during the first half of FY '25, which underscores our leadership in the territories

items.statement: Q2 seasonally lean due to monsoon and festivals; excise portals in Delhi and Rajasthan non-functional for a fortnight impacting sales
items.quote: However, we delivered our consolidated income of INR291 crores, representing a 17.3% year-over-year growth. Our sales for the quarter were also impacted categorically by the excise portals in Delhi and Rajasthan, which were not functioning for about a fortnight.

items.statement: Gross debt reduced by INR30 crores and net debt by INR35 crores QoQ; debt-equity ratio improved from 0.29x to 0.23x; credit rating upgraded from BBB+ to A-
items.quote: On the balance sheet, we reduced our gross debt by INR30 crores and a net debt by INR35 crores over last quarter, strengthening our financial position. This also brought down our debt equity ratio from 0.29x to 0.23x. Recently, our credit rating upgrade from BBB+ plus to A - is an indicator of improved financial strength and prudent risk management practices.

items.statement: Revenue concentration in Madhya Pradesh reduced from ~70% to 30-40% over few years; aim to diversify further with new units in other states
items.quote: So from that perspective, our revenues coming from Madhya Pradesh have been reducing and other states are sitting in with more. I think a couple of years back, we were roughly -- 70% of our revenues were from MP, which has drastically come down to 30% to 40% now. So therefore, that's why the need for setting up another unit, and we look forward to bringing this down further Som Distilleries & by h

items.statement: Optimistic about festive season and summer season preparation; Q3 festive and Q4 sales pick-up expected
items.quote: ahead, we are optimistic about the festive season as well as the coming season preparation for the summer

items.statement: Bhopal plant wraparound packaging equipment improved can production efficiency by 25%
items.quote: Operationally, we have commissioned a couple of equipments across our units and wraparound packaging equipment at our Bhopal plant, which has improved efficiency in the can production by 25%.

items.statement: Q2 product margins at about 10%, M&R margins close to 15%, services negative 4% margin
items.quote: We did see the product margins for Q2 at about 10%. M&R margins were close to 15%. And services, of course, had a negative 4% margin.

items.statement: PBT margin dropped to about 9% in H1 from 11% last year, ROCE fell from 21% to 19%
items.quote: If you look at the PBT margins, there's a slight drop for H1 compared to last year, where we closed at about 11%. Margin we are down to about 9%. The ROCE has subsequently fallen from 21% to 19%.

items.statement: Welding margins expected to return fast to steady state and push upwards a few percent from there
items.quote: Welding margins are abnormally lower in Q2, and we expect to return fairly fast to not only the steady state level we had prior to that, but within our target of pushing upwards from there to a few percent, which we think is definitely possible.

items.statement: Flare project in last 6-8 months, execution on track with conservative accounting expected to yield back-end benefit
items.quote: On the flares front, we're happy to report that it's progressing in a much, much stronger basis right now. We are in the last six to eight months of the project and we're getting a lot of confidence from the team in terms of their execution.

items.statement: New higher range welding equipment launching Dec-Jan, battery-operated welder with CE approval gaining international traction
items.quote: We are introducing a higher range of welding equipments. Most of these are competing against imported products. And we are continuously upgrading our technology accordingly. And we should see a new range of products being released over the course of December and January

items.statement: H1 volumes flat to 2% down, Q2 volumes slightly lower, steel price drop caused revenue dip
items.quote: On H1 basis, it's been pretty much a little bit 2% down as such. The revenue dip has happened as steel prices have tended to drop fairly sharply during this period.

items.statement: Hopeful of good growth in H2, exports targeting 25-30% growth for FY25
items.quote: I'm hoping that we close the year at approximately 25% to 30% in terms of growth for the exports. It continues to remain strong.

items.statement: Services EBIT loss largely due to ONGC project, conservative accounting, margin improvement expected over next 6-8 months
items.quote: The EBIT loss in the services is very much related a lot in large part to that project at OTC. It is a very large part is related to that. And as I said, we've been very conservative on accounting on that front.

items.statement: M&R division growth expected around 10% level, focus on international market and low-hanging fruit applications
items.quote: I expect that growth rate to be pretty much the region of anywhere between a 10% level up and down a little bit on that front.

items.statement: Steel cost pass-through normally 4-6 week cycle, shortened in Q2 due to demand drop
items.quote: On a normal basis, ideally, it should work on a 4 to 6-week cycle. This is normally how you should do it on a steel price basis. However, it also depends on what sort of demand you are sort of seeing.

items.statement: 3D aligner business impairment INR 32 cr due to drastic change in business projections, board conservative on valuation
items.quote: The nature of the dental aligner business in the last, I would say the last 6, 8, 9 months has changed quite drastically, which has obviously forced business projections and the reality on the ground is slightly different.

items.statement: Target 2% low-hanging fruit margin improvement next year, another 1.5-2% over 2-3 years from mix, exports, cost cuts
items.quote: We're looking at about 2% being as low hanging fruit that needs to be worked on for the next year. And beyond that, we need to push a little harder for another 2%. I think 1.5%, 2% -- 3%, 4% is what we internally talk about.

items.statement: FY25 H2 expected better than H1 on margins and demand, seeing early signs of improvement
items.quote: Yes for sure. I think it is as I said, it is an aberration. It should be a better H2, especially in terms of margins. In terms of demand, it seems to be like I said, little signs are there of being better than they were for those 3 months in the middle.

items.statement: Focus shifting to smaller, higher-margin projects with minimal site work, moving away from large offsite projects
items.quote: We may not see very large offsite projects being taken on, but what we will see is smaller projects with higher margins, because there's going to be more margin focused projects that we are taking on.

items.statement: Merger completed 25th September, all M&A costs (stamp duty, legal fees ~INR 5.7 cr) booked in Q2
items.quote: The merger was affected on, I think, 25th of September and we have provided for all the known expenses as of now.

items.statement: FY26 total revenue target INR 2,300 crores (INR 1,600 crores existing business + INR 700 crores Smart Meters) with blended EBITDA margin at least 11%
items.quote: Looking ahead to FY26, we anticipate robust revenue growth, projecting a 20% increase in our existing businesses, aiming to reach close to around INR 1,600 crores in total revenue. The Smart Meter segment alone is expected to contribute an additional INR 700 crores approximately, underscoring its strategic importance. Furthermore, we are focusing on margin improvement, targeting a margin of at lea

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth 20-22% excluding Smart Meters; minimal Smart Meter revenue expected in FY25
items.quote: FY '25, I think we already mentioned in last quarter, we are definitely expecting to grow between 20% and 23% in the top line as well as in the bottom line. It looks like I think we are in line with that projection as of now. This is excluding the Smart Meter again. And we don't expect big revenues to flow in on the smart meters for this year.

items.statement: First Smart Meter order of INR 45 crores received from leading AMISP; invoicing to start November/December
items.quote: I'm very pleased to announce that we have received our first order for the smart meters for a value of INR 45 crores from a leading AMISP in India. Though this is a very small step forward, but this is a big achievement. And it is a testament to our team's dedication to advancing smart metering technology.

items.statement: Switchgear EBITDA margin expected ~12.5% in FY26; blended company margin target at least 11%
items.quote: Out of INR1,600 crores, around 50% to 55% will be the Switchgear business. And the rest will come from Wire & Cable in the Building segment. Yes, the Switchgear margin EBITDA, we expect around 12.5% approximately.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia subsidiary: INR 10-12 crores investment in equipment/machinery; operations to start in 4-6 months; target INR 100 crores revenue in 2-3 years
items.quote: So we expect that this will happen 4 to 6 months from now. That is the timeline that we have got from various authorities on their adding a space. So once we get the space, we will start the operation, and this is going to be a INR10 crores to INR12 crores of investments in the equipment and machineries and in 2 to 3 years' time, we should be able to see a INR100 crores revenue coming from Saudi A

items.statement: Industrial Switchgear and Wire & Cable grew 20%+ in H1 FY25 driven by economic activity; transformer business grew ~30% YoY
items.quote: No, I would say that it's a normal growth that is coming from various industry sectors. As you have seen both Industrial Switchgear and Wire & Cable ha ve been about 20% -plus growth in this H1. So there is nothing specific, no new products

items.statement: Smart Meter capacity 40 lakh meters at full capacity (INR 1,000 crores revenue); 85% single-phase, 15% three-phase market split
items.quote: For capacity is what, 40 lakh meters? At full capacity, to the INR1,000 crores revenue.

items.statement: Smart Meter rollout slower than expected due to tender delays, reverse bidding, and field installation challenges; FY25 revenue may be minimal
items.quote: Yes, I think post-election there's 1 or 2 tenders have come up and some bidders have won. But the process is actually a very slow process. Even after winning the bid there is a reverse bidding that will happen, which will take a month or so to complete. And then there's, again, a lot of process that the bid winners have to undergo before they secure an LOI from the government to start to the work.

items.statement: Sold 1.5% stake in Kaycee Industries for INR 15.6 crores other income; may dilute further if opportunity arises but will maintain 70%+ stake
items.quote: The other income includes profit on sale of shares of our subsidiary, Kaycee Industries Limited to the extent of 1.5%. So that contributes to around INR15.6 crores and that's what is the other income.

items.statement: Kaycee Industries H1 FY25: revenue INR 13.34 crores (+13.3%), EBITDA INR 2.15 crores (+41.5%), PAT margin 11.5% vs 8%
items.quote: Kaycee's top line grew 13.3% to INR13.34 crores from INR 11.77 crores last year. EBITDA grew 41.5% to INR 2.15 crores from INR 1.52 crores last year. PAT margins in H1 FY 25 stood a t 11.5% as against 8% in H1 FY 24, which is an improvement of close to 3.5

items.statement: Export growth: Americas +7%, Asia +17%, Middle East & Africa +43% YoY in Q2; export share 29% of quarterly revenue
items.quote: Exports to the Americas grew 7% year-on-year; Asian countries grew 17%; Middle East and Africa grew 43% combined year-on-year in this quarter. For this quarter, the export share of the revenue was really 29%, but as for the half year, it was 28%.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 segment EBITDA margins: Industrial Switchgear 12.5%, Wire & Cable 6.9%, Building Products -4%
items.quote: It's around 12.5%, Industrial Switchgear; 7%, 6.9% for the Wire & Cable; our Building segment, we are still at negative 4%.

items.statement: Debt at INR 320 crores working capital + INR 17 crores term loan; term loans may rise INR 2-3 crores; working capital to remain at current level
items.quote: Debt levels right now, it's increased compared to what it was in FY '24. But to remain at this level, we are at around INR320 crores in working capital and the INR17 crores term loan, which is for the Smart Meter factory and other inves tments that we have made. The term loans might go up a little bit by INR2 crores or INR3 crores maximum. Our working capital will remain at this level for this fin

items.statement: Transformer business (low-voltage only) ~INR 250-300 crores annual revenue; grew ~30% YoY in H1; no plans for utility/distribution transformers
items.quote: Sir, our total transformer business approximately, because I don't have the product or a sales breakup with me, but I know approximately, we will be doing around INR250 crores to INR300 crores of transformer business in the current revenue approximately. And I want to be very specific here, we are not into manufacturing distribution transformers.

items.statement: Nashik ice cream plant capex estimated at INR185 crores with commercialization expected in April 2025
items.quote: The total capex for this site is now estimated to be INR185 crores, and the commercialization is expected in April 2025.

items.statement: Lucknow ice cream plant expansion capex of around INR20 crores to be completed before February 2025
items.quote: The expansion of capacity at the ice cream plant in Lucknow with a capex of around INR20 crores is in progress and will be completed before February '25.

items.statement: Board sanctioned INR15 crores capex to expand Mysuru beverage plant capacity by over 30%
items.quote: With increased demand seen the beverage category, the Board has sanctioned a further capex of INR15 crores to expand our capacity at our Mysuru plant. This will increase our capacity by over 30% from manufacturing and filling up beverages.

items.statement: Board sanctioned up to INR35 crores to acquire Orissa-based company for bottling mineral water for a multinational
items.quote: The board has sanctioned an investment of up to INR35 crores to acquire a company based in Orissa for bottling mineral water for a multinational company.

items.statement: Gross block expected to reach over INR1,800 crores by FY26
items.quote: With the Board adjustment and the constructive discussion with our clients, we now have a well-defined part of capital investment, which is expected to raise our gross block to over INR1,800 crores by FY '26.

items.statement: Shoe business integration costs of INR6-7 crores for H1 FY25 impacted EBITDA and profitability
items.quote: So on a very broad basis, Nitesh, the cost indication cost is what we could have better is around INR6 crores to INR7 crores for H1 total H1, right?

items.statement: Shoe business expected to turn profitable by Q4 FY25 as South factory ramps up to full capacity
items.quote: I think it will be Q4 of this financial year when South will be fully ramped up to its capacity. And broadly, I would say, around that time, you should be -- we should be able to see positive numbers coming in from the shoe business as well.

items.statement: Shoe business expected to have similar EBITDA margin profile to existing contract manufacturing business
items.quote: Our expectation is it's going to be very similar to the contract manufacturing business. It's our first year. So I'm hesitant to give you any definitive numbers. But given that the overall business model is very similar to what we are doing I do believe that the number should be similar to our existing businesses.

items.statement: Shoe factories have order book covering more than 100% of current capacities
items.quote: All I can say is that all our factories are BIS certified, all our factories have an order book which is taking care of more than 100% of the capacities that we have.

items.statement: Ice cream asset turns expected between 2 to 2.5x, lower than company average due to higher investment size
items.quote: No. Unfortunately, ice cream asset turns are a little lower than the average of us because the investment size is more. So it will go around it will it will be between 2 to 2.5x asset turns in the ice cream.

items.statement: INR225 crores from warrants raised in January still to come, will fund part of INR550 crores incremental capex with 1:1 debt-equity
items.quote: We have raised some money in January this year, which is in the warrants form. Some money of that is still to come around INR225 crores is still to come. And because these projects are also dedicated model where there is a debt equity always there, if we even take 1:1 debt equity ratio, then also this INR500 crores can be completed in the next 2 years.

items.statement: Hyderabad brownfield expansion groundbreaking done 2-3 weeks ago, targeting commercialization by May-June CY25
items.quote: We did the groundbreaking just about 2, 3 weeks ago. We started construction there. We are hoping that we get commercialized by May or June latest of CY '25.

items.statement: Shoe business integration challenges include inventory buildup, recruitment of 500+ people, and learning curve in South factory
items.quote: If you take a look at our w orking capital numbers for this quarter, you'll see a huge increase in inventories, etcetera. So Ganesh and team have actually gone ahead and bought material try to ensure that the lines are not starving for raw material as well as other materials. And in the South, we've just started ramping up the capacity being a very hands-on industry. We have -- there's a huge lear

items.statement: Dedicated manufacturing model guarantees 80-85% of gross block and bottom line, providing stability for diversification into higher-risk categories
items.quote: As far as dedicated manufacturing sites are concerned, whether we are manufacturing Home Care liquids or we are manufacturing, Ice Creams or we are manufacturing Tea. The commercial model remains the same, which is that it is a pay-or-pay contract. So from that perspective, it actually does not make any difference what we are manufacturing as long as it's a dedicated manufacturing site.

items.statement: Consolidated order book at INR 602 crores as of September 2024, up 27% sequentially, with 8 months visibility internationally and 5 months domestically
items.quote: As of September 2024, our consolidated order book stands at a robust INR 602 crores, representing sequential growth of 27%.

items.statement: Current order backlog around INR 600 crores; India business 5 months, international business 8 months to fulfill
items.quote: Yeah, so current order backlog is around INR 600 crores and for India business, it would be around five months and for international business, it would be around eight months.

items.statement: No capex project planned for upcoming year; only replacement capex
items.quote: For upcoming year, as such, no capex project is planned. We will stick to the replacement capex only.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margins for GLE business seen at 17-20% long term; current margins reflect recent order book downtick
items.quote: I think the sustainable EBITDA margins in the GLE business range between 17% and 20% in the longer term.

items.statement: Filtration and drying business sustainable margins at 16-18% long term; historically over 15-17%
items.quote: We believe that sustainable margins are in the 16% to 18% range, even with the current economics and dynamics.

items.statement: Thaletec standalone sustainable margins expected at 15-17% long term
items.quote: The margins, as we believe, on a long-term sustainable basis will be in between the 15% to 17% range for Thaletech standalone.

items.statement: Pharma driving uptick in GLE segment; chemical inquiries building but not yet converting to orders
items.quote: We are seeing that pharma is showing a stronger growth and we are seeing more interest from our pharma customers than we are seeing from the chemical.

items.statement: Filtration and drying seeing good uptake from pharma; healthier order book will reflect in next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: We are seeing a good uptake and encouraging demand coming in from the pharma industry, and especially during the recent quarters.

items.statement: Pharma share of revenue historically 35-60%; currently at lower end, expected to rise; agrochemicals and fine chemicals share to reduce
items.quote: Historically, pharma has ranged from a low of 35% to a high of almost 60% in our overall revenues. We believe that that end will be retained and will of course, it's a pretty wide range, but it will be within that range is what we expect.

items.statement: No plans to enter Chinese market; market fragmented with 20-30 players, not a priority
items.quote: So, we don't have a plan to venture into the Chinese market. Predominantly, the Chinese glasslined equipment market, especially, while this is true for the entire process equipment market, but this stands especially true for glasslined equipment. So, it's a very, very fragmented market with something like 20, 30 different players within the Chinese glasslined equipment market.

items.statement: Joint venture with Clean Max Enviro Energy by acquiring 26% stake in Clean Max Anchorage for up to INR 3.36 crores for captive solar (2.31 MWp) and wind (3.30 MW) in Gujarat
items.quote: We are excited to announce the joint venture with Clean Max Enviro Energy Private Limited by acquisition of 26% stake in Clean Max Anchorage Private Limited for a total investment up to INR 3.36 crores.

items.statement: Debt repaid INR 35 crores in H1 FY25; expect to double to ~INR 70 crores for full year
items.quote: I think to answer it very simplistically, we did INR 35 crores in half a year. So I would assume we should double it for the whole entire year.

items.statement: Thaletec range launched in India two quarters ago; ~25 equipment sold or under execution; doing better than expectations
items.quote: We launched the Thaletech range of solutions in India about two quarters ago. And over the last two quarters, we have made significant effort in promoting these products, as well as we have generated not just a strong interest, so in terms of order pipeline, but also we have now close to 25 odd equipment, which are either sold or currently under different stages of execution.

items.statement: Kinam integration phase 3 underway; NCLT filing for amalgamation in progress; breakthrough order in oil & gas
items.quote: We have received stock exchange approval for scheme of amalgamation of Kinam Enterprise Private Limited with HLE Glascoat Limited and are now in the process of filing the application with NCLT.

items.statement: Service revenue currently 5-7% of sales; pure after-sales may reach 10% optimal; automation and retrofit packages also serve service orientation
items.quote: So while service has, so strictly speaking, service in the traditional sense, it constitutes between 5% and 7% of our, or maybe roughly, let's say closer to 7% of our sales.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA guidance revised to around INR80 crores from earlier INR100 crores
items.quote: I don't think we'll be able to achieve INR100 crores, but let's say, ballpark is about INR80 crores EBITDA level.

items.statement: Panoli plant commercial production expected within 3-4 months, full revenue potential INR200-250 crores over 3 years
items.quote: Over a period of 3 years, INR200 crores to INR250 crores is what we are looking at achieving from Panoli plant.

items.statement: New API products at Panoli include Ticagrelor, Apixaban, Rivaroxaban, Lacosamide, Riociguat, Edoxaban
items.quote: These products include Ticagrelor, Apixaban, Rivaroxaban, and some new products like Lacosamide, and we are targeting to complete another new product, Riociguat in quarter 3.

items.statement: Penem vial filling line to take 1-1.5 years for hardware plus 6-8 months sterile validation, ideal target 2 years
items.quote: So the Penem vial facility is a sterile facility. We may take 1 year to do the hardware. But between 6 to 8 months, it requires for sterile validation, the environmental validation because this is a product which is a lifesaving used in hospitals, and then we need to get regulatory approvals.

items.statement: Penem API prices down ~25% in last 6 months due to Chinese capacity expansion and internal competition
items.quote: Penems prices have, I mean, gone down by about 25%.

items.statement: Penem volumes increased despite price pressure
items.quote: Volumes have increased, but prices are low.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 divisional EBITDA margins: Formulations 3.68%, API ~6%
items.quote: In this quarter, division-wise margin, if I say formulations, EBITDA margin is 3.68% and API is about 6%.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis elongating supply chain cycles to Europe and UK
items.quote: Already the impact is there. Our material to Europe and U.K. are all going around the world and reaching there. So that impact is already there.

items.statement: Teva ethanol supply progressing slowly due to Israel war, next quarter business spilling to next year
items.quote: Teva is progressing for sure. We received the first order also. But time line-wise, they are moving a little slow. Mainly, it has happened due to the Israel war, so the time lines are a bit slow.

items.statement: R&D pipeline: 10+ products under development, plan to commercialize 10 products in 2 years focusing on cardiac, diabetes, CNS, newer Penems
items.quote: Apart from that, we have more than 10 products under R&D. And in the next 2 years, we plan to commercialize 10 products. Our main focus is on cardiac, diabetes and CNS, apart from the newer Penems like Tebipenem, so few Antibiotics.

items.statement: LATAM registrations expected to come through next year, Middle East GCC dossiers planned for UAE next year
items.quote: We expect many registrations of LATAM to come through next year. Regarding the Middle East, the GCC is the biggest market where registration normally takes 3 years apart from plant products. We are already working in Oman and in Yemen, and we are planning to put in dossiers next year in the UAE also.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to return to 15%+ by Q1 FY26
items.quote: we see ourselves resuming back to the 15%-plus gross EBITDA margins by Q1 end.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin of 15%+ expected in Q1 FY26 if export mix stays at current level
items.quote: I would say if export remains at this level that is currently going on, we will achieve 15% plus EBITDA.

items.statement: Gross margin at 23.7% in Q2 FY25 due to 7% higher basmati unit costs and 3% higher realizations
items.quote: Our gross margin for the quarter was at 23.7%, impacted by a 7% year- on-year increase in basmati unit costs as paddy prices were higher in the last se ason, while average sales realization in the period rose by 3

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 12.1% in Q2 FY25 vs 18.2% last year due to gross margin pressure and higher employee costs, doubtful debt provisions
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 12.1% compared to 18.2 % corresponding quarter last year, primarily reflecting the impact on gross margin as well as higher employee costs, provision for doubtful debt and other expenses.

items.statement: Domestic branded basmati volume grew 10% in Q2 FY25 and H1 FY25 despite FMCG urban volume growth of ~2.5%
items.quote: In the generally slowing FMCG market, with urban growth volumes of around 2.5% in H1, we delivered an impressive 10% volume growth in the branded basmati segment, supported by solid performance across both consumer and bulk rice segments.

items.statement: Regional rice business revenue expected at INR 275-300 crores in FY25 vs INR 200 crores last year
items.quote: So last year, we did a INR 200 crores of revenue in the regional rice business, and we're expecting it to be close to about INR 275 crores and INR 300 crores in this financial year.

items.statement: Fresh orders of over 3,000 tons received from Saudi Arabia for shipment by end of December
items.quote: And we have got now fresh orders more than 3,000 tons from Saudi, which we have to export up by end of December.

items.statement: New processing plants set up in Karnataka, Gangavati, and Kandla Port for aged specialty non-basmati rice
items.quote: We have now put up a small processing plant in Karnataka also. We are putting up a plant in Gangavati also, we have already put up a plant at Kandla Port also.

items.statement: Margins under pressure for next 2 quarters due to high-cost inventory; expected to normalize by Q1 FY26
items.quote: You see we are carrying high-cost inventory. So margins will be under pressure for another 2 quarters. That is maximum. Another 2 quarters, we will be operating under 15% only, but first quarter of next financial which should come to the same glory of 15% plus.

items.statement: Inventory position by September 2025 expected to be highest ever due to aging requirements and higher procurement
items.quote: This year, our stock inventory should be higher than last year. So our inventory position in the next September '2025 should be the highest ever.

items.statement: No plans to monetize land bank; all land used for paddy storage and warehousing; buying more land instead
items.quote: We have a lot of land bank, but we don't want to sell anything. It is all in use. So we use all the land in storing our paddy and we have got about 5 million square foot of warehouses and our open land is used for storage of paddy and we are buying more land rather than selling.

items.statement: Management expects credit cycle to take at least a year to improve; sees potential improvement by Q4 FY25 if cycle started in April
items.quote: once a credit cycle starts, it takes at least a year for things to start getting back on track. And so if I say get this credit cycle started in April, which is when, it really kind of started surfacing very, very quickly. That would mean that by Q4 end we should start seeing things getting back on track or improving or getting better.

items.statement: Industry facing substantial rise in impairment costs due to overleveraging in rural retail unsecured lending and high field staff attrition affecting collections
items.quote: the industry is experiencing a substantial rise in impairment cost. This increase is largely due to over leveraging in the rural retail unsecured lending space , impacting both microfinan ce institutions and MFIs

items.statement: Company adopting cautious growth strategy prioritizing collections and portfolio health over expansion given severity of challenges
items.quote: Given these conditions, we have opted for a cautious growth strategy, emphasizing collections and portfolio health over expansion. This conservative approach is crucial to preserving the quality of our assets and maintaining a stable financial position.

items.statement: Consolidated yields at 25.4% and cost to income at 33.3% for Q2 FY25
items.quote: Consolidated yields for the quarter stood at 25.4%. Cost to income for the quarter stood at 33.3%.

items.statement: October-November collections disrupted by Diwali; rate of descent slowing but downcycle not ended
items.quote: November has been fairly disrupted due to the Diwali festival. So, as far as availability of customers and everything is concerned that became an issue. Right now, obviously its covering up and covering up very quickly, so that is good news at least. But yeah, I do not think this down cycle has ended and neither can you expect it to end. So, quick as well to be perfectly frank with you. But I woul

items.statement: MFIN guardrails being implemented; company establishing independent credit teams across all branches by end of FY25
items.quote: The MFIN guardrails have been introduced to manage overleveraging and we are currently in the process of also, establishing an independent credit teams across all branches by the end of this fiscal year.

items.statement: H1 FY25 total disbursements Rs. 832 crores, down from Rs. 1,068 crores in H1 FY24 reflecting focus on asset quality over growth
items.quote: For H1 F Y ‘25 total disbursements were Rs. 832 crores, down from Rs. 1,068 crores in H1 at FY’24. This reduction reflects our decision to prioritize asset quality and to focus on collections rather than growth

items.statement: Consolidated impairment costs Rs. 99 crores for H1 FY25 reflecting current risk environment impact
items.quote: The impairment cost were at Rs. 99 crores for the first-half of FY '25, reflecting the current risk environments impact on our financia ls.

items.statement: GNPA at 3.74% and NNPA at 0.64% as of September 2024; management overlay at Rs. 114 crores with ~50% towards 31-90 day bucket
items.quote: Our assets under management as of 30th September stood at Rs. 2,465 crores, while gross non-performing assets or GNPA stood at 3.74% and net non performing assets or NNPA to that 0.64%.

items.statement: Namra plus 4 or more lenders at household level was 22.8% at origination; outstanding less than Rs. 50k for 47% of customers
items.quote: the lenders at the time of origination at household level. I mean, was 22.8%, which is Namra plus 4 or more. And Namra plus 3 would have been about 18%. Basically, if you look at the outstanding, practically none of the customers at the household level for us had a outstanding of more than two years.

items.statement: Healthy liquidity position with Rs. 281 crores in cash, bank balances, liquid investments and undrawn CC limits plus Rs. 157 crores undrawn sanctions
items.quote: As on 30th September 2024, the company has a healthy liquidity position with Rs. 281 crores in cash and bank balances, liquid investments and undrawn CC limits. In addition, the company has Rs. 157 crores of undrawn sanctions from existing lenders.

items.statement: Zero DPD collection efficiency needs to reach 98.5-99% for improvement; currently not there yet
items.quote: So, I would say things will not improve until the zero DPD bucket repayment rate goes up to at least 99%, 98.5% to 99%, which is what typically what we used to. But even if it gets back up to 98.5%, I am confident to say, okay, the worst is behind us and things will progress forward.

items.statement: Regulatory risk on high-yield MSME book (28-32% rates) being monitored; RBI discussions ongoing but no specific action against Arman/Namra
items.quote: Honestly, it is getting a bit difficult to kind of predict what is in the regulators mind at this point. And so there is a lot of guesswork involved. What they want, what their intent is, I think the intent is quite clear , d o not charge more than you want or than you should

items.statement: Customer inquiries have decreased, indicating borrowers also becoming cautious
