items.statement: Actively scouting second acquisition in South India (coating brand with metal expertise); budget capped at INR100 crores.
items.quote: We are capping our acquisition in the range of about INR100 crores, not more than that.

items.statement: Welcome brand EBITDA margin ~15%, below Sirca core margins, diluting consolidated EBITDA.
items.quote: EBITDA here is coming out to be about 15%.

items.statement: H1 FY25 capex of INR22 crores was entirely for Welcome brand acquisition; no other capex incurred.
items.quote: No, that is spent for the acquisition of the brand Welcome. Dishant Jain: Okay. Apoorv Agarwal: Yes. We have not done any other new capex as of now

items.statement: Inventory elevated due to demand shortfall vs planning and Red Sea shipping delays increasing import lead time by 30 days; expect normalization in 4 months.
items.quote: in the next 4 months, we will be in a much bett er position because against the top 10 products will be here and the whole imported stock will be out, where we will be working at a 30 days inventory

items.statement: Marketing spend steady at 4-5% of revenue; focused on B2B architect/contractor meets in South/West; pulled back in North due to weak demand.
items.quote: currently, again, we are more or less on the sa me percentage that we did last year, which averages between 4% to 5% of our

items.statement: H2 FY25 revenue expected 8-10% above H1; full FY25 revenue in line with FY24; FY26 more promising
items.quote: Our forecast sort of shows that because of the sort of slow nature of the market, we have to sort of revise the overall forecast for the year. So, while H2 will be about 8% to 10% over H1, the overall performance for FY '25 will be more or less in line with FY '24.

items.statement: Export revenue share expected ~20% in Q4 FY25, continuing into FY26
items.quote: In Q4 of FY '25, we expect revenue share from exports to be about 20% of our revenue. And that trend then will continue in FY '26.

items.statement: Mahindra Thar ROXX 4WD bookings over 170,000 units with ~30% 4WD mix; transfer case demand over 50,000 units from first tranche
items.quote: The total demand that we are seeing out of the first tranche of bookings is over 50,000 units of transfer cases.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 28%, up 463 bps QoQ; expect to maintain margin profile going forward
items.quote: EBITDA margins for the quarter stood at 28%, improved by 463 basis points on quarter-on-quarter basis. This quarter, we regained our margin profile level and expect to maintain going forward.

items.statement: Invoked volume-based pricing clause in contracts to compensate for lower volumes; adjusted for commodity and FX changes
items.quote: So, we took advantage of that and were able to successfully renegotiate for the lower volume.

items.statement: Plan to add 5 new EV models over 9-12 months covering 35-120kW range for 4x2 and 4x4 applications
items.quote: the next 9 to 12 months, we hope to add -- not hope, I should say, that's the wrong phrase- we plan to add 5 new vehicle models to the portfolio and realize the vision of having a complete portfolio of solutions from about 35 to 40 -kilowatt to 120-kilowatt from the little A - class car to a complete full

items.statement: Fresh issue proceeds earmarked for automatic transmission capacity; 2-year gestation period needed
items.quote: And it's precisely for opportunities of this magnitude that we have done this fresh issue. And so, in a way, we'll come back a full circle and realize the original goal of putting capacity for automatic transmission manufacturing in India.

items.statement: EV demand slackening at Tata; Mahindra 4WD growth lacking; component export approvals delayed 2 months
items.quote: we, in particula r, have been affected by a slackening in the EV demand at Tata, which I think is well known in the industry. And the continuing sort of a lack of growth in the Mahindra 4 -wheel drive business

items.statement: Automatic transmission localization feasibility study targeted for completion by Dec 20; SOP ~2027; volumes >200k units
items.quote: We have committed to the customer that we will complete the study by the 20th of December. It may take a few days here and there. But as you can see, it's a question of weeks and months. And it is important that this project has kicked off in the first few months of '25 because the OEMs want the saving and by '27.

items.statement: Quoted on 3-in-1 EDU for multinational OEM in India; quoted on dedicated hybrid transmission (SOP ~2027)
items.quote: I'm also pleased to report that we have submitted a bid for what is called a 3 -in-1 electric drive unit for a multinational OEM in India to explore the opportunity to deliver the entire powertrain system.

items.statement: EV 3-wheeler segment gaining traction; new designs under prototyping for domestic and global (ATV/UTV) opportunities
items.quote: we have new designs that are under prototyping right now. And we continue to work with a variety of players, both I must add in India and overseas because these -- what we -- what the Indian 3-wheeler industry needs is also needed by the global ATV

items.statement: Export components on track; systems business could push exports >30% if kicks in next year, else ~22-23%
items.quote: If the system-level business kicks in next year, we could see exports at more than 30%. Without the systems business, the revenue -- export revenue will be well over 20%. I think it's 22% or 23%.

items.statement: Long-range EV transmission prototyping completed with successful NVH tests; portfolio to cover Tiago, Tigor, Punch, Nexon, Curvv + 2 unannounced models by Apr-May 2025
items.quote: We have very successful test results, not completed the testing yet, but the most important aspect of the test is what we call NVH, noise, vibration, harshness because that is a measure of the refinement of the gearbox.

items.statement: Defense supply chain bottlenecks resolved; significant uptick expected in defense work in Q4 FY25
items.quote: We are also seeing that whatever bottlenecks there were in the supply chain for the defense work have been unraveled. And so, in the last quarter, we expect to see a significant uptick in our defense work.

items.statement: Thar ROXX monthly rate ~4,000 units; other suppliers behind schedule causing flat orders till March 2025
items.quote: So, we should be at around 4,000 a month. And even then it will take more than a year to execute the quantity they have garnered in the first booking. So we understand that, that is because there are other elements and other suppliers who have not yet come up to speed.

items.statement: Working with European OEMs/Tier 1s on transfer cases, manual transmissions, synchronizers for ICE cost reduction
items.quote: We have been approached by both OEMs and Tier 1s from Europe in this regard and that exploration and investigation continues, not just in 4-wheel drive transfer cases, but also manual transmissions and synchronizers.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance of INR700 crores maintained, dependent on a large government contract expected to be finalized by mid-December
items.quote: We are working hard towards that line. And actually the one of the big government contracts is under consideration. And unfortunately the finalization of that contract is taking some time because of the value of the contract. Hence, it may be expected in next one month or so.

items.statement: PAT margin guidance for FY25 maintained at 4% to 5%
items.quote: It will be between 4% to 5%. Because earlier it was 2.5% types. So we have reduced some cost and when the business increases, we get the leverage.

items.statement: Post-FY25 target of 20% year-on-year revenue growth
items.quote: So, after this significant growth we want to maintain 20% year-on-year growth in the coming years.

items.statement: UPSRTC express parcel partnership expected to generate INR60 crores revenue over five years
items.quote: We were appointed as an authorized partner for Express Parcel Services by the Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (UPSRTC), securing space in 9,000 UPSRTC buses for parcel delivery services. This partnership is expected to generate ₹60 crore in revenue over the next five years.

items.statement: Government tender valued at INR500 crores, expected to contribute INR100 crores revenue in FY25 if finalized by mid-December
items.quote: The tender is a very big tender. We have estimated its revenue to be around INR100 crores. The tender value is INR500 crores. We are expecting INR100 crores revenue in this year of this tender.

items.statement: Plan to add owned assets of INR25-30 crores and leased assets of INR50 crores by March 2025 for steel and cement clients
items.quote: We will add an asset of INR25 crores-INR30 crores, and we may take an asset of INR50 crores on lease.

items.statement: Shift to light asset model via sale-and-leaseback and leasing; EBITDA margin slightly lower but PAT improving
items.quote: So, this is the light asset model. And in this scenario, the PAT is improving whereas EBITDA is a little bit minorly, there may be some reduction. But overall PAT is improving, and we are working towards the light asset model business that leasing is available in the market.

items.statement: Strong demand from FMCG and retail sectors; adding 15 new clients including Haldiram, Anmol Biscuits, Dalmia Cement, Supreme
items.quote: Strong demand in FMCG, retail sector played a key role in this performance. we continue to strengthen our infrastructure to navigate India's diverse logistics terrain.

items.statement: Targeting cement and steel sectors; 20% of a typical cement plant volume yields INR50-60 crores revenue; steel logistics spend by majors like Tata Steel is INR7,000-8,000 crores
items.quote: Basically what happens is, this is a very big industry, and in each plant, t here is a lot of production, like 50,000 tons, 1,00,000 tons, this is how much production they do. And if we work 20% of a plant, so 20% work is a very good volume, and 20% work will give us a revenue of around INR50 to INR60 crores

items.statement: Promoter warrants conversion ongoing; 655,000 shares already converted, balance 25% to be paid by mid-December, final deadline Dec 31
items.quote: promoters already invested in 655,000 shares already converted by the promoters. Rishi Kothari: And that should be converted by whom? Management: By December 15 or 20. The last date is 31st December. So 25% has been already paid. So balance we need to pay by third week or maximum third week we will complete this

items.statement: Two acquisitions in progress: one ~INR45 crores revenue closing in Q3 FY25, second ~INR170 crores revenue closing in Q4 FY25
items.quote: So, out of the two deals, one is in the maturity level, and it will definitely complete in this quarter, current quarter, third quarter. And the second deal will be happening in the fourth quarter.

items.statement: Cement/steel margins similar to FMCG on investment basis; better cash conversion with 1-15 day payment terms vs 75-90 days in FMCG
items.quote: No, FMCG is a bit low. But what is there in it is that in FMCG, payment terms are a little high. Like customers are paying in 75 -90 days and in this industry, the payment terms are very competitive and 1 week or 15 days. So, our margin on investments are almost same.

items.statement: Cross-border logistics to Nepal and Bangladesh for Nestle, HUL; in talks with Colgate, P&G for similar routes
items.quote: We are doing for 2-3 customers li ke Nestle and HUL , we are doing for this Nepal and Bangladesh, and we are talking to some other customers also because these are the countries where the plants are not available

items.statement: Added 121 fleets in H1 FY25 to strengthen operational capabilities
items.quote: Continuing our expansion journey we added 121 fleets in H1 FY25 to strengthen our operational capabilities to meet the growing demand and expand our market footprint.

items.statement: Management guides for approximately 18% year-on-year top-line growth for FY25, with bottom-line growth target of 15-18% before a one-time duty impact of INR 50-60 crore.
items.quote: we are looking at around approximately an 18% growth year-on-year. The gold prices have been on an upward trend but let us assume an 18% growth year-on-year in terms of top line. In terms of bottom line our endeavour from the very beginning was to grow about 15% to 18%

items.statement: Management expects full-year gross margin of 16-17%, with H2 margins normalizing to the same range as H1 (~15%) after adjusting for duty cut impact.
items.quote: Overall, in the year, we take a gross margin of 16% to 17%. So, therefore, I think there will be more of a normalized gross margin for this particular year.

items.statement: Store addition target remains 18-20 stores for FY25 despite higher gold prices requiring more capital; pipeline includes 6-7 COCO and 4-5 franchise stores.
items.quote: No, the store addition target continues to remain the same. Gold prices moving up by 20% to 30% would in effect mean that 20% to 30% more capital is needed to open the same number of stores, or you reduce the number of stores by 20% to 30%.

items.statement: QIP of up to INR 500 crore approved primarily for working capital to maintain gold inventory levels and fund new store expansions after gold prices rose ~25% since IPO.
items.quote: So, this QIP is purely in order to maintain the business at the same level and that is why we are raising this fund primarily for the working capital.

items.statement: October 2024 recorded best-ever monthly sales of INR 1,000 crore driven by Navratri, Diwali and Dhanteras falling in the same month.
items.quote: I'm very happy to share that this October, we achieved the best-ever sales in Senco's history. We surpassed INR 1,000 crore in sales for the month, with Navratri, Diwali, and Dhanteras all falling within the same period.

items.statement: H1 FY25 consolidated gross margin at 14.7% (15.7% adjusting for INR 29.83 crore duty impact), in line with 15-16% guidance; Q2 standalone PAT grew 40% to INR 16.8 crore.
items.quote: if you look at H1 gross margin, that is around 14.7% as against 12.2%. Now, if you look at quarter-to-quarter, obviously quarter-to-quarter has come down.

items.statement: Custom duty cut impact of INR 29.83 crore taken in Q2; balance INR 30 crore expected in Q3, total impact INR 58-60 crore for FY25.
items.quote: our total impact is likely to be around INR 58 crore to INR 60 crore. So now that INR 29.83 crore has come in quarter 2, balance amount impact will come in quarter 3 that is H2.

items.statement: October volume growth estimated at low single digits (3-4%) despite 20-22% value growth from gold price increase; wedding season expected to drive demand with 40 lakh weddings Nov-Mar.
items.quote: So, it will be around 3% to 4% volume growth.

items.statement: Studded ratio target 15% (currently ~10-12%); focus on daily wear diamond jewellery to drive growth; Sennes brand targeting lab-grown diamond solitaires 30-50 cents+ at affordable price points.
items.quote: Our endeavour is to take this stud ratio towards 15%. Currently last year it was 11%. We were aiming that this year we will be closer to 12% to 12.5% due to the market condition. We are stuck at about 10%

items.statement: Competitive intensity from unorganized players expected to remain high for 1-2 years due to gold price volatility; industry working towards sustainable growth models.
items.quote: So, for the next 1 year to 2 years minimum, the intensity will remain. That is number one. But at a much broader perspective, we at the industry level is also of the opinion that this is not sustainable.

items.statement: Hedging maintained at 85% of gold inventory (down from 95% in Q1 due to price rise); mix of Gold Metal Loans and MCX futures used to de-risk metal volatility.
items.quote: as far as this quarter is concerned, our hedging was almost 85% as we ended the quarter.

items.statement: Sennes brand expanded to 6 stores (4 added in H1); targeting 8-10 stores by FY25 end; focus on lab-grown diamond solitaires 30-50 cents+ and lifestyle products including perfumes launching next quarter.
items.quote: So, total we have six stores of Sennes and 2 to 3 more in the pipeline. So, by the end of the year, we will have 8 to 10.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance raised to 50-55% for FY25; confident of doubling FY24 revenue in next 2 years
items.quote: Given our strong performance this quarter, we are upping our guidance to 50% to 55% growth in our top line for FY25. We are very confident of doubling our FY24 revenues in the next 2 years.

items.statement: Board approved fund raise up to INR950 crores via QIP, subject to shareholder approval, valid for one year
items.quote: In line with our growth plans, we have taken approval from the Board of Directors for a fund raise up to INR950 crores, which is INR9,500 million, subject to shareholders' approval.

items.statement: Propel gross margins temporarily dipped to 3.5% in Q2 due to high brand usage; expected to normalize to 7-9% in H2 FY25
items.quote: So, from next quarter onwards, end of this year H2, we will get the margins back to normalized margins of 7 percentage to 9 percentage.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 9.8% in Q2 FY25; management aims to protect and grow margins over time
items.quote: Our adjusted EBITDA for the quarter reached INR29.5 crores or INR295 million, representing a growth of 36% year-on-year. So, for the overall total revenue has been INR302.6 crores, our adjusted EBITDA is INR29.5 crores, adjusted EBITDA margin is 9.8%.

items.statement: ESOP expenses expected to be close to INR100 million for full FY25
items.quote: During FY25, we expect to record total ESOP expenses close to INR100 million.

items.statement: Zoyer petty cash and BBPS solutions gaining traction with marquee clients like Dr. Batra's and Berkowits; fleet solution went live with Torrent Gas
items.quote: We foresee high acceptance of this solution in businesses with multiple location operations. Dr. Batra's Positive Health Clinic Private Limited is one such example. An existing customer with about 1,000 employees using the Zaggle SAVE solution, which encompasses employee expenses, reimbursements, and benefits. Recently, we were able to cross-sell Zoyer to Dr. Batra's to help them manage their acco

items.statement: TaxSpanner acquisition completed to add tax services; board approved investment in Mobileware Technologies for payment infrastructure
items.quote: During this quarter, we completed the strategic acquisition of TaxSpanner, which will allow Zaggle to add comprehensive tax services to our repertoire of products, which are under spend management solution. We have also received the board approval for an investment in Mobileware Technologies, a company leading the payment infrastructure development in India.

items.statement: International expansion focused on US market; leveraging India cost structure to offer competitive pricing
items.quote: In the international markets, US market remains as a key opportunity due to its vast potential. There are particular segments and segues which could possibly provide us an easier landing and faster expanding. We also see that there is a strong customer demand in the US for products like ours.

items.statement: Management takes conservative approach to RBI compliance; integrates directly with banks and widely accepted systems to avoid regulatory gray areas
items.quote: We've always held on the side of caution and taken a very conservative view when it comes to compliance and regulation. We've always looked to integrate directly either with banks or systems that are very widely accepted, so that we don't end up using platforms that are in the gray area.

items.statement: Revenue breakdown for Q2 FY25: SaaS/platform fee INR8.5 crores, program fees INR126 crores, Propel Points INR168 crores (gross basis, 7-9% margins)
items.quote: Our SaaS fee, platform fee, or service fee, the revenue contribution of this line, stood at INR85 million or INR8.5 crores in the last quarter. Program fees, the revenue stood from program fees at about INR1,261 million Indian rupees or INR126 crores. Propel Points revenue stood at INR1,679 million INR or about INR168 crores.

items.statement: Pre-sales target of Rs. 850 crores for FY25 with seven new project launches totaling GDV of Rs. 1,150 crores
items.quote: Looking ahead, we aim for pre-sales of Rs. 850 crores for the current financial year with plans to launch seven new projects totaling to a GDV of Rs. 1,150 crores.

items.statement: Raised Rs. 343 crores via preferential allotment and convertible warrants; Rs. 269 crores received in October 2024
items.quote: We have raised Rs. 343 crores via preferential allotment of equity shares amounting to Rs. 243 crores and an additional Rs. 100 crores via issue of convertible share warrants.

items.statement: Approximately 40% of raised funds allocated for new business development and land acquisition to be spent before March 2025
items.quote: So, mainly the objects of the fundraise is also for business development, so a good portion of that would be, roughly around 40% would be for new BD and land acquisition.

items.statement: Ongoing projects sold 5.39 lakh sq ft of 6.09 lakh sq ft generating Rs. 1,370 crores with Rs. 767 crores receivable; unsold inventory 2.71 lakh sq ft with GDV Rs. 395 crores
items.quote: The combined receivables of Rs. 1,162 crores from sold and unsold portion of our current ongoing portfolio are expected to materialize between FY '25 and FY '29.

items.statement: Future pipeline of 18 projects with 9 lakh sq ft carpet area: 67% value luxury, 14% luxury, 7% mixed, 12% commercial; GDV exceeding Rs. 5,000 crores
items.quote: The 18 projects are projected to generate a GDV exceeding Rs. 5,000 crores.

items.statement: Average realizations trending up over last three quarters: Q4 53,650, Q1 51,116, Q2 48,366 per sq ft; unsold inventory estimated at 55,500 per sq ft
items.quote: So, if you see our average realization quarter-on-quarter, Q4 average realization was about 53,650, Q1 was 51,116 to be precise, and this quarter was about 48,366.

items.statement: Construction costs seeing steady labor price increases but no substantial hike expected; labor shortfall may marginally impact costs
items.quote: But we do not see a very substantial hike in the construction cost, it's normally steady. But of course, there is a labor shortfall we see overall in the entire construction industry and I think that may impact the construction cost, though very marginally.

items.statement: Value luxury segment (Rs. 1-3 crores) showing steady growth in both realization and velocity; commercial demand strong; luxury prices expected to remain steady
items.quote: So, that is a constant segment in which there has been steady growth, in terms of not only realization but also in velocity. Even the larger ticket is doing well, but of course we see that prices won't go higher than this.

items.statement: RERA approval timelines extended due to increased compliances; Marinagar project targeting big launch next year, Girgaonkarwadi following year
items.quote: Normally RERA approvals take some time. The number of compliances from RERA standpoint also has increased in the recent circular. So, normally it does take time to get that approval compared to earlier.

items.statement: Bandra redevelopment project has first phase approvals; targeting launch between Q2 and Q3 next year
items.quote: It again depends on certain approvals, but I think between Q2 and Q3 is something which we are targeting.

items.statement: Commercial project at Tulsi Pipe Road with 1 lakh sq ft has approvals IoD and CC; RERA pending; GDV approximately Rs. 450 crores for this single project launch
items.quote: We have the approvals IoD and the CC for that particular project. It's just that the RERA approvals are pending which is taking some time. So, as soon as that RERA approval comes in we are seeing a GDV of approximately Rs. 450 crores of launch only in that one project.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit revenue growth in H2 FY25 after flat H1, aided by Raipur commissioning in Q4
items.quote: Hopefully, we should be able to deliver on that. First half was slightly out of our control because of the local issues and the floods in Tripura. Hopefully, we should be able to deliver in the second half, and especially with the Raipur hospital being commissioned in Q4, that should add more flip to the functioning.

items.statement: Aim to become a 1,000-bed hospital chain within the next 2-3 years
items.quote: As previously announced, we are steadfast to become a 1,000-bed hospital chain within the next 2-3 years.

items.statement: Maintenance capex runs at INR 8-10 crores annually
items.quote: The current maintenance capex varies between INR8 crores to INR10 crores on an annual basis. This is more or less standard.

items.statement: Raipur hospital (160 beds) to commence operations in Q4 FY25
items.quote: The Raipur Hospital, a 160-bed facility, will commence operations from Q4 FY25.

items.statement: Agartala oncology block: PET CT commissioned Nov 2024, LINAC by Feb 2025, full ops 6-8 months later, expected INR 20 cr annual revenue at maturity
items.quote: We have already started with the PET scan for this department and we are awaiting the installation of the LINAC. Once the oncology department is in full-fledged operations, we expect it to give a revenue of almost 20 crores annually after its maturity.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 80 bps to 24.2% in H1 FY25; Q2 EBITDA INR 26.3 cr at 24% margin
items.quote: EBITDA margin has increased by 80 basis points to 24.2% with a slight increase of 2% in EBITDA for the quarter to INR26.3 crores.

items.statement: Target ROE 20% and ROCE 25% for full year FY25; H1 ROE 11%, ROCE 15%
items.quote: We continue to remain on track to achieve the return on equity of 20% and ROCE of 25% for the full year with ROE of 11% and ROCE of 15% for the half-year ended September 30, 2024.

items.statement: ARPOB rose to INR 36,700 group-level; Salt Lake ARPOB up to ~INR 39,500, Dum Dum ~INR 41,400, Howrah H1 ARPOB up 21% YoY
items.quote: Notably, our ARPOB stands at INR36,700, aligned with our commitment to serving the aspiring population of the society with higher disposable income in the middle to higher income segment.

items.statement: Inpatient volumes grew QoQ: Salt Lake +8.4%, Agartala +11.8%, Howrah +23%; Bangladesh impact ~5% of Agartala volumes in Aug-Sep, now recovering
items.quote: If you see, there has been a consistent improvement in our inpatient volumes across all hospitals. Salt Lake Hospital has increased by almost 8.4% on a quarter-on-quarter basis, Agartala by 11.8%, Howrah, which is a new hospital, by almost 23%.

items.statement: Bangladesh patient volumes (~5% of Agartala) were hit in Aug-Sep due to unrest; flow restarting in Nov
items.quote: So, roughly, Bangladesh volumes in our Agartala Hospital is almost 5% of our patient volumes, which was impacted in the month of August and September. It is in November that we are seeing a re-trickling of that again.

items.statement: Strategy: reduce ALOS (group 3.51 days in H1) via short-stay surgeries (gastro, urology, ortho robotics, cardiology, cardiothoracic, oncology) to raise ARPOB and throughput
items.quote: Because of this, we've been able to focus on short-stay surgeries and if you see, we have been able to increase our volumes. Now, because of the length of stay coming down, the occupancy is seen to dip, for which we are now in a position to take additional patients.

items.statement: Ranchi expansion delayed awaiting Jharkhand regulatory clearances (state elections); no cancellation
items.quote: No, the Ranchi expansion has not been cancelled. I think we are awaiting some regulatory clearances from the government of Jharkhand. Currently, there are elections in Jharkhand. So, that process is getting delayed.

items.statement: Q2 operations impacted by local disturbances and floods in Tripura; no strikes in hospitals
items.quote: There was an unstable environment in Q2 on account of local situations. So, which did end up impacting operations for us. So, and there was no strike. Yes, doctors were protesting, but there was no strike in any of our hospitals.

items.statement: Acquisition pipeline: evaluating opportunities, no deal closed, no fixed timeline; committed to 1,000-bed target by 2027
items.quote: As of now, there is no update on the acquisition. We are evaluating opportunities. Unfortunately, we have not been able to close one at this point.

items.statement: Howrah orthopedic surgical robot procurement underway, expected availability by year-end
items.quote: We are in the process of procuring an orthopedic surgical robot for this hospital as well. The facility shall be available by the end of the year.

items.statement: Dum Dum adding full-fledged cardiothoracic surgery setup and revamping clinical offerings
items.quote: The company intends to commence a full-fledged cardiothoracic surgery setup and is revamping its other clinical offerings in this hospital as well to further strengthen its scope of service.

items.statement: Order book is looking very nicely placed and signs are looking very good
items.quote: Our order book is looking very nicely placed. Our endeavor is to grow last year's number.

items.statement: Second half of the year is much heavier than the first half; last year H1 was INR70 crores out of INR237 crores full year
items.quote: Our second half of the year is much heavier than the first half. I mean, if we compare it to last year, out of INR237 crores, we only did INR70 crores in the first half of the year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expands in H2 because fixed costs stay flat while revenue rises
items.quote: Our cost remains the same. You know, we do not have a raw material cost, we do not have any plant and machinery. It is the fixed cost which is there, for example, the rentals which we have, the manpower which we have, the overheads which we have.

items.statement: Opened Kolkata office with a 24-year industry veteran to tap eastern India clients
items.quote: We've opened our Kolkata office. We've hired a new team under the leadership of a gentleman who has about 24 years of work experience in the MICE industry.

items.statement: No sign of recession; order booking is very strong with two large international orders executed
items.quote: Our order booking is very strong and our performance is there in front of you. So there is no recession, nothing which we, kind of, have to worry about.

items.statement: Entering B2C via Book My Yatra portal and targeting religious tourism around Kumbh Mela
items.quote: We are also working towards, the religious tourism, which we had wished to penetrate into. And, you would be aware that there is Kumbh Mela, which is being, planned. So we wish to, do extensive B2C sales during that Kumbh.

items.statement: Working capital increased to over INR50 crores post-IPO from INR30 crores a year ago
items.quote: Sir, we have working capital more than INR50 crores. You can see the result s, INR50 crores plus

items.statement: No fixed EBITDA margin floor for bidding; margins vary case by case and by domestic vs international
items.quote: It is not that way. We want to pick up the business, which gives us, of course, a short profit. There is no formula which is fixed that we would work on this margin only.

items.statement: Management will disclose order book numbers by middle of next week
items.quote: The team has noted it and we shall by middle of next week come back to you with the order book numbers and I'm sure you'll be happy to see those numbers.

items.statement: Secured a long-term order from Tata Steel for Joda sponge iron plant worth over INR40 crores for three years covering first mile and handling operations for loose and bagged DRI.
items.quote: An important milestone that we have achieved in this quarter is that we have secured an order from Tata Steel for their Joda sponge iron plant in which we are going to be doing their entire first mile and handling operations at their site, which is an order in excess of INR40 crores.

items.statement: Demand is strong in metals, FMCG, industrial chemicals, and MSMEs; EXIM volumes expected to grow in H2 after flat H1 due to geopolitical disruptions.
items.quote: So the demand is looking good in the metal side. We are also seeing strong demand arising in FMCG, industrial chemicals, as well as MSMEs. So the demand is very strong right now, sir.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin improved 53 bps to 8.38% from 7.86% in H1 FY24 led by cost optimization and reduction of redundancies like detention and damage.
items.quote: EBITDA margins, like I said, have improved 53 basis points to 8.38% from 7.86% in H1 FY24. This is led by cost optimization, like I said.

items.statement: Fuel cost pass-through via DPVC (diesel price variation clause) in most large road contracts; rail haulage changes passed through to customers, providing a natural hedge.
items.quote: So fuel costs, what happens? I want to tell you that most of the fuel costs of all our large contracts, most of them are on a DPVC basis. DPVC is diesel price variation cost. So if the diesel price goes up, my rates will go up.

items.statement: Incurred capex of around INR67-68 crores over the last two years for specialized customized containers not available in the market.
items.quote: One is that we have done a capex of around INR67 crores, INR68 crores in the last two years in buying specialized containers that are not available in the market, which are customized for our customers.

items.statement: Working capital receivables elevated at ~4 months due to elongated payment cycles post-COVID and new complex supply chain projects; improvement expected in next 3-4 quarters, especially from MSMEs.
items.quote: No, for sure, this is going to improve, sir. And the improvements, not across the company, but across several sectors, we are already seeing the improvements, especially in MSME businesses.

items.statement: Used INR163.5 crores from IPO proceeds to repay outstanding working capital borrowings.
items.quote: We also cleared out a large chunk of our working capital borrowings from our IPO proceeds. We paid out INR163.5 crores of outstanding borrowings from our IPO proceeds.

items.statement: Domestic container volumes grew in H1 FY25 (approx 39,500 containers) while EXIM volumes were flat (approx 65,000 containers); domestic growth offset EXIM weakness.
items.quote: So we did approximately 39,500 containers in domestic. And in EXIM, we did approximately 65,000 containers for H1 of this year. This is a growth of about 1,200 containers from last year H1.

items.statement: Expect H2 FY25 to be strong with EXIM numbers showing growth like domestic; busy season for railway starts 1st October driving second-half volumes.
items.quote: We are very positive and hopeful that H2, the EXIM numbers will also show growth just like we are showing in the domestic.

items.statement: Asset-light model maintained with 80-85% of volumes from non-owned assets; only critical supply chain assets like reach stackers and forklifts owned.
items.quote: So, my business, from my owned assets would be a fraction of my total business. Though we don't salami slice our financials in the way that you are asking. But I would say that maybe 80%, 85% of my volumes would come from non-owned assets.

items.statement: Expect close to 40% to 50% growth in defense revenue this year and hope to keep substantial growth next year
items.quote: Last year, we did about 1,300 crores. So, we have said that we will have close to 40% to 50% growth this year. We are hoping that we are able to keep a substantial level of growth even going forward next year.

items.statement: Executable defense order book stands at about Rs. 5,900 crores as of 30th September, excluding potential domestic or export orders
items.quote: And with order wins of almost Rs. 1,400 crores in H1, the executable order book as on 30th September now stands at about Rs. 5,900 crores. This order book does not include any potential orders from the domestic or export market.

items.statement: US second phase CAPEX nearly complete with only $8-10 million remaining; India second half CAPEX significantly lower, mainly maintenance
items.quote: There is not much CAPEX left in the subsidiaries. This was for our second phase in the U.S. There is hardly anything left there. Maybe about $8-10 million. The rest of it was all in India. And I think in the second half, in India, we have about significantly lower CAPEX. So, we will just have the maintenance CAPEX.

items.statement: Aerospace order wins of almost Rs. 300 crores in H1 exceed full year FY24 revenue of Rs. 240 crores; expect business to grow multiple times current size
items.quote: Almost 300 crores of that is aerospace. Put that into context, last year our aerospace business was 240 crores. So, it's more than the entire business we did last year. And this is an annualized kind of business that we will do going forward once it fully ramps up. So, we expect to see the aerospace business grow quite substantially and become multiple times the size of its business that it is now

items.statement: EV vertical expected to reach EBITDA break-even in next two to three quarters despite European slowdown
items.quote: I will expect the EV vertical to be EBITDA break-even in the next two to three quarters. Because of the current slowdown and downturn in Europe, it is taking a little longer, but we are still working hard at it, and we are confident that we will get this under control as soon as possible.

items.statement: European operations about a quarter or two away from achieving decent margins; aluminum side actions completed with results visible next year; steel side facing demand issues
items.quote: I think we are about a quarter or two away from getting to that level in Europe. On the aluminum side, we have made a lot of good progress, and I think from next year, we will have a much better situation. On the steel side, we have issues on demand and therefore we are doing a lot of work on the cost side.

items.statement: Downsizing European and Swedish operations; committed to fixing these businesses in a short period of time
items.quote: We are feeling some pain in our European and Swedish operations. We are downsizing these operations. And we have committed that we will fix these businesses in a short period of time, and that is what we are working on.

items.statement: ATAGS order expected this financial year; revenue contribution from Q1 FY26 directionally correct with 6-7 month process after order for FOPM approval then bulk supplies
items.quote: So, everything you said before Q1 '26 is directionally correct. There is a process. First, the order has to get, there is a negotiation process, then you get the order, contracting is done, then you have to do FOPM supplies and then you have to start bulk supplies once the FOPM is approved. So, this whole process of approval past the, after getting the full order takes about 6 to 7 months and then

items.statement: Domestic defense revenue expected to grow faster than exports from next year; domestic to become 30% to 40% of overall defense business; naval systems identified as key domestic growth area for next 12-24 months
items.quote: I would expect our revenues in India from next year to grow at a faster rate than the revenues from export simply because we are starting from a smaller base, and eventually I think domestic will become 30% to 40% over our overall business.

items.statement: US aluminum second phase will double capacity and come online next year
items.quote: It will double the capacity. It will come out live only next year.

items.statement: India MHCV demand muted in H1 due to election cycle and inventory factors; OEM outlook reasonably positive; better traction expected in one or two quarters as inventory clears
items.quote: The general belief is that the India growth story is still intact, and we should start seeing a better traction in terms of orders including MHCV. But it might take maybe one or two quarters for it to start being more visible as inventory and all of that disappears from the system. But overall, the outlook of most OEMs is reasonably positive. Not excessively positive, but positive.

items.statement: Enabling resolutions for subsidiary investments over next 12-18 months largely India-based including loan repayments; no new projects outside India
items.quote: So, Pramod, these are the enabling resolutions, and the investment will happen over a period of time, but this is not a new investment, or we are not going to do any new projects outside India. This is largely India based and some of the loan repayments which we are planning to do.

items.statement: Traditional business won new orders of about Rs. 646 crores in H1; total order wins across segments Rs. 2,200 crores in H1 dominated by defense Rs. 1,400 crores, aerospace ~Rs. 300 crores, JSA and traditional
items.quote: The traditional business won new orders of about Rs. 646 crores in H1. And during the same period, across the segments, we won orders of Rs. 2,200 crores, largely dominated by defense of almost Rs. 1,400 crores, followed by JSA, aerospace and the traditional business.

items.statement: Standalone margin expanded 140 bps to 28.8% in Q2 on favorable product mix; consolidated H1 EBITDA margin improved 240 bps to 18.6% driven by Indian entity
items.quote: Q2 standalone performance was resilient given the underlying demand conditions. While the top line was flat at 2,247 crores, the margin expanded by 140 basis points to 28.8% reflective of a favorable product mix.

items.statement: Added three new customers in component business in H1; diversified revenue streams across geographies and sectors insulate business; growing market share with strategic customers
items.quote: And, sorry, I forgot to mention that we have added three new customers in the first half of this year in the component business.

items.statement: Management aims to increase stainless steel capacity utilization from 55-60% to 90% technically achievable, expects revenue to grow commensurately but declines formal guidance
items.quote: I would not like to give any formal guidance, but yes, we definitely aim and aspire to increase the capacity utilization to 90% odd and we are taking various measures for it

items.statement: Forward integration project for downstream stainless steel products capped at INR50 crores, to be done in phases within existing premises
items.quote: We have capped our capex plans for it to the extent of INR50 crores because that's the plan so far. We want to do it in phases.

items.statement: Plan to launch stainless steel TMT bars (400 series) in retail segment by Q4 FY25, shifting from B2B to B2C model
items.quote: We are awaiting a few approvals to come in and then I expect the approvals to come in soon. And hopefully in the last quarter, we are expecting to launch the SS TMT bars.

items.statement: Historical EBITDA margins 4-6%, currently 4.23% in Q2; expects 200 bps improvement in better scenario through capacity utilization and product mix
items.quote: In a better scenario, we expect the margins to be up by around 200 basis points. That is what we have historically assumed also in the recent past.

items.statement: Stainless steel TMT bars realization around INR90,000 per ton; current stainless sales realizations INR90,000-95,000 per ton; raw material cost 75-80% of sales
items.quote: The present prices are in the close – in the range of around INR90,000 per ton, but this will obviously depend upon the prices being offered by other customers

items.statement: Domestic stainless steel demand growing due to infrastructure push, solar, defence, auto sectors; import pressure from China affects sentiment but not long products directly
items.quote: Stainless is a growing market. I believe that stainless steel's growth with the per capita consumption that we have in the country, there is a large distance to cover.

items.statement: Chinese oversupply in flat products affecting sentiment; government measures expected to address imports; competition from Sunflag, Shyam Metalics, Jindal Stainless in SS TMT bars
items.quote: Of course, from a global perspective, there is an oversupply scenario in China which is dumping, but that is not much happening in the long product space that we are into.

items.statement: Completed INR114 crores preferential allotment in February 2024 at INR32.25 (non-promoters) and INR55 (promoter preference share conversion); used for debt reduction and working capital
items.quote: We had also successfully completed a fundraise of almost INR114 crores through a preferential allotment sometime in the month of February 2024

items.statement: Cost optimization project achieved direct charging of stainless billets to wire rods, eliminating reheating; first in India, reducing fuel consumption and carbon footprint
items.quote: We probably - we're definitely the first in India and the very few globally to be able to achieve direct charging of stainless-steel billets to wire rods, thereby eliminating an entire process of reheating the stainless-steel billets.

items.statement: API revenue run rate expected at INR85-95 crore per quarter steady state
items.quote: I think we are right now looking, as we had indicated earlier that between an INR85 crores to INR95 crore run rate is what should be a sort of steady state for us.

items.statement: SeQuent standalone PAT growth expected to flow through in FY26
items.quote: And therefore, FY '26 is where most of the incremental SeQuent Scientific Limited November 14, 2024 growth, which would come into margin and EBITDA would flow through straight into the PAT

items.statement: Merger completion expected in 12-15 months
items.quote: We expect this maybe next 12 months -- 12 to 15 months, as I explained earlier, I think it's on track.

items.statement: Viyash reduced capex due to existing free capacity and strong infrastructure
items.quote: As we mentioned earlier also, we have actually strong infrastructure in manufacturing and also we have some free capacity. That's how we were able to reduce capex.

items.statement: SeQuent Q2 gross margin improved 190 bps to 47%; H1 improved 265 bps to 46%
items.quote: We are pleased to report an improvement in our gross margins, which increased by 190 basis points in Q2 rising from 45.1% to 47%.

items.statement: SeQuent Q2 EBITDA margin pre-ESOP improved 452 bps to 12.1%; H1 improved 700 bps to 12.3%
items.quote: EBITDA margins pre -ESOP, which increased by 452 basis points in Q2 from 7.6% in Q2 financial year '24 to 12.1% in Q2 financial year '25.

items.statement: Viyash Q2 EBITDA margin 17.3% up ~3% YoY; H1 EBITDA margin 17.2% up 3.3% YoY
items.quote: Viyash had EBITDA margins of 73% with an improvement of almost 3% year-on-year.

items.statement: Combined entity Q2 EBITDA margin 14.7% up 380 bps YoY; H1 14.6% up 510 bps YoY
items.quote: The combined business had an EBITDA of INR108 crores with 14.7% margins with 380 basis points improvement year-on-year.

items.statement: Price increases implemented in Europe and Turkey; selective targeted price increases driving emerging markets growth
items.quote: We are beginning to slowly get price increases in an inflationary environment.

items.statement: Formulations business growing double digits overall and in most geographies; India formulations up 25% YoY
items.quote: Our formulations business, which is spread over many countries has had a good quarter and a good first half for the fiscal year, growing in double digits overall and in most geographies.

items.statement: Turkey currency stable, government actions predictable; accelerating product launches and price increases
items.quote: We are seeing a more predictable and steady currency scenario in Turkey, and the government actions are also more calibrated and predictable.

items.statement: Viyash rationalized antiretroviral intermediates losing INR150-200 crore topline; shifting to complex/oncology products
items.quote: We lost almost INR150 crores, INR200 crores topline. We downsized that commodity business.

items.statement: Viyash filed 19 products globally in H1 (17 API, 2 FDF); launched 2 products; 25 products in pipeline, 9 validations completed
items.quote: First half, we are able to do 19 products globally. Of course, 17 are API and 2 FDFs we filed all over the world.

items.statement: Merger exceptional costs of INR43.2 million incurred in Q2/H1; more costs expected as process continues
items.quote: For the above merger process, we incurred a cost of INR43.2 million during Q2 and H1 of financial year '25, which are accounted for and disclosed as an exceptional item.

items.statement: ESOP cost accelerated due to final grants and vesting changes; expected to trend down in next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: We have nearly completed all the grants which were there. So it's one, the balance grants, which have been provided in this particular quarter as well as some change in the vesting conditions.

items.statement: Combined net debt/EBITDA improved to 1.4x; SeQuent standalone net debt/EBITDA improved to 2.3x from 3.55x
items.quote: The combined net debt today, net debt -to-EBITDA ratio is 1.4x, and it's going to improve continuously.

items.statement: Revenue potential at full capacity is INR4,000 crores; targeting that run rate in 18 to 24 months
items.quote: I've shared with investors earlier that at full capacity, our revenue potential is in the region of INR4,000 crores, and we will be working in the medium term to head in that direction.

items.statement: Recalibration of brand portfolio to impact revenue for another 4 to 6 months
items.quote: And our recalibration initiatives are likely to impact us for another 4 to 6 months is what we estimate at this point.

items.statement: Major capex cycle is behind the company; focus now on balance sheet and utilization
items.quote: Our major capex cycle is behind us. And our 2 areas of focus now is delivering our balance sheet and enhancing our utilization levels, and those will be our only two primary areas of focus.

items.statement: India revenues to reach just under INR100 crores in FY25; target INR300-400 crores in 2 years
items.quote: And as far as fiscal '25 is concerned, we should see revenues from this jurisdiction stand at between roughly just under INR100 crores.

items.statement: India revenue target INR300-400 crores in 2-year horizon from sub-INR50 crore base in FY24
items.quote: In the 2 -year horizon, we're looking to ramp it up to in the region of INR300 crores to INR400 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin range 18% to 22%; currently swimming in 18% to 20% range
items.quote: Yes, we have always shared with investors that as things stand now and -- things could always change. But the way things stand now, our EBITDA profile should be in that 18% to 22% range, of which we should probably swim in this 18% to 20% range is what I, at this point, feel.

items.statement: Margins can move between 18% and 22% due to product mix and inflationary pressures
items.quote: I want to share with investors that our margins can move between 18% and 22%. So it's possible on account of product mix. It's possible on account of inflationary pressures.

items.statement: Stable demand environment; enhanced U.S. sourcing interest due to China Plus One and Pakistan issues
items.quote: We continue to see a stable demand environment at this point.

items.statement: U.S. retailers showing enhanced interest in shifting sourcing; EU, UK, Middle East, India, Far East leading growth
items.quote: No, I think the industry continues to see some enhanced interest from the U.S. vis -a-vis strategically trying to shift some of their sourcing basis, be it China Plus One or be it certain geopolitical headwinds they're facing vis -a-vis Pakistan, that theme does continue.

items.statement: Branded revenue share down to ~30% from ~50% two years ago; India brands (Himeya, Liv, Atmosphere) to drive growth
items.quote: In context to your other question in terms of how much is our revenue stream from brands, it's approximately -- it hovers between approximately 30% thereabouts at this stage of our revenue mix vis-a-vis private label.

items.statement: Branded share was 40-50% two years ago; now ~30%; margin-neutral churn
items.quote: Two years back, it was, yes, about between 40% and 50%.

items.statement: No tariffs imposed on products in US in last 10-15 years; no current knowledge of new tariffs
items.quote: No, not in the categories that we have operated in recent times. I mean, in the last 10, 15 years since we've been in the space since 2007, we haven't seen any change in tariff structure in the United States.

items.statement: Completed INR400 crore QIP; proceeds to substantially reduce net debt in Q3 FY25; internal initiatives to cut term debt by ~INR200 crores
items.quote: The same was a INR400 crores issue, which we successfully closed and have got some marquee investors on board. As communicated to investors earlier, a substantial portion of the proceeds of the QIP will be used to repay term debt of the company, which will bring down our net debt by a substantial amount.

items.statement: QIP proceeds plus internal initiatives to reduce term debt by ~INR200 crores; repayments reduced over 16-18 months
items.quote: And in addition to the QIP, we are working on a few internal initiatives to bring down term debt by another approximately INR200 crores.

items.statement: Working capital cycles expanded post-COVID; priority to rein them in alongside utilization and balance sheet
items.quote: Our NWC cycles have seen some expansion, and we are working on reining that in. So one of our priorities other than capacity utilization and delivering the balance sheet will also be to correct our working capital cycles, which we are working on.

items.statement: Terry Towel utilization at 67% due to debottlenecking; strong demand expected to lift utilization after product mix shifts
items.quote: So the Terry division, we are working on debottlenecking of certain specs in our plant, which is currently underway. It is because of this reason that the utilization levels are range bound at this point.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 25-30% annually for next couple of years
items.quote: we are expecting a revenue growth of about 25% to 30% every year for the next couple of years.

items.statement: Odisha expansion Phase 1: 45,000 tons rPET granules capacity, INR 450 crore capex, two lines of 22,500 tons each, targeting March 2026 commissioning
items.quote: expansion plan, which we are looking for as a INR450 c rores investment, 45,000 capacity, it is first phase only - Phase one only. So, the entire capacity would be, 45,000 will be operational in one

items.statement: Total capital employed for all projects including working capital estimated at INR 550 crore
items.quote: we are looking for about INR550 crores for all these projects, including the working capital.

items.statement: rPET granules demand strong for next 12 months, may not be able to fulfill all orders
items.quote: We have very good demand for next 12 months and may not be able to accept/ fulfil the orders.

items.statement: Warangal project currently at 22% EBITDA margin, expected to maintain or improve
items.quote: Currently, we are operating at about 22% EBITDA margins at our Warangal project. And so, we are expecting it will improve further from here.

items.statement: rPSF facing difficulty passing on raw material cost increases; focusing on exports and value-added non-woven segments for better pricing
items.quote: in rPSF, we are facing some issues in passing on the increase in raw material prices as I have informed in the opening remarks. So, we are trying to further i mprove our export business as well as our value-added products, particularly from yarn segment to other non-woven technical textile segments, where the pricing is much better than our yarn spinning business

items.statement: Warangal rPET granules capacity utilization at 72%, expected to reach 90%+ by March; RPSF at 80-85% to reach 90% by March; filament yarn to reach 70-75% by March
items.quote: we are already working at about 72% capacity in rPet granules and we expect it to, by March, it will ramp up to 90% plus level. And we are also expecting that our RPSF, we are already 80%-85% and that will also ramp up to 90% by March.

items.statement: FY25 gross revenue guidance of 240-250 crore
items.quote: we remain confident in achieving our stated guidance of gross revenue between 240 to 250 crore for financial year 25.

items.statement: FY26 gross revenue estimate around 300 crore
items.quote: the next year estimated will be around 300 crores gross revenue.

items.statement: FY27 gross revenue potential up to 500 crore with current capacity
items.quote: Now with the same capacity, we can reach up to 500 CR gross which will be there around FY27

items.statement: Small annual capex of 7-8 crore from internal funds for debottlenecking
items.quote: The small Cap ex of 7 -8 crore, which is a continuous process per year , we keep on doing it from our internal fund raising at the moment for any project.

items.statement: CWIP of 4-5 crore for new forging hammer and debottlenecking to be completed by March
items.quote: It is a debottlenecking exercise as well as installing our new hammer in the forging division, so it will be around 4 to 5 crore, which we are already doing for this financial year.

items.statement: Booked for next 6-8 months, running at 75-80% capacity with healthy order book across all segments
items.quote: we are already booked for next 6 to 8 months, we are already having a good order and we are running our business with 75 to 80% capacity, orders are in a good position.

items.statement: Air spring division booked for almost full next financial year at extended 250 coaches/month capacity
items.quote: We are booked for almost the full year for the next financial year.

items.statement: Indian Railways increasing passenger coaches from 6,000 to 10,000 per year and freight wagons from 10-11k to 30k per year for next 3-4 years
items.quote: Indian Railways are already working and keeping increase the capacity of manufacturing their f reight wagons, passenger coaches and locomotives where we are supplying our product and next year onwards, they are already planning to go for 6000 passenger coaches to 10,000 passenger coaches and as well as freight wagons and locomotives

items.statement: FY25 revenue mix: coil spring 80-90 crore, air spring 80-90 crore, forging 60-70 crore
items.quote: The air spring this year, the same 90 :90 for air spring and coil spring and around 60 to 70 for forging.

items.statement: Emergency procurement for LSD coaches driving favorable coil spring pricing with stable raw material costs
items.quote: The Emergency Procurement Associates with this demand has resulted in favorable price realization along with the stable raw material cost.

items.statement: Only three approved air spring sources; next competitor approval takes at least 2 years
items.quote: There are still only three approved sources and I think maybe another one is t here in line to get himself registered and getting registered with railways because these are the safety products required a lot of time prepping and it requires at least two years to get your product approved in the railways after testing field trial and all

items.statement: Client concentration in Indian Railways but no downfall seen for 10-20 years given infrastructure push
items.quote: for next 10 -20 years, we don't see any downfall as far as the railway business are concerned

items.statement: Evaluating takeover of railway-related businesses using cash; due diligence on 1-2 companies at initial stage
items.quote: we are looking for some takeover of some businesses related to railways. The talks are on the very initial basis. Let something happen then we'll definitely reveal to shareholders. We are already working on to multifold our business taking over some companies with our cash

items.statement: Maintains FY25 pre-sales guidance of Rs. 2,000 crores
items.quote: We continue to maintain our guidance of Rs. 2000 crores of pre-sales in the current year.

items.statement: FY25 PAT margin similar to last year ~9%, FY26 12-13%, FY27 20%

This year, again, similar to last year kind of profit margins, last year, I believe we did

items.statement: Key H2 FY25 launches: Amarah Phase-5, Nitara Phase-2, Ekansh Phase-4, Swarang, Amodh Phase-2, Tarang
items.quote: So, we have Amarah Phase-5, we will be launching Phase-2 of Nitara, Ekansh Phase-4, Ashiana Swarang, Ashiana Amodh Phase-2. There is some more in Tarang as well. Of this, the biggest piece would definitely be Ashiana Amarah.

items.quote: Yes, the unit pricing is higher because the launch discounts have been taken off the unit s and I hope to continue to increase pricing as well. So, I don't know when the next price increase will come, but the launch discounts have been taken off. So, effective pricing is done

items.statement: Malhar Phase-3 and Pune pricing to move up; focus on better price over volume
items.quote: Pune, our pricing was a little bit of a concern to us. And Phase-1, 2, we wanted to sell a lot of volume to get the project going. In future phases, we are okay with a little slower sales because you still have time in the project, so cash will anyways come in as when the project will get built, but the project has gotten a sense of financial security now to get through and get going and put that

items.quote: So, first, if we are going to raise money, we will raise money by way of debentures or loans. We have a platform tied up with IFC to invest in our funds and that is Rs. 225 crores platform. We will be utilizing some of that platform for some of our projects. We have also probably taken up approval to raise secured debentures.

items.quote: And yes, I see about 2-4 lakh square foot annual market for Elite Homes in Jaipur for Ashiana to play out. Maybe take another project of 4-5 lakh square foot and then take it from there into the next step and then take it from there would be the ideal way

items.statement: Expect to close FY25 with results similar to FY24
items.quote: we remain optimistic about the outlook for the upcoming quarters and are confident that we will close the year with results similar to FY24.

items.statement: Major growth expected in Q4 FY25 with expansion plans in place
items.quote: the second-half of FY25 looks good, but the major focus or the major growth coming in Q4, Q3 you know I personally feel would be somewhat similar and Q4 is where we're expecting the major growth coming in with our expansion plans being in place.

items.statement: Phase 1 expansion on track to be fully operational by end of December 2024 with 30 tons per day capacity
items.quote: We are on track to have our upgraded facility in Sohna, Haryana fully operational by the end of December 2024. This facility will have a production capacity of approximately 30 tons per day

items.statement: Phase 2 expansion estimated at 100 crores to begin in H2 FY26 for injection molded toys
items.quote: The estimated investment for this phase is about 100 crores and we plan to leverage the benefits of the production linked incentive, the PLI scheme, once it is announced

items.statement: Robust order book supports optimistic growth outlook for toys business
items.quote: our robust order book supports are optimistic growth outlook for the toys business.

items.statement: EBITDA margins at 20-22% across both business domains
items.quote: we are working at about a 20 to 22% EBITDA across the two business domains.

items.statement: Toy business grew 15% quarter on quarter in Q2 FY25
items.quote: For Q2 of FY25, our toy business has grown by approximately 15% quarter on quarter, demonstrating solid momentum.

items.statement: Automotive business declined 13% quarter on quarter in Q2 FY25
items.quote: In quarter two, our auto business declined by approximately 13% quarter on quarter.

items.statement: New partnerships with Vestas and Indo Cool for rotational and blow molded components
items.quote: We are now manufacturing rotational and blow molded components for leading companies such as Vestas and Indo Cool.

items.statement: Phase 2 expansion to include injection molded toys like battery operated cars and role play toys
items.quote: This phase will involve the production of injection molded toys, including battery operated cars and role play toys.

items.statement: Auto business performance tied to commercial vehicle market which has underperformed
items.quote: our automotive business is pretty much in line with how the commercial vehicle market performs because 75 to 80% of our business is plastic fuel tanks largely for the MHCV segment. And if you track the CV market, the CV market has not been doing as well as anticipated

items.quote: That is also ongoing, that is ongoing, but it all depends on the market sentiment. So as of now we have put that on hold, though we may go ahead with that.

items.statement: Inventory at 180 days, targeting 60 days in 2-3 quarters; substantial part is EV inventory
items.quote: as of now it is close to 180 days which should come down to about 60 days.

items.statement: Asset turnover of 3-3.5x expected from new blow molding CapEx
items.quote: the CapEx that we are doing today, which is largely into blow molded products should give us asset turnover ratio about 3 to 3.5x. This is what we're anticipating.

items.statement: Phase 1 expansion to achieve 4X growth in monthly production rate by Q4 FY25
items.quote: we're confident that this will help us achieve a 4X growth in our monthly production rate in the final quarter of this financial year.

items.statement: Air filtration business pilot completed at IIT Delhi, results under analysis
items.quote: we have conducted an extremely successful pilot in IIT Delhi in Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi with these air purifiers being installed in various classrooms and as we speak today, you know the analysis is going on

items.statement: Consolidated revenue growth target of minimum 15% annually
items.quote: our endeavor will be to grow at a minimum of 15% and if we are able to grow even faster, there is nothing stopping us because there is a lot of business tailwind

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target over 10% this year and at least 12% steady state
items.quote: As I said, the steady state, our immediate endeavor is to take the console EBITDA to over 10% pretty quickly, very, very quickly and that should happen this year itself

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin expected to reach close to 13% next financial year
items.quote: So, that will also improve margins. I am presuming that it will help us take the standalone next year to close to 13%.

items.statement: Standalone operating margin to improve by 1% in FY26 and 0.75% in FY27
items.quote: Operating level for standalone entity, I am expecting one percentage up in the next financial year that is FY '26 and one more percentage up in FY '27.

items.statement: Capex of Rs 100 crore planned for FY25, Rs 55 crore incurred, Rs 45 crore remaining
items.quote: I think out of Rs. 100 crore that we planned for this year, I think we have already incurred Rs. 55 odd crores. I think the rest of Rs. 45 crores which will go in will help in taking our capacities up.

items.statement: Bhopal Unit-2 construction to start in Q3 FY25, complete in nine months
items.quote: we are planning to commence work on the second unit, which will happen in this quarter and hopefull y, the work will get comp leted in nine

items.statement: Atraco expanding capacity by 900 machines, work in full swing
items.quote: In fact, in Atraco we are looking at expanding the capacity by another. 900 machines, we have already gone ahead, and that work is going on in full swing.

items.statement: Order book remains strong securing robust near-term prospects
items.quote: The company's order book remains strong, securing robust near-term prospects.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin to improve by 150 bps in second half
items.quote: As far as the consolidated EBITDA is concerned there also I feel that at a consol level we, should be seeing a 1.5% improvement in EBITDA margin. That is 150 that bps.

items.statement: Like-for-like EBITDA margin confident to reach 12%
items.quote: I feel confident about it. When you say like-for-like it is the old Gokaldas organizations without the acquired entities. So, yes, that will happen.

items.statement: US retail sales up 3% year-to-date, brands selling at full price, inventory low, purchasing resumed
items.quote: Retail sales have been resilient and maintained gains year to-date. In fact, if I look at the current year-to-date, retail sales in the US have been +3% over the same period last year.

items.statement: US apparel imports trending up from July, import increase started in Q2
items.quote: So, the quarter from July, we have seen that imports for July, August, and September this period has trended above the same period last year.

items.statement: Focus on high-margin women's fashion and sportswear knits, avoiding low-margin core programs
items.quote: We tend to remain in the highly profitable women's fashion business, etc. We tend to stay away from men's, kids we use, because their the pricing will be sharper.

items.period: Q2 FY25 impact, mitigation from Q4 FY25
items.quote: The other one-off is the Kenyan Shillings going up against US dollar, which was not anticipated by us. That was the last currency we thought would go so strong vis à vis US dollars appreciating from 160 to 128 or 129.

items.statement: BRFL investment increased to Rs 80 crore by October, further capex by BRFL for machinery
items.period: end of Q2 FY25 and October
items.quote: Until the end of Q2, it has been Rs. 60 crores. And I think in October we have infused another Rs. 20 crores. So, it is about Rs. 80 crores.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target around ₹500 crores; FY27 another ~20% addition possible
items.quote: FY '26, like earlier, we had said we will be touching somewhere around ₹500 crores of the top line. And FY '27, another addition of some 20% might be there.

items.statement: 21 upcoming hotels, 16 expected to open in next 4-5 months; 3 openings in next month, 6 pushed to April-June next year
items.quote: Predominantly, most of those rooms should be on stream by the end of this financial year. We have three openings coming up in the next month or so. And there are six hotels that would get pushed into the term between April and that Q1 of next year.

items.statement: Working to post better margin in coming quarters than recent past; consolidated EBITDA grew 2% YoY in Q2 due to Ind AS and cost increases
items.quote: We are working to post better margin in th e coming quarter than what the company has witnessed in the recent past

items.statement: North Goa micro market suffered due to weather in Q2; leisure and managed hotel revenue down YoY; expect benefit of renovations and new properties from April next year
items.quote: In one market, we did suffer in North Goa, it's very public, actually in the papers, if you read, North Goa was actually really suffering as a micro market, and it did affect us year-on-year in quarter two.

items.statement: SEBI final order dropped promoter share sale allegations; penalty on accounting treatment stayed at SAT; contesting appeal
items.quote: we are glad to inform that the SEBI, the final order has come wherein they have removed all the allegations against the promoter sale of share. That has been dropped. But they are stuck to the accounting treatment, okay? So there was a levy of penalty on three of the m anagement as well as the company. We have gone to SAT and we have filed an appeal, and we got a stay from the SAT on that

items.statement: Surat managed property: 188 of 288 keys operational; full completion in ~12 months; phased opening aligned with demand; large banqueting and wedding business
items.quote: We will get to the 288 keys, I would say in about 12 months from now, right? Along with each one of the room opening, the room blocks, I guess, room floors opening, a couple of new facilities are added to it.

items.statement: On track to achieve ₹100 crore PAT by 2026-27; expect to overachieve; revenue growth from new hotels and renovations visible from Q4 FY25
items.quote: Yes, we are in line with what we have said for 2026 and '27. I think it is definitely doable. We will be overachieving that.

items.statement: Expect 15% revenue growth from existing hotels next year from renovation benefits, expansion, and new Mumbai property; combination of ARR, occupancy, F&B growth
items.quote: So overall, I feel that the revenue should go up by next year by 15% of the existing hotels. And of course, we are adding the new hotel, Bombay, that will give us bump up.

items.statement: Refurbishment done in phases without shutting hotels; flagship hotel 24 rooms done, 28 more later; resort adding 28 wooden cottages; Metropole phased renovation
items.quote: We have done 24 rooms have been completed, another 28 rooms will be taken up a little later, because it's early now the season. So probably in March, we'll take up the balance then they'll complete two floors, about 54 rooms -or-so will get completed.

items.statement: Ind AS adjustments non-cash; without Ind AS Q2 PAT would be ₹8.72 crores vs reported ₹7.52 crores; healthy cash profits
items.quote: A perusal of the same will reveal that without Ind AS, our PAT for the quarter would have been ₹8.72 crores instead of ₹7.52 crores as reported by us. This Ind AS adjustments need to be done as per accounting standards. However, they're not cash in nature.

items.statement: FY25 launch pipeline of Rs. 7,000 crore GDV planned
items.quote: As we look ahead, our l aunch pipeline remains robust, with projects representing a total GDV of Rs. 7,000 crore planned for the fiscal year

items.statement: FY25 revenue target of ~Rs. 1,800 crore
items.quote: While the first half has been low on revenue recognition, we are on track to close the year with strong deliveries and revenue of ~Rs. 1,800 crore.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin target of early double digits (11-12%)
items.quote: At least for the financial year, we estimate around 11%, 12% is achievable number.

items.statement: FY25 business development target of Rs. 8,000 crore
items.quote: As far as our BD goals, in a couple of BDs we are in quite advanced stage, and we are pretty confident that this number of Rs. 8,000 crores of our guidance we will meet.

items.statement: FY25 interest cost forecast of Rs. 70-75 crore
items.quote: I see that around Rs. 70 crores, Rs. 75 crores is roughly the number, as you said.

items.statement: H1 FY25 pre-sales value of Rs. 1,481 crore with 1.99 msf volume

items.statement: H1 FY25 gross margin of 23%, EBITDA margin of 7%
items.quote: Moving on to the margins, we recorded 23% gross margins for H1. As higher margins projects get recognized in H, there will be further improvement in margins.
