items.statement: Internal margin targets: outright deals 25%, JV projects 17-18%, redevelopment similar
items.quote: For outright deal we have expectations of around 25% of the margin, for joint v enture projects around 17%, 18% of the margins, redevelopment works around the same margin

items.statement: Sustained strong demand in Pune West/Hinjewadi micro-markets driven by infrastructure
items.quote: We see this demand is sustained and will grow from here onward. There is absolutely no concern over the demand on those, particularly Life Republic itself.

items.statement: 24K luxury segment contributed 30% of H1 pre-sales value vs 12% in FY22
items.quote: 24K luxury segment contributed 30% to the pre-sales by value for H1 reflecting the sustained demand for premium and high-quality residences. This number was 12% for FY22.

items.statement: Year-to-date launched 2.2 msf saleable area across Pune and Mumbai
items.quote: Year-to-date, we have launched projects with nearly 2.2 million square feet in saleable area.

items.statement: Mumbai launch certainty dependent on post-election approvals, Pune launches on schedule
items.quote: Pune portfolio, we have seen a visibility of launching this as per our schedule itself. And maybe in Mumbai portfolio also, we are trying our best to meet the expectations of this launching. However, maybe post-election or maybe by mid of the December, we have to take a call if this pipeline will have any changes.

items.statement: Project-level financing from Marubeni, Motilal Oswal at zero coupon for growth capital
items.quote: is towards the strategy for expanding and growing the business as well as the ongoing projects to be supported with the righ t amount of cash flow securing the TD R and the approvals. And we see that it's coming from Marubeni, the Japanese fund as we ll as a couple of other funds like Motilal Oswal and this is very much at a project strategic financing as well as helping us for the growth of the n

items.statement: Net debt negative Rs. 58 crore as of Sep 30, 2024; H1 operating cash flow Rs. 442 crore
items.quote: Our net debt as on 30th September stands at negative Rs. 58 crores. For H1 FY '25, operating cash flow stood at Rs. 442 crores, underscoring our commitment to financial discipline and operational efficiency.

items.statement: H1 FY25 order intake was INR 1,104 crores, up 17.5% year-on-year.
items.quote: Our orders are INR 1,104 crores, which is 17.5% over and above last year.

items.statement: Order backlog stands at INR 1,389 crores, up 14.3% year-on-year.
items.quote: Order backlog is practically up by 14.3%.

items.statement: H2 FY25 is historically stronger than H1 and expected to be similar this year.
items.quote: H2 is always better. H2 is always better historically for any company, and we are no different because there is a lot of impetus on actually capitalizing it.

items.statement: H1 FY25 gross margin expanded to 39.5%, up 300 basis points year-on-year.
items.quote: This has given us a material margin or a gross margin at 39.5%, which is 3 points over and above corresponding period of last year.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 gross margin was 38.8%, up 240 basis points year-on-year.
items.quote: Material costs are at INR 376 crores, and which has given us a gross margin of 38.8%. Again, this is higher by 2.4 points over corresponding period of last year.

items.statement: RDSS scheme (INR 300,000 crore investment) drives continued business for power distribution.
items.quote: Now one of the major drivers is this RDSS scheme perhaps which you are referring to, which talks about INR300,000 crore lakhs of investment in India. And that certainly gives us impetus to people like us.

items.statement: Emerging segments like solar, EV, storage, and data centres will drive future growth.
items.quote: These are multipole. These are solar, the EV, the storage, the data centres , these are the elements, which were non-existent if you really ask me in 2015, '17. But now what existed in '15, '17, '18, '19 around COVID, that stays, and we are seeing these additional revenues, which actually will drive India future.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 sales mix: Systems 70%, Transactional 19%, Services 11%, Group company 21%.
items.quote: So we have the breakup for Q2: systems is at 70%, transaction 19%, services 11%, and group company is 21%.

items.statement: H1 FY25 order intake mix: Equipment 47%, Projects 13%, Transactional 23%, Services 17%.
items.quote: So the order intake is: equipment is at 47%, projects at 13%, transaction 23%, and services 17%.

items.statement: Kolkata factory commissioning on track for Q1 next year (FY26), with partial start in Q4 FY25.
items.quote: It is actually coming up sometime around the first quarter of next year. That will happen. And it will perhaps start maybe in the last quarter of this year, and we will sort of conclude the other -- installation of other furnaces by Q1 next year.

items.statement: Margin expansion driven by better pricing, product mix, volume leverage, and operational efficiency.
items.quote: Overall, our margin has expanded due to better product mix, order pricing, volume leverage, operational efficiency and also, most importantly, the in-time orders and the sales execution.

items.statement: Exports contribute approximately 14% of total sales.
items.quote: Out of our total sales, we have been 14% of that approximately contributes -- comes from the exports.

items.statement: Intergroup order pipeline indicated at close to INR 125 crores.
items.quote: Intergroup, we do not capture orders as such, but it is -- the indicated number is close to INR125 crores.

items.statement: Channel partner strategy: ~2:1 asset supply ratio in favour of license partners in H1 FY25.
items.quote: Suparna -- under control of Suparna, it would be typically, I would say, maybe 2:1, 2 in favour of license partner. That's what we have done in H1 in terms of number of assets.

items.statement: Revenue growth north of 15% and EBITDA growth north of 20% YoY expected for October-November
items.value: north of 15% revenue, north of 20% EBITDA
items.quote: I would reckon that we should be north of 15%. Now, obviously we have our number in mind, but let me just say our revenue should be north o f 15% and our EBITDA should be north of hopefully 20% YoY

items.quote: I think we are sticking to our guidance that in the next 3 - 3.5 years, we should be debt free, but if we list Fleur before that then we will be debt free that much earlier.

items.statement: Renovation investment of Rs. 250-300 crore over 3 years vs normal Rs. 60-70 crore, peaking in H1 FY25 and H1 FY26
items.quote: we are spending a large amount of money in renovation. As I said, in 3 years, we will spend Rs. 250 - Rs. 300 crore instead of what would normally have been say, Rs. 20 crore a year, instead of Rs. 60 - Rs. 70 crore, we will be spending 3 .5x that.

items.statement: Post-renovation steady state expense expected at 1.5%-1.6% of revenue annually from FY27
items.quote: Post this, renovation expenses are expected to be between 1.5% - 1.6% of revenue on an ongoing basis.

items.statement: Signed 19 new management/franchise contracts adding 1,373 rooms in Q2; pipeline stands at 75 hotels with 5,220 rooms
items.quote: During the quarter, we signed 19 new management and franchise c ontracts which added 1,373 new rooms to our pipeline and operationalized 5 hotels which added 193 rooms to our portfolio. As of 30th September 2024, the inventory for the group stands at 112 operational hotels with 10,318 rooms and a pipeline of 75 hotels with 5,220 rooms

items.statement: Q2 net EBITDA margin 46.1% (+53 bps YoY); excluding extra renovation Rs. 8 crore, margin would be ~49% (+340 bps)

This is translated into a RevPAR of Rs. 4,035 which increased by 7% YoY. In Q2 FY25, if we exclude the increase in renovation expens es of Rs. 8 crores beyond that spent last year. In Q2 our net EBITDA margin would be around 49%, 340 bps increase

items.statement: Aurika Mumbai expected to achieve 60%+ EBITDA margin in H2 FY25
items.quote: See Aurika Bombay, I expect will do EBITDA margin of 60% plus in H2.

items.statement: Keys portfolio targeting Rs. 60 crore EBITDA (~Rs. 6.5 lakh/room) post-stabilization
items.quote: I will give a broad guidance that after we stabilize it, we are looking at an EBITDA of roughly Rs. 60 crores from the portfolio, which means about Rs. 6.5 lakhs a room.

items.statement: Renovation strategy targets 2-year payback: Rs. 250 crore investment over 3 years to yield Rs. 125 crore incremental EBITDA annually
items.quote: Our expectation is that whatever we inv est in renovation, every year we should be able to recover it in 2 years. Put another way, if we over 3 years invest Rs. 250 crore or say Rs. 80 crore a year, we think we will be able to r ecover this after 3 years in incremental EBITDA of Rs. 125 crore each year

items.statement: Demand growth expected to exceed supply growth in next few years with structural tailwinds in branded mid-market hotels
items.quote: with demand growth expected to exceed supply growth in the next few years accompanied by the structural tailwinds in discretionary consumption of branded hotel rooms that India is now starting to witness.

items.statement: Aurika Mumbai targeting one-third each mix: 150-200 rooms crew, 200 retail, 150-200 corporate/MICE
items.quote: We would like retail to be another 200 and corporate meetings, conferences, etc., to be 150 - 200, so roughly one-third each. Some we will achieve earlier, some will take a little longer, but that is, I would say the one year forward perspective.

items.statement: Bangalore underperformance due to renovation shutdowns (10% inventory), IT hiring slowdown, and absence in Outer Ring Road micro-market
items.quote: Bangalore has multiple markets. Today, all big cities have many markets. There is a market in Bangalore alon g Outer Ring Road, which is a fabulous market where we do not have a hotel. There is a market in Whitefield where about a large part of our Lemon Tree Whitefield Hotel was shut for renovation. Then there is a market in Hosur and Electronic City where we have two hotels where the re was a di

items.statement: Fleur Hotels IPO expected within next 2-3 years
items.quote: Well, I would reckon within the next 2-3 years at most.

items.statement: Management fee income guided at Rs. 65-70 crore for FY25 (vs analyst Rs. 55-60 crore estimate)
items.quote: if you say 30% - 35% is the growth in third-party fees, then obviously we will be north of Rs. 65 more likely to be Rs. 70 crores. It is not your numbers, it is closer to 70 because of seasonality.

items.statement: Aurika Mumbai Q3 occupancy expected over 60% (vs ~50% in Q2)
items.quote: as far as Aurika goes in Q3, I do not want to give specific figures, b ut we are doing quite well, but let me say, it will be over 60

items.statement: Management reaffirmed full-year revenue growth guidance of 18% YoY despite H1 shortfall
items.quote: No, I think we will stick to our earlier guidance.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 27-28% by FY27 reiterated; H2 margins expected to be better than H1
items.quote: EBITDA margin, we have spoken 27% to 28% by FY '27. So, I mean, what does H2 look like in terms of EBITDA margin guidance now? Harsh Bansal: Sir, generally, like I mentioned earlier also, the H2 is better than H1, and so our EBITDA numbers will reflect that, sir

items.statement: Phase 2 expansion of Rs 100 crore funded equally by debt and internal accruals planned for immediate future
items.quote: Phase 2 with an outlay of Rs. 100 crores, funded equally through debt and internal accruals, is planned for the immediate future.

items.statement: New facilities for infrastructure, solar and defense planned with efficient CapEx; details before next quarter call
items.quote: The company plans to establish new facilities focusing on infrastructure, solar and defense. These facilities will be designed to operate with very efficient capital expenditure, CapEx, while enabling high volume and value-added production.

items.quote: Additionally, the agreement for the conversion of GP/GC sheets through the CRM complex has been extended until November 2024. items.statement: Q2 FY25 Operating EBITDA margin 23.4%; gross margin 63.7%; PAT margin 11.7%

items.statement: Q2 revenue declined to Rs 150.24 crore from Rs 159.42 crore in Q1 due to customer capital maintenance during monsoon quarter

This decline was primarily due to lower order volumes as our customers undertook capital maintenance, which also prompted us to conduct our own maintenance activities during the quarter.

items.statement: 120,000 ton bar mill decommissioned due to low utilization; 180,000 ton mill to continue at consistent tonnage
items.quote: So, we will continue to operate the 180,000 ton bar mill at the consistent tonnage that has been shown. And the smaller one, we have chosen not to operate it, because operating at a low utilization actually costs us money.

items.statement: Business model agnostic to steel price volatility; Tata Steel supplies HRC for conversion work
items.quote: No, sir. I mean, the short answer is no, sir. Because, we are not on the steel side, and one of the reasons why we are in the sector that we are in is because we are agnostic to steel prices.

items.statement: Dividend policy maintained at 15-20% of PAT
items.quote: Sir, I think we had declared that we will continue to maintain a 15% to 20% dividend on the PAT basis, and we are sticking to that.

items.statement: Expansion focus remains in eastern region; not actively looking beyond for conversion business

items.statement: Industry leaders VIP and Safari billing at unsustainable low prices (₹4,000/set vs ₹12,500); heavy discounting hurting branded play; VIP up for sale.

items.statement: UCB contribution rose from 3% to 10% of H1 revenue; Juicy Couture handbags launch targeted for March; UCB handbags launched with good feedback.
items.quote: Last year, H1 was about ₹127 crores. Instead of ₹127 crores, now we are at ₹140 crores. So out of that ₹140 crores, 10% is UCB now.

items.statement: In advanced discussions with one or two large brands for licensing; could take company to a different orbit.
items.quote: We are in quite advanced stages. And I would not want to comment right now, but with probably one or two brands, we're trying to, if we are able to crack it, it will be like we would have another tick mark on this thing. It will help us take us to a different orbit altogether.

items.statement: EBO same-store sales improved from -10-12% to low single-digit degrowth (-2% to -4%); expects flat by December.
items.quote: By H1, this thing, I think we would be very low-digit degrowth, low single-digit degrowth, minus 2%, minus 3%, minus 4% kinds, which I expect that we should be able to meet it out by December if everything goes well, I think we should be at a flat same sales in our EBOs at least.

items.statement: Store expansion targeting 100 stores in 18-24 months from current 46-47; new store format 800-1,000 sq ft, experimenting with 1,500-2,500 sq ft category killer stores.
items.quote: I can safely confirm that we'll have 100 stores. Now the store count is about 46, 47.

items.statement: Institutional business down 50% YoY in H1 (₹25 cr to ₹12.5 cr) due to non-recurring Shoppers Stop programme; developing institutional channel for recurring revenue.
items.quote: Industry, so H1 itself, if you see, we had done about ₹25-odd crores. And whereas this year in H1, we've done close to ₹12 crores, ₹12.5 crores, so it's down by almost 50%.

items.statement: Full year EBITDA margin expected above 8%
items.quote: And what will be the margins? Can we assume more than 8%? Yes.

items.statement: Freezer plant operational, awaiting certification by mid-December to end-December for commercial billing
items.quote: The freezer plant is already operational. Now we are only waiting for the certification. So that process is going on and we are hoping that all the certifications should be in place by December, mid-December to end December.

items.statement: ODU capacity ramping to 5-6 lakh by end of this year
items.quote: The ramping up of ODU is also underway and I think by the end of this year we should be able to hit the number of 5 to 6 lakh in terms of the capacity for outdoor units.

items.statement: Voltas has booked capacity for next couple of years (FY25-FY27)
items.quote: For the next couple of years from whatever our discussion with them is over the next couple of years we don't see a challenge.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA margin range 8-10%, currently at upper end; compressor EBITDA 7-8%, EV charger controllers 13-15%, freezers 10-12%
items.quote: EBITDA margins that we believe we'll be in is between 8% to 10% is the range of most of our products, blended EBITDA margin that we normally sit in. And we are, I think, on the upper end of that spectrum.

items.statement: FY26 revenue mix target: 50% AC, 25% commercial refrigeration & water dispensers, 15% lighting, 10% components (compressors rising to 20-25% by 2027)
items.quote: So the revenue breakup that we are looking at is about 50% coming from ACs, about 25% coming from commercial refrigeration and water dispensers, about 15% coming from lighting and the remaining 10% will start coming from components, which includes compressors.

items.statement: Commercial refrigeration market growing at 24-25% CAGR; 17-18 lakh freezers sold annually in India
items.quote: So opportunity wise the deep freezer market or the commercial refrigeration market is effectively growing at 24%, 25% CAGR. So the growth rate there is very aggressive. And in India today about freezer specific, about 17 to 18 lakh freezers are sold every year.

items.statement: Preferential share listing delayed due to BSE migration rules conflict; SEBI waiver filed Oct 24, organic migration by Sep 2025 if waiver denied
items.quote: Now, at this point in time, there were two conflicting or contradictory regulations that we kind of got squeezed between. One of them, as I said, is that we were crossing the threshold of %25 crores, so we could not stay on the SME board. The other is that, because we had not completed the mandatory period of three years on the SME board, we could not migrate

items.statement: IDU capacity 600k currently, ramping to 800k by FY26; ODU capacity 400k in H1, targeting 600k and 800k by end FY26; Freezer capacity 400k by next year
items.quote: IDU, last year we had 600. We are ramping it up to 800. ODU, we ramped it up to 400 in HQ1 and we are going to 600k and effectively 800k by end of next year is the plan for ODU to match IDU. And yeah, I mean, those are the two main categories. Freezers, we have to go up to 400,000 next year

items.statement: Compressor IRR target 25% with current investment; rotary compressors 2.5x price and investment of reciprocating; COP reciprocating 1.2-1.9 vs rotary 3+
items.quote: So with the current investment and probably with the vacuum, we are looking at a 25% IRR in our investment. That is point number one. Point number two is that rotary compressors are almost 2.5 times the price of reciprocatory compressors.

items.statement: Working capital days trending down but seasonal spikes expected due to new product ramp-ups
items.quote: But overall if you see the inventory days are improving and we want to continue doing that. So the trend will be downward trend, which means that the number of days will keep reducing. But there will be small spikes here and there because of product.

items.statement: Revenue guidance for FY25 revised down to Rs 570 crore from Rs 600 crore due to pricing pressure
items.quote: Due to the pricing, we won't be able to achieve Rs. 600 crores, but it will definitely be able to achieve or cross Rs. 570 crores.

items.statement: Long-term revenue target for FY27 revised to Rs 850-950 crore from Rs 900-1000 crore due to falling pricing
items.quote: I use say Rs. 900 – 1000 crore for March’27. With pricing falling the figure should be Rs. 850-950 crore.

items.statement: FY25 margin expected around 8%, improvement to 10-11% targeted from Q1 FY26 driven by solar plant savings
items.quote: We should expect around 8%.

items.statement: Solar plant savings of Rs 10 crore expected to improve margins by 2-2.5% from 2026
items.quote: See margins will improve by 2%-2.5% on account of only one reason that is the solar plant. The power cost savings of Rs. 10 crores that itself will lead an 2%-2.5% growth.

items.statement: FY25 capex budget revised to Rs 90 crore including Rs 50 crore for captive solar plant; Rs 35 crore spent in H1, Rs 55 crore more in H2
items.quote: We have revised the capex budget for the current fiscal year to Rs. 90 crores, which includes Rs. 50 crores for Captive Solar Power Plant. We have already incurred Rs. 34 crores in H1 FY25.

items.statement: FY26 capex allocation of Rs 20-30 crore for expansions at Units 6, 7, and 8
items.quote: For FY26, we have allocated Rs. 20-30 crore for expansions at Units 6, 7, and 8.

items.statement: 15.25 MW solar power plant to be live by February-March 2025, expected to reduce annual power costs by Rs 8-10 crore
items.quote: Our 15.25 MW solar power plant, set to be live in February-March 2025, is expected to reduce our annual power costs by approximately Rs. 8-10 crores.

items.statement: Healthy order book with recurring customer base; all manufactured products being sold completely
items.quote: We have a healthy order book. So, once we onboard the customer, the customer remains with us for a long long time. So, it doesn't go.

items.statement: MS Drums volume grew 44% YoY in Q2 FY25; capacity expansion from 30,000 to 50,000 units/month, targeting 90,000 by Q3 FY25
items.quote: MS Drums, this segment has truly outperformed, with an impressive 44% growth in volume year -on-year, leading to a 45% increase in revenue for Q2 FY25.

items.statement: HDPE Drums volume grew 4% YoY in Q2 FY25; polymer production at Unit 7 starting next month, additional capacity at Unit 8 Wada
items.quote: For HDPE Drums, while we are operating at near full optimum capacity, we have achieved a growth of 4% YoY in volume during Q2 FY25.

items.statement: IBC volume grew 7% YoY but impacted by pricing pressure; Unit 7 operating at >50% capacity, new capacity being added
items.quote: The IBC Segment saw a growth of 7% in volume terms, but it was somewhat impacted by pricing pressures due to fluctuating raw material costs and some competition.

items.statement: Raw material price decreased Rs 1.5-2/kg last quarter; buying at Rs 93-94/kg, selling at Rs 120/kg for polymer drums
items.quote: Sir, in the last quarter, it has decreased by like Rs. 1.5-2 per kg.

items.statement: IBC new customer onboarding discounts of Rs 200-400/unit (selling at Rs 7500-7700 vs Rs 8000 standard) temporarily pressuring margins
items.quote: If we are selling IBC, it is at Rs. 8000. So, to onboard, I have given a discount of Rs. 200-400, in IBC.

items.statement: New competitor in IBC segment temporarily impacted margins; management expects competitor to exit or match market rates
items.quote: No one will be able to earn. Either it will stop or it will shut do wn. They will have to come in the market

items.statement: Board approved up to 250 crores CAPEX in two phases; Phase 1 of ~150 crores scheduled for completion by December 2025; 24 crores already incurred
items.quote: The first phase involving an investment of about 150 crores is scheduled for completion by December 2025, while the second phase will be contingent on the success of the initial projects.

items.statement: Phase 1A (crumb rubber + one pyrolysis line) to commence operations in Q4 FY25; Phase 1B (additional pyrolysis line + downstream RCB) and new reclaim rubber lines by December 2025
items.quote: We are starting the crumb rubber facility in one line or one phase of the tire pyrolysis facility, for which commissioning will be completed in this fiscal. Therefore, in Q4 of FY '25, revenues from this phase 1 of phase 1, so I would say phase 1A would be operationalized.

items.statement: Signed definitive term loan up to 15 million euro ECB from Proparco in three phases; Board approved raising up to 150 crores via QIP or other permissible modes subject to approvals
items.quote: To fund these growth projects, the company has signed a definitive term loan of up to 15 million euro to be drawn across three phases through an ECB from Proparco of France.

items.statement: Board approved raising additional up to 150 crores through equity shares or other eligible securities via QIP or other permissible modes subject to necessary approvals
items.quote: The Board has also approved raising an additional up to 150 crores through equity shares or other eligible securities via a qualified institutional placement or other permissible modes subject to necessary approvals to fund not just the above opportunities but others that are also on the horizon.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin 9% consistent with H1 FY24; gross margin pressure from export volume drop, synthetic rubber mix, and freight costs; expects raw material prices to moderate post December-January
items.quote: EBITDA margin for H1 FY '25 was 9%, which is consistent with the margin of H1 FY '24.

items.statement: Implemented modest price increase for reclaim rubber portfolio in Q2; natural rubber prices trending higher due to demand-supply mismatch; synthetic rubber prices elevated with crude oil; freight costs high till October due to Red Sea tensi
items.quote: Amidst these challenges, we have managed to implement a modest price increase for our reclaim rubber portfolio in the quarter under review.

items.statement: Tire manufacturers aggressively setting sustainability targets to integrate recycled materials; recovered carbon black sector entering new growth phase in India, APAC, North America, Europe; non-tire rubber goods commercializing RCB
items.quote: Within the industry of relevance to us, which are the ti re manufacturers, they are actively and aggressively setting sustainability targets to integrate more recycling materials such as reclaim rubber, crumb rubber, biopolymers, and pyrolysis -based polymers into their products and formulations.

items.statement: Non-reclaim rubber volumes grew 36% YoY in Q2 with double-digit EBITDA margin; engineering plastics business driving growth with global approvals and expansion into European markets
items.quote: Our non-reclaim rubber business has shown significant growth with volumes increasing by 36% year-on-year during the quarter accompanied by a double -digit EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Reclaim rubber sales mix ~60% natural rubber / 40% synthetic rubber; export share dropped from >60% to <60% YoY; synthetic rubber reclaim margins under pressure due to elevated prices and freight costs
items.quote: Roughly 60 odd percentage of our volume sales are natural while about 40 has been synthetic. But as far as the current year is concerned, as I said, the exports have dropped from a little more than 60% in the previous year to closer to about little lower than 60%.

items.statement: GCSL (repurposed polyolefin) faces headwinds from delayed EPR regulation enforcement; waiting for April 2025 regulation kick-in for demand pickup; PP sourcing challenges as not in municipal waste streams
items.quote: However, the regulation has been pushed out by one year on account of the lack of readiness by the recycling industry to meet the demand for this material, both from a performance as well as a capacity point of view.

items.statement: EPR credit revenue recognition on cash sale basis; building inventory due to uncertainty on weightages/conversion factors at 70% procurement requirement; will sell credits in next two quarters
items.quote: As a result of that, we have not sold any credits in Q2 of FY '25, and we continue to build an inventory of the credits that we have on the portal.

items.statement: Committed to invest in SPV for 4.3 MW solar plant in Maharashtra under group captive scheme targeting 50% renewable energy sourcing
items.quote: The company has committed to invest in an SPV to establish a 4.3-megawatt solar plant under a group captive power scheme in Maharashtra.

items.statement: Reclaim rubber capacity 72 KTPA at ~90% utilization; new technology line 3.5-5 KTPA at ~30% utilization; advanced piloting with two Indian tire companies, targeting >50-60% utilization by end FY25
items.quote: So, our stated capacity for reclaim rubber is 72,000 tons or 72 KTPA, of which currently we are operating at closer to 90% of utilization.

items.statement: Expects raw material prices to moderate post December-January; non-reclaim rubber targeting >85% utilization by end FY25 to plan next expansion; RCB margins aspirational to be better than reclaim but early to comment
items.quote: I would expect that the raw material prices would sort of start moderating post December-January of this fiscal.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 capex was Rs 83 crore, up from Rs 41 crore YoY and Rs 50.8 crore QoQ
items.quote: The CAPEX for the quarter is Rs. 83 crore whereas it was Rs. 41 crore for the corresponding quarter of the Financial Year 2024 and Rs. 50.8 crore in the previous quarter ended June ‘24.

items.statement: Management expects H2 FY25 to be better than H1 FY25
items.quote: So, now we are hoping that these prices will remain stable for a long period, and the prices of finished products are already bottomed out as per our peers' review. So, we expect that H2’ 25 would be better than H1.

items.statement: Non-ibu export target ~50% of non-ibu revenue in 2-3 years from ~23-24% currently
items.quote: Non-ibu segment, our target is around 50% export collection from non-ibu segment within upcoming 2 to 3 years which is presently around 23 to 24%.

items.statement: New 101-acre land acquired; regulatory approvals take 6-8 quarters; commercialization not before FY26; capex amount not yet finalized
items.quote: have just gotten possession of the land and just went to approval, which usually took 6 to 8 quarters in getting all regulatory approvals. So, we can't expect commercialization until FY’26. After that, it will be commercialized. Amit Agicha: What is the CAPEX involved? Rakesh Mahajan: CAPEX yet to be seen, but we will update in the source to the stock exchanges accordingly

items.statement: US FDA inspection timing uncertain; expected soon but no fixed timeline; will cover additional facilities with filed ANDAs
items.quote: US FDA inspectiong is pending since long. But as a practice, they never intimate us well in advance. They intimate 2-3 days, max to max. So, but we are expecting that it is going to be soon and we also received some intimations that whenever they will be coming, they will be intimating the other facilities of ourselves

items.statement: Acetic acid prices stable last 1-2 quarters; Ethyl acetate prices stable; Delta maintained between the two
items.quote: The prices of acetic acid has been stable since the last 1-2 quarters. In the last quarter, we had some inventory. Ethyl acetate prices are also stable and Delta is being maintained between the two.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 numbers expected to remain more or less same with slight improvement vs Q2
items.quote: We think that numbers will remain more or less same with slight improvement.

items.statement: Previous margin guidance of 13-15% not met due to market volatility; management says impossible to predict one year ahead
items.quote: The guidance which we have provided earlier we are not meeting those guidance. But see, this is beyond our control also. Because what we say, we say considering the situation at that time. When we expect something, we discuss that with all the investors. But this market is very volatile. It is practically getting impossible to talk about what will be happening after one year.

items.statement: Sanofi (global ibuprofen customer) visiting facilities for Paracetamol qualification; hope to secure Paracetamol orders
items.quote: We have just discussed that Sanofi, one of the biggest customers for the ibuprofen, also require Paracetamol. So, they visitour facilities regularly, and when they go through inspection of our plant for Paracetamol, we hope they will start giving some orders for Paracetamol also

items.statement: CWIP Rs 122 crore includes growth capex; Rs 133 crore capex includes some growth capex to be capitalized within FY25
items.quote: Rs. 133 crore of CAPEX includes some growth CAPEX which will be updated within FY’25 results. Same will be updated all of you through stock exchanges

name: S H Kelkar and Company Ltd

items.statement: Full-year revenue expected around Rs 2,100 crore, implying ~14% growth, subject to no major changes
items.quote: I would expect to reach around 2,100 or something like this number, 14% odd for the full year. This is a subject that no major changes happen between now and the end of the year.

items.statement: H2 revenue expected to be better than H1; full-year growth well in excess of 12% midterm CAGR target
items.quote: Expect our sales to be better than 12% for the full year. Whether it is 15% in the second half, a little bit more or less, in the full-year basis we will be well in excess of our 12% target.

items.statement: Gross margin expectation for H2 around 40-45% as reported in H1, but cautious on raw material availability in Q4/Q1 next year
items.quote: So, we are cautious, I would say that our gross margin expectation is still around the 40%-45% that we have reported for the first half.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin for H2 expected similar to H1 at ~16.8%, with additional Rs 10-12 crore cost for Creative Centres
items.quote: So, I think H2 will be similar in terms of percentage. I just want to note or put on record that we have now the full cost of Germany and America Creative Centres which has come on board.

items.statement: H2 FY25 capex ~Rs 50 crore; H1 FY26 another ~Rs 50 crore; incremental capex after insurance ~Rs 60 crore; Rs 45-50 crore per new factory in Europe over next 2-3 years
items.quote: So, I think in the second half, we would have roughly around Rs. 50 crore and the first half next year, another Rs. 50 crore of CAPEX, out of which almost Rs. 100 odd crore would be the reinstatement of the Vashivali factory itself.

items.statement: Global MNC account orders secured for FY25 and execution well underway, trending as expected
items.quote: On our global MNC account, we are pleased to report t hat execution of orders is secured for FY25 and is well underway. This continues to gain momentum

items.statement: Acute shortages expected in Q4/Q1 next year for key natural oils (orange, patchouli, vetiver ~15% of purchase basket); will negotiate price pass-through with customers by Feb-Mar
items.quote: there are few natural oils which are currently in difficult scenario due to bad weather conditions or crop failures in different parts of the world. So , specifically products like orange oil, patchouli oil, vetiver oil these are the key components, which is roughly I would say 15% of our purchase basket

items.statement: Domestic large FMCG customers soft; strong momentum in small, mid-sized customers and new accounts; H2 seasonally stronger
items.quote: While domestic demand for large customers remains soft, we are encouraged by strong momentum across our small, mid-sized customers and new accounts. Having delivered a healthy performance in H1, we anticipate an even better H2.

items.statement: Q2 gross margin muted due to Rs 25-30 crore lower-margin backlog carried from Q1 post-fire; H1 composite margin representative of business
items.quote: Just to explain that more, I think the 1st Quarter of this year, due to the fire incident, we prioritized orders and execution towards the higher margin products and some of the lower margin or some of the backlog went into the 2nd Quarter.

items.statement: Potential raw material availability and pricing issues in Q4 FY25/Q1 FY26; US administration changes may impact trade; Europe tariff risk on gross margins
items.quote: However, there are some raw materials where acute shortages are expected in the 4th Quarter or 1st Quarter of next year. As of now, we are adequately covered with the stocks in hand, but given the strong growth momentum we are seeing, we may have certain raw material pricing or raw material availability issues in the last quarter.

items.statement: Insurance payout expected Dec-Jan; inventory claim first, then CAPEX reimbursement on reinstatement basis; substantial payments to start
items.quote: We expect by December -January substantial payments to start to come in. The plant and machinery CAPEX reinstatement will only happen once we have rebuilt the plant. So, that is a reimbursement of the insurance amount.

items.statement: Vanavate factory expected Q4 FY25 (calendar Q1); Vashivali rebuild 9-10 months more; Mulund closure post-Vashivali; Europe at 75-80% utilization, new factory 18-20 months
items.quote: So, the new factory in Vanavate is expected to come up in the 1st Quarter calendar next year, so 4th Quarter. Vashivali which is the rebuild of the factory will still take another 9 months to 10 months before it is rebuilt.

items.statement: Creative Development Centres in Germany (launched June) and Manchester (early next year) add recurring Rs 20 crore/year OPEX; revenues to start next year
items.quote: Those are all employee and OPEX costs. So, there is a recurring Rs. 20 crore order per annum.

items.quote: Currently we are at an order book of INR 6,546 Crore; we expect a multifold increase in the construction order book going forward as Adani portfolio of companies are engaged in infrastructure development across ports, airports, data centers, realty, etc.

items.statement: Order inflow guidance for FY25 maintained at INR 3,500-4,000 Crore.
items.quote: Yes. items.statement: Targeting to maintain company-level EBITDA margin at 10% going forward.

So today also what we have agreed and what we are aiming for future when we are working with Adani or whether we are working with other groups or whether we are working at government level, we will try and stick to maintain our EBITDA at 10%.

items.quote: INR232 crores approximately

items.statement: Adani Portfolio plans USD 100 billion capex over the next decade.
items.quote: Adani Portfolio of Companies is looking to invest USD 100bn as capex over the course of next decade.

items.statement: Bidding for INR 1,000 Crore projects each at Ahmedabad and Mumbai airports, INR 500 Crore at Kandla, plus Dharavi and data centre opportunities.
items.quote: The first and the foremost thing we have already said you, we are already bidding for about INR1,000 crores projects, INR1,000 crores projects at the Ahmedabad airport, INR1,000 plus crores at Mumbai Airport, and already INR500 crores projects in Kandla.

items.statement: Focus on precast technology; operating three precast plants (Ahmedabad, Mundra, Mumbai) to accelerate delivery.
items.quote: They are already installing three Precast Plants, one in Mundra, one in Mumbai, and one, we are already having under.

items.statement: Private contracts with Adani use base rates for major materials (cement, steel), insulating PSP from material cost inflation risk seen in government projects like UP.
items.quote: Here the base prices of the cement or steel, whatever it is, we have added today that will be paid off, whatever, whether it is minus or plus. What is going to be fixed is my overheads and what is going to be fixed is my margin and what is going to be fixed is my cost.

items.quote: As per the arrangement, Adani Infra to acquire up to 30.07% stake from the founder promoter. Post the open offer for 26%; both the companies will maintain equal equity of the company. items.quote: As we are working on L&T order, the present facility has already been doubled. So, after that L&T order is over in June, we have that space available, we simply have to invest in mould.

About INR1,000 plus-crores projects we are discussing at Mumbai Airport. And about I think INR300 plus-crores projects we are discussing at Dharavi, which is going to be the first project of rehabilitation.

items.statement: Related party transaction approvals required only if order value exceeds threshold; not needed currently.
items.quote: So if at all it is required in the future, if the transaction value is more than the threshold which I will be giving year-on-year, we'll be going ahead with this. As of now, there's no need to take this.

items.statement: Promoter proceeds from stake sale (INR 685 Cr) for personal use; no company-level fund raise indicated.
items.quote: Why are you asking about that money today. Even i'm not sure what I'll be doing of that money.

items.statement: Operational control remains 100% with existing management (PS Patel as CMD & CEO); Adani to nominate two board members only.
items.quote: We have clearly mentioned that the operational part 100% remains with PS Patel, being Managing Director, Chairman and CEO till today. items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance of INR3,300 crores including INR2,700 crores from core operations and INR600 crores from subsidiaries
items.quote: Our FY25 revenue guidance stands at INR3,300 crores which includes INR2,700 crores from our core operations and an additional INR600 crores from our subsidiaries which we acquired recently.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance of INR6,300 crores with INR5,000 crores from parent and INR1,300 crores from subsidiaries
items.quote: Already we have given a blended of INR3,300 crores this year and FY26 is INR6,300 crores. So, INR1,300 crores from subsidiaries and INR5,000 from the parent companies.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 blended revenue expectation of INR1,000 crores with INR700-750 crores from parent and INR150-350 crores from subsidiaries
items.quote: So, we are expecting a totally blended INR1,000 crores revenue in the next quarter, from the parent company INR700-INR750 crores what we are going by the run rate and from the subsidiary INR150 crores-INR350 crores.

items.statement: Target gross margin of 7-8% through optimized product mix and exports, long-term EBITDA margin of 5-5.5%
items.quote: We aim to achieve 7% to 8% gross margin through an optimized product mix and export, while maintaining a long-term EBITDA margin of 5% to 5.5%.

items.statement: PAT margin target of 3.5% for FY25 and 4% for FY26-27 driven by interest cost reduction from gold metal loans
items.quote: So, we can give a guidance of 3.5%. But going forward for FY '26- '27, we will target 4%, 100% will go up to 4%.

items.statement: Raised INR270 crores for product portfolio expansion in 18 carat gold and diamond jewellery, capital infusion into subsidiaries Star Mangalsutra and Sparkling Chains
items.quote: Additionally, I am excited to announce a significant milestone in our company's journey as we have successfully raised INR270 crores. This investment will be strategically allocated across broadening our product portfolio with expanded offerings in 18 carat gold and diamond jewellery to align with evolving customer preferences.

items.statement: Strong wedding season demand with 25% more weddings this year, gold prices down 5% from 81,000 to 76,000 boosting demand
items.quote: 100% as all our client has given the outlook is very good for the wedding season as rates are also down by 5% of gold. Rates from 81,000, has come down to 76,000. So, it is helping to boost the season already.

items.statement: Increasing studded and 18 carat jewellery mix, planning Moissanite and lab-grown diamond jewellery for FY25-26

items.statement: Next quarter blended revenue expectation of INR1,000 crores with parent at INR700-750 crores and subsidiaries at INR150-350 crores
items.quote: So, we are expecting a totally blended INR1,000 crores revenue in the next quarter, from the parent company INR700-INR750 crores what we are going by the run rate and from the subsidiary INR150 crores-INR350 crores.

items.statement: Volume guidance of 375-400 kgs per month by end of FY25, 550-600 kgs per month by FY26, and 750 kgs per month by FY27
items.quote: So, we are at 350 kgs per month run rate in H1 and we are having [inaudible] 375 kgs, 400 kgs per month till end of the year. And by FY27, we are expecting to go to 750 kgs per month.

items.statement: Targeting 7-8% gross margin through optimized product mix and exports, long-term EBITDA margin of 5-5.5%
items.quote: We aim to achieve 7% to 8% gross margin through an optimized product mix and export, while maintaining a long-term EBITDA margin of 5% to 5.5%.

items.statement: Conservative gross margin expectation of 6.5% and EBITDA margin of 5-5.5% for FY25
items.quote: So, gross margin we are expecting to be 6.5% conservatively and EBITDA margin is 5% to 5.5%.

items.statement: PAT margin target of 3.5% for FY25 and 4% for FY26-27 through interest cost reduction and product mix improvement
items.quote: So, we are targeting to 3.5% by reducing our interest cost. We got little bit later for GML because of the bank policies and all, but I think we will be at 50%-60% of GML by December quarter and 80% by March quarter.

items.statement: Raised INR270 crores to broaden product portfolio in 18 carat gold and diamond jewellery, infuse capital into subsidiaries, enhance organizational capacity, and target international markets
items.quote: Additionally, I am excited to announce a significant milestone in our company's journey as we have successfully raised INR270 crores. This investment will be strategically allocated across broadening our product portfolio with expanded offerings in 18 carat gold and diamond jewellery to align with evolving customer preferences.

items.statement: Gold metal loan usage increased from 10% to 25% currently, targeting 50-60% by December quarter and 80-85% eventually at blended cost of 2.75-3%
items.quote: So,. we were last quarter at 10%. We have moved approximately to 20%-22%. So, this quarter, we are hardly trying because some banks have other policies. So, I think by December quarter, we will be at 50%-60%.

items.statement: Strong wedding season demand with 25% more weddings this year, gold prices down 5% from 81,000 to 76,000 boosting demand
items.quote: 100% as all our client has given the outlook is very good for the wedding season as rates are also down by 5% of gold. Rates from 81,000, has come down to 76,000. So, it is helping to boost the season already.

items.statement: Increasing studded and 18 carat jewellery mix, planning Moissanite jewellery for FY25 and exploring lab-grown diamonds post March quarter
items.quote: Yes studded and 18 Carat we are increasing, and we have infused the amount for 18 Carat and Studded only. So, in this December quarter also you will see that our Studded and 18 Carat is increasing.

items.statement: Inventory fully hedged on MCX daily, gold metal loan hedging policy ensures no gain/loss from gold price fluctuations
items.quote: Yes. So, already our inventory is totally hedged in the MCX, which is available in India to hedge. So, our inventory is already hedged, and we hedge every sale and purchase on a daily basis in the hedging platform MCX.

items.statement: Export target of 12-13% of revenue this year and 15% next year, focusing on Middle East, UAE, Singapore, Malaysia with gross margins of 6-7%
items.quote: So, I think this year we will be at 12%-13% and next year we will be at 15%.

items.statement: Subsidiary capacity utilization at 30-33%, targeting 70-80% with capital infusion and new verticals
items.quote: Subsidiary companies is about 30%-33% utilization both the subsidiaries.

items.statement: Working capital cycle at 75 days, receivables temporarily higher due to high gold prices but expected to normalize in coming quarters
items.quote: So, we are at a total of working capital cycle of 75 days approximately.

items.statement: No dividend for 1-2 years until cash flow positive and debt-free by FY26/27, focusing on profit retention
items.quote: So, we are not going for dividend for 1-2 years, whenever we are cash flow positive and lets say by FY26/27 post that. So, right now we are 1 year, or 2 years and we are not thinking about them.

items.statement: Revenue CAGR of 40% to 50% over next three to five years with EBITDA margins sustained at 23% to 25%
items.quote: we look to grow the Company until next three to five years with the CAG R revenue of about 40% to 50% and this growth will also sustain the EBITDA margins in the range of 23% to 25

items.statement: Order book stands at ₹206 crores as of 30th September
items.quote: In the H1FY'25, we have and today as on 30th September, the order book is at ₹206 crores.

items.statement: Advanced Rail Control had an order book of ₹140 crores at acquisition, expected to be completed in 16 to 18 months
items.quote: The company had an order book of ₹140 crores in pending. So we hope that we will be completing in next 16 to 18 months approximately.

items.statement: EBITDA margins increased by 248 basis points in H1 FY25
items.quote: And the EBITDA margins have also increased by 248 basis points.

items.statement: Annual capex may exceed ₹2-5 crores; will add facilities as required
items.quote: May be more than that.

items.statement: Locomotive products from Advanced Rail Control target addressable market of ₹2,000-2,500 crores over next five to six years
items.quote: From the locomotive products, we said that the target addressable market is about ₹2.5 thousand crores for the next five to six years and that is going to contribute maximum.

items.statement: Kavach approval process ongoing with multiple milestones; SIL 4 certification in progress
items.quote: First, the product has to be developed, then the capacity assessment has to happen. Then the product feasibility has to be checked and approved by RDSO, then it goes for a field trial. And parallelly, the SIL 4 certification, which is the highest level of safety certification globally for any such public usage product has to happen.

items.statement: Preferential funds used for working capital, reducing Advanced Rail leverage, capex, and further acquisitions
items.quote: It's a mix of all. It's also to fund the working capital requirement. It's also to reduce leverage of Advanced Rail in terms of loans. It is also to further invest on Capex and further acquisitions and so it's a mix of all.

items.statement: Margins expected to improve further as company transitions from product to solutions provider
items.quote: When you move from a product company to a solutions company, your margin tends to improve slightly. So we are hoping that it will further improve.

items.statement: ROCE declined to 25-28% due to acquisitions and new share issue; expected to improve going forward
items.quote: So, I think, largely it is because of contribution for the acquisitions and we're significantly improving and going forward. We will see a better ratios in coming years.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin was approximately 18.5%
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR19 crores with a margin of approximately 18.5%.

items.statement: European demand weak due to macro and geopolitical factors; global capacity exceeds demand pressuring prices and margins
items.quote: Demand in Europe, the company's second largest market, has been weak due to macroeconomic and geopolitical factors. Additionally, production capacities globally currently exceed demand, putting a pressure on price and margins.

items.statement: Chinese insoluble sulphur prices near cost break-even; limited scope for further price decline
items.quote: Globally, I believe that the price of insoluble sulphur, as far as China is concerned, is at a level where there is a very little scope of further correction.

items.statement: Long-term demand forecast 2-3% growth with focus on India; European demand decline has already happened
items.quote: as far as demand is concerned, I think the decline which needed to happen, which we anticipated to happen because of the geopolitical situation and the economic situation in Europe has happened. We are looking at growth in India. So, I mean, if you loo k at the long -term forecast, it still stays 2% to 3% with the focus of growth being India

items.statement: Capacity utilization below optimum; new 5,000 ton capacity remains unutilized; sales tonnage up 10-12% YoY
items.quote: As far as new capacities are concerned our capacity utilization is below optimum level, and therefore, there is still room for growth within the existing capacity. Or, in other terms, the additional capacities still remain unutilized.

items.statement: Three major factors affecting margins: international pricing from China capacity, dumping in India, and international freight rates
items.quote: So, price, international pricing, because of capacities in China, is affecting our margin. The dumping of material into India is affecting our margins severely. And international freights are affecting our margins. These are the three major factors which are affecting our margins.

items.statement: No formal guidance given; expect freight cost tailwinds in H2 FY25; anti-dumping duty unlikely to impact H2
items.quote: We normally do not give guidance, but as I have said, that we are seeing tailwinds as far as international freights are concerned. So, that should help us. Secondly, okay, you are talking about H2, then anti -dumping is something which might not happen by then.

items.statement: Global capacity utilization estimated around 70%; no capacity additions in last 1.5 years
items.quote: However, in our estimates, the global capacity utilisation would be around 70%. Saket Kapoor: The global capacity? Anurag Jain: Yeah, and in the last 2 years, there has not been any capacity addition. There were rapid capacity additions before that, but not in the last 1.5 year

items.statement: Coating oil stable with downward trend last 3-4 months; sulphur prices uptick in last 3-4 months after previous decline
items.quote: So, in the last 3, 4 months, coating oil has been stable with a downward trend. As far as Sulphur is concerned, we have seen an uptick in the Sulphur prices in the last 3, 4 months. Before that, it was coming down, but it has started going up, and it's currently there is an uptick in Sulphur prices.

items.statement: Surplus cash to be invested in standard treasury instruments; priority to reduce debt and working capital drawdown
items.quote: They will be invested in standard treasury instruments. As of now, we do not really have any surplus funds. So, as and when they have it, the first thing will be to reduce debt and reduce the drawdown of the working capital limit. And after that, when we have it, we will put it judiciously in things like debt funds and all of those things.

items.statement: Historically sustainable margin around 25%; return to that level will take time as freight, Europe geopolitics, and China capacity issues resolve
items.quote: See, currently, the markets, the margins are depressed because of three reasons. And because of higher international freight rates, geopolitical situation in Europe, which is a significant market for us, higher capacities in China. Once these are resolved to a certain extent, then we can look at margins returning to the earlier level, but it will take some time.

items.statement: H2 FY25 EBITDA expected to be more than 100% of full-year EBITDA based on past three-year trend
items.quote: For the last 3 years, EBITDA for H2 is more than 100% against the total EBITDA for the financial year.

items.statement: Biobased specialty chemicals demand stronger in FY25 with higher demand expected in H2 2025
items.quote: In terms of the biobased specialty chemicals chemical business is stronger in this financial year and in some of the chemicals that we operate in, we are expecting to see a higher demand in H2 of 2025 itself.

items.statement: Capacity increases for biobased chemicals visible from Q4 2025 onwards
items.quote: Some of these increases will be immediately seen in certain capacity expansions beginning from Q4 2025, and then we will also further expand to increase capacities of more biobased chemicals going forward.

items.statement: Grain-based ethanol capacity investment planned; capital expenditure details to be shared next quarter
items.quote: Right now, we are working on the capital expenditure required for the grain-based ethanol and we would be able to give an much stronger update in the next quarter call.

items.statement: Bid for over 10 crore litres of ethanol; allotted 7.5 crore litres plus from OMCs
items.quote: So, the total allotted quantity from the OMC is 7.5 crores litres plus. So, on 5.4 crores for the juice and for 2.5 crores for B-Heavy.

items.statement: Biobased specialty chemicals have very strong gross margins
items.quote: I just would like to say that the margins across the biobased specialty chemicals are quite strong. In the exact number, I would like to not be able to give immediately, but the margin numbers for the biobased specialty chemicals are a very strong gross margin.

items.statement: Strong demand seen in fragrances for 1,3-butylene glycol and newly launched ethyl vinyl ether
items.quote: We are definitely seeing strong demand in sectors such as fragrances, where we are making products such as 1,3-butylene glycol that we make and we also launched our product, ethyl vinyl ether a couple of months ago, which is used primarily as a feedstock for agrochemicals and also in fragrances.

items.statement: Grain-based ethanol facility planned to mitigate climate risk and policy disruptions from poor monsoons
items.quote: The strategy of the company is to invest in grain-based ethanol in the future so that it gives the company a dual feedstock to produce ethanol, which will help mitigate climate risk, such as what happened in the poor monsoons of 2023.

items.statement: IPO proceeds of Rs. 240 crores allocated for debt repayment to reduce borrowing costs and improve debt-equity ratio
items.quote: We intend to allocate Rs. 240 crores from the net proceeds for the full or partial repayment or prepayment of certain company borrowings. The repayment is aimed at reducing our outstanding debt and servicing costs, improving our debt equity ratio, and allowing us to channel our internal accruals now towards business growth and expansion.

items.statement: Annual R&D expense around Rs. 10-12 crores
items.quote: Annually, Around Rs. 10 crores to Rs. 12 crores of the expense we incurred on the R&D.

items.statement: Sugarcane crushing commenced about 10 days ago for the current season
items.quote: We are very happy to tell you that the factory has started about 10 days ago. So, the crushing season has commenced.

items.statement: Sugarcane price paid at Rs. 3000 per ton ex-field
items.quote: I think the factory is paying a price of Rs. 3000 per ton ex-field for sugarcane in where we operate.

items.statement: 2G ethanol demonstration plant planned at Sameerwadi with Rs. 150 million grant from Centre for Higher Technology
items.quote: We are planning a demonstration plant of our 2G ethanol production using bagasse at Sameerwadi, a significant milestone backed by a grant of Rs. 150 million from the Centre for Higher Technology under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.

items.statement: Cancer drug molecule currently in Phase 1 safety trials; updates to be shared when available
items.quote: Currently that molecule is undergoing trials in safety. And we will definitely share updates as and when they become available, Currently that molecule is under trials in phase one for safety.

items.statement: Ethanol produced from sugarcane and grain is the same for blending program (C2H5OH)
items.quote: I think as far as the ethanol blending program is concerned, it is the same for the two ethanol. It is both the same C2H5OH and so for the ethanol blending program it is the same.

items.statement: Management revised sales plan from 30-35% growth to 16% growth for the year
items.quote: We revised, I think, in mid of this year saying that we will not grow at 30 to 35%. We'll grow at 16%.

items.statement: Management cannot provide revised H2 guidance until customer forecasts arrive before Christmas
items.quote: Right now, the real things are not come, but to very honest, we are already planning visit to Europe to have a face to face meeting and discussions to get a realistic numbers based upon that, we will definitely be able to give more crisp information.

items.statement: Received new nomination from BMW for drive train parts for Electric Sports car with commercial production expected from 2026
items.quote: So we have got one more nomination from a from a big German player and it's BMW. So we have bought a new nomination from supply of drive train parts project, Electric Sports car. Right now, and this is a very big project which we have brought the nomination from BMW.

items.statement: Project Titan first sample phase completed successfully in less than six months; second trial phase scheduled Feb 2025; mass production expected August 2026
items.quote: So basically, as we have said that the gestation period for these products is very high, takes about lot of cycling and lot of work prototypes and all which happens. So we have completed a supplier for sample and they have approved our samples already. In less than six months, which in our opinion is a very big achievement and which means the whatever the initial quality standards which was set by

items.statement: Signed agreement with UP government to invest 250 crores by November 2026; already invested ~150 crores; subsidy claimable after 200 crores investment
items.quote: I think we already announced in one of our investors call and we disclose on our public domain also that we have signed agreement with government of up wherein we are to invest total of 250 Crores from November 2022 until November 2026, they are given us a four years window. So, we have already signed 250 crores of investment into that Government of UP already approved our investment subsidy and t

items.statement: Domestic margins slightly lower than exports but balanced by faster receivables (30 days vs 75-80 days); company maintains premium positioning
items.quote: You are right, domestic margins have been very competitive, but then you get better receivable management, you get money pretty fast. So somewhere it balances out all the stuff

items.statement: Steel price pass-through achieved on full year basis; raw material consumption impact improved in Q2 but H1 still down 0.64%
items.quote: However, since we have been able to pass on the steel on a full year number, this will add to our this will help us in better margins in the on a full year basis.

items.statement: European automotive sector facing headwinds: high Chinese EV competition, slow EV adoption, high energy costs, inventory corrections; EU car registrations declined 12-13% for 3-4 months but grew 1.1% in October
items.quote: If we look at new EU car registrations? OK, talk in for the continuous decline for last 3-4 months and decline as. Is 12-13% also in the month of October, the new EU car registrations have. Have got a growth of modest growth of 1.1%, which in our opinion have started now signaling that the market should start picking up from there.

items.statement: Green shoots appearing: ATV/snowmobile demand picking up due to heavy snow predictions; November forecasts improved
items.quote: There is a big prediction that northern Hemisphere is going to have very, very hot spring time, very heavy snow and in fact today one of your seen in Canada your this lots of snow storm that started coming in even in North India in Gulmarg you got 4 feet of snow in October. Due to this, snowmobile business has started picking up. So now I'll say the green shoots has started coming

items.statement: Shift from predominantly 2-wheeler to passenger vehicles and commercial vehicles; passenger car share increasing with BMW and Project Titan nominations
items.quote: Earlier we used to be predominantly supply of products for two Wheelers. But now we are doing our share of passenger vehicles and commercial vehicles are increasing, which are bigger products which have a little more manufacturing period and all.

items.statement: High customer concentration risk mitigated by platform-specific agreements with +/-20% to +/-40% volume commitments; single-source supplier for each part
items.quote: So whatever number that produces. We have to supply to them and we cannot say no also. 'Cause when they give the business, they always take from us a commitment plus -20%. Some customer this customer which ordered this BMW project this time since this electric car they are also not knowing which way wind will go. They are taking commitment from US plus 40%. And of course, -40 also, they say we do

items.statement: Geopolitical risks: Red Sea crisis extended shipment periods by 40-45 days; China trade barriers (15% duty); Vietnam 45% duty; India-EU FTA under negotiation
items.quote: So basically, if you were not at like the Red Sea crisis, which at and all that the overall shipment levels have gone up and it has persisted for a long period of time in order not that is something which has impacted because first of all ours. Shipment periods have also gone up. As high as by 40-45 days.

items.statement: Board approved NSE listing application at final stages; will improve investor access and transparency
items.quote: We have decided to get a stock listed on NSE. We have already bought approval from board of Directors. Our application is almost at final stages right now. At NSE So hopefully we should be able to share the good news.

items.statement: H1 FY25 capex 22.28 crores (22% of budget) vs 57 crores H1 FY24; postponed investments to next year
items.quote: In addition to FIXED Asset in half year this year is close to about 22.28. Which is just 22% as compared to almost close to 57 crores of investments, which we had done last year.

items.statement: Registered ESG under Dun & Bradstreet per global standards; ESG compliance helped win BMW nomination
items.quote: We were the only company and there So yeah, this is all and somebody asked that why JJ not joined the CITI bank. Why you're in RACL? I see a Jitender. Jain is leading our compliance and our ESG to work. So, it would have never gotten to work on this project in the back.

items.statement: New plant with land and construction to cost INR 20-21 crores; INR 11 crores already utilized, INR 9 crores balance.
items.quote: The new land with construction and bit capex and all, it should roughly cost around INR 20 crores-INR21 crores.

items.statement: One unit to shift completely by March or April 2025; full transition to new facility by September 30, 2025.
items.quote: one of the units should shift completely and become operational by March or April. Karthikeyan: Okay. I'm getting you. Nishant Garg: And then another 3 months for the shifting of second unit. So maximum by September 30th, next year the entire plant should have been the older both units should have been shut down with no machine over

items.statement: Proceeds from sale of existing land estimated at INR 30 crores; INR 4-5 crores earmarked for debt reduction.
items.quote: Approximately you can say INR30 crores.

items.statement: Internal target of 15-20% top-line growth annually, driven by volume growth assuming stable steel prices.
items.quote: Our target annually for the growth is somewhere between 15% to 20% in the top line that is our internal target, that we target that every year we target 20%, but we consider it decent if in our kind of nature of industry it happens between somewhere between 15% to 20%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 8.95% in H1 FY25; management expects significant improvement once stainless steel volume reaches 40% mix but declines to quantify.
items.quote: It should be very much incremental, but I won't be able to comment on that now. It should be far better than what it is now, but now it is too soon to comment on that.

items.statement: Customer demand currently at 60-70% of normal levels; volume grew 7-8% in H1 FY25 despite demand slump.
items.quote: But the overall demand approximately from our customers, those were existing plus the new customers. They have only about 60% to 70% demand of what it used to be.

items.statement: Registered with Ordnance Factory Board; commenced supplies to HAL (INR ~10 lakhs) and NTPC; tender pipeline described as huge.
items.quote: We have already served last month to HAL and this month we have supplied to NTPC, our first order. So the potential is huge. Right now also we are filling up multiple tenders with some of smaller quantities and some of huge quantities.

items.statement: Steel prices down 7-8% YoY, causing ~3% revenue decline despite higher volumes.
items.quote: The steel prices are at rock bottom. We expected last year that that was the rock bottom. But this year it has gone down by approximately 7%-8% vis-a-vis last year average pricing.

items.statement: Projected 30% CAGR in top line revenue and sustainable PAT margin of 9% over next 3 years
items.quote: Looking ahead, Aztec remains optimistic with a projected of 30% CAGR in top line revenue and a sustainable PAT margin of 9% over the next 3 years.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to grow from 13.01% to 14.5% over next 3 years driven by higher consumable use and backward integration
items.quote: Additionally, we expect our EBITDA margin to grow from 13.01% to 14.5% over the next 3 years, driven by the higher consumable uses and backward integration.

items.statement: Target to produce 60-80% of subparts domestically within next 3 to 5 years
items.quote: Our expected future manufacturing plants include a goal to produce 60-80% of subparts domestically within the next 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: New 11,028 sqm assembly unit operational from 1st September with capacity of 50 machines daily
items.quote: We are excited to announce the launch of our new 11,028 square meter assembly unit, which will significantly enhance our manufacturing capabilities. The facility is set to 50 machines daily.

items.statement: Investment of INR 8-10 crores for new facility with expected payback period of 2-3 years
items.quote: Around INR 8 to INR 12 crores, sir. INR 8 to INR 10 crores, yes

items.statement: Blended EBITDA margin ranges between 15-20%
items.quote: It ranges anything between 15-20%.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margins to reach 16-17% going forward as installed base increases
items.quote: Expected EBITDA margins, I don't see 19%, but we can see that we can touch 16%, 17% sir, 16-17%.

items.statement: Indian coding and printing industry poised for steady growth at 13.4% CAGR annually
items.quote: The Indian coding and printing industry is poised for the steady growth around the CAGR of 13.4% annually with the demand for the advanced printing technology continuing to arise.

items.statement: Consumables contribute ~47-48% of revenue, printer sales 20-28%, spares 15-20%, AMC 10-12%
items.quote: Around sorry, you can say the AMC is around 10% of our total contribution and spares is around 15 -20% of our total contribution of the revenue. 20 -28% will be the printer sale, and the rest are the consumable.

items.statement: Export growth gradual due to need for sales and service support infrastructure; currently 3-4% of revenue
items.quote: As of now, our export revenue is very low. We range around 4%, around 3 -4% of the total revenue comes from exports. And overall, what we can, what we are doing, and what we are expecting to do in the next 1 or 2 years, we want to at least go for a doubling of that in the revenue sense.

items.statement: Jet Inks acquisition expected to contribute 20% revenue increase; synergy benefits over 2-3 year horizon
items.quote: This strategic acquisition significantly enhanced our marketable presence in Southern and Eastern India and is expected to contribute to a 20% increase in our revenue.

items.statement: Working capital days around 45-60 days
items.quote: It's been 45 to 60, but yes, the average you can come down to around 45 to 60 days.

items.statement: BIS compulsory licensing provides regulatory moat; new entrants need 6-12 months to obtain
items.quote: will, depends, but it will take at least 6 months, what we see in normal… Harsh Rawal From 6 months to 1 year

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 11% plus for FY25 and going forward
items.quote: So, our guidance will remain that we will be clocking around 11% margin.

items.statement: Order book INR 34,152 crore as of Sep 2024; L1 bids INR 10,154 crore (now ~INR 7,700 crore); H1 order inflow INR 8,925 crore
items.quote: As of September, our order book stood at INR34,152 crores, of which we have received an order inflow of INR.8,925 crores in the first half of the year, along with L1 bids amounting to INR 10,154 crores.

items.statement: Full-year order booking target INR 25,000 crore (highest ever), including L1 conversion and new bids
items.quote: We have already submitted quite a few bids, and we are submitting further bids. And therefore, we expect a further order booking of not less than INR 5,000 crores. Okay. And taking that into consideration, it will be safe to assume that we may be booking an order for the whole year of INR25,000 crores, which will be the highest in the history of Afcons.

items.statement: Full-year capex reduced vs plan due to TBM delivery shifts; long-term capex run-rate ~3-4% of revenue
items.quote: Generally, we try to maintain in that range only. The capex generally is in that range only of the top line.

items.statement: India construction market expected INR 38.5 trillion by FY28, 10% CAGR FY23-28; overseas markets to outpace global peers 2024-2033
items.quote: India is poised to be the fastest growing construction market globally, expected to reach INR 38.5 trillion by FY28. With the Indian government's focus on enhanced infrastructure spending, it is anticipated the industry will grow at the CAGR of 10% between FY23 and FY28.

items.statement: H1 FY25 revenue split 71% domestic, 29% overseas; order book currently 85% domestic / 15% overseas, targeting 70:30 long-term
items.quote: So as far as the turnover for the half year is concerned, 29% was from overseas market and 71% was from the domestic market.

items.statement: Selective bidding in oil & gas until contracting methodology changes; Middle East largely avoided due to cash-flow negativity and weak dispute resolution; Saudi Arabia selective with local JV
items.quote: On hydrocarbon sector we have kept this thing. We have been making presentations to the government and also to ONGC. We have requested for certain change in contracting methodology and also change in contract administration and while we learned that it is in principle accepted, it is not put into action. So we have taken a position with respect to ONGC that till such time these corrections are mad

items.statement: IPO fresh issue INR 1,250 crore received (INR 1,223 crore net); used for debt repayment, working capital, capex; OFS proceeds to selling shareholder
items.quote: we have received - the company has received INR1,250 crores and after adjusting for the issue expenses, the proceeds have been used by company. Of this, we received some after the expenses, we received some INR1,223 crores. We have used a large po rtion of it towards repayment of debt and towards working capital we have already utilized

items.statement: Net debt INR 2,640 crore (Sep 2024), debt/equity 0.7x; expect significant reduction in H2 FY25 as cash flows improve
items.quote: So, the net debt, we have closed September with INR 2,640 crores. And on the net debt basis, our debt to equity was around 0.7.

items.statement: Full-year operating cash flow expected positive; H1 negative due to delayed certifications/payments and no sizable advances
items.quote: We will be generating operating cash flow positive for the full year, because as I explained that during first half year, generally the payments are not up to date and that gets updated by the year end.

items.statement: Employee cost ~10.5% of revenue, finance cost ~3.5-3.6% for FY25; both expected to decline medium-term via per-employee productivity and lower debt
items.quote: So the employee cost anywhere it will be on the overall year, it will be somewhere around 10.5% or so and finance cost, it will be somewhere around 3.5% to 3.6%.

items.statement: Bangladesh exposure: 4 projects (3 roads, 1 rail); one road project (~INR 600 cr) may be foreclosed without rate revision; payments awaited on others
items.quote: On Bangladesh, we are doing four projects, three road projects and one railway projects. Out of which one road project, we had right from the beginning we have maintained the position because the order itself was given after 19 months of the submission of date. Therefore, without rate revision, we will not commence the work.

items.statement: Order pipeline INR 3.2 lakh crore over next 2 years; urban infra INR 1 lakh crore, surface transport INR 60,000 crore, marine & hydro ~INR 50,000 crore each; 70% domestic / 30% overseas

items.quote: We look to have about 30% of our work subcontracted. Today, we are somewhere between 22% to 25% of our work getting subcontracted. We intend to move to 30% subcontracting.

items.quote: So, our whole of this 4.2 gigawatt is expected to be charged before around 2027.

items.quote: A quarter delay is definitely possible in any of t hese infrastructure projects which Power Grid also is an infrastructure project, whatever they ex ecute, but in bulk of the places where we are doing connectivity, it's more of an equipment rollout or a transmission link strengthening which generally doesn't get delayed

items.statement: IPO proceeds of INR1,800-2,000 crore to retire debt; no equity raise needed per current capex estimates; InvIT not on table
items.quote: with the IPO proceeds that we have received, we plan to retire some of the debt to the tune of roughly I NR1,800 to INR2,000 odd crores

items.quote: You can say around 900 megawatt-odd is coming onli ne in the next financial year

items.quote: Our total revenue for H1 FY25 stood at INR635 cror es, up 5.5% Y-o-Y basis, and for the quarter, it stood at INR295 crores, which is up 7.4% Y-o-Y. EBITDA for the first six months stood at INR558 crores, which is up 4.8% Y-o-Y

items.quote: I think some of the PPAs, we thought that should h ave happened in October, which might happen in this month or in next. name: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Ltd

items.statement: Retail growth trajectory expected at 17%-18% CAGR over next four to five years from mix of volume and value growth
items.quote: Inherently, you know, our own assessment is that the growth trajectory on retail will continue to be a CAGR of 17%-18% over the next four five years.

items.statement: Price increase of around 10% taken for two products contributing 25% of retail portfolio; plan similar increase for one or two products covering 10% of portfolio
items.quote: In terms of price increase, we have taken price increase of around 10% for two products, which contribute around 25% in retail portfolio. And we plan to take, again, some price increase close to 10% for one or two products, which contribute around 10% of the portfolio.

items.quote: Overall, as Mr. Krishnan mentioned, overall, new business grew at a 40% number. Largely, all channels grew in the similar manner. The direct digital and our own digital business grew better than the average.

items.quote: So by the time the year is done, we believe about in the mid-20s is where the overall proportion of business is the multi-year book for us.

items.quote: And as a proportion of our overall book, roughly that number is in the mid-20s. But from, you know, from our standpoint, fro m an economic standpoint, we neutralize, in terms of the incentives that we pay both to our commissions as well as sales incentives to our employees

items.statement: Significant capex program over last 4.5 years: added ~150 offices, grew agency force from 40,000 to ~160,000, bank partners from 12 to 21, own sales headcount 4x
items.period: last four and a half years
items.quote: we've embarked on a significant capex program over the last four and a half years. We have added, you know, 150 odd offices. We have grown our agency strength over the last four years from 40,000 to ~160,000. We have grown our bank partners to from about 12 to about 21. Our own sales headcount has grown 4x in the last four years

items.statement: Investment yield of 7.5% expected to be maintained despite falling G-sec yields due to duration strategy; portfolio is all debt
items.quote: We do not expect this to come down. What we did was implemented a strategy since last two years of investing in duration. items.statement: Digital channel (including Policy Bazaar and direct-to-consumer) has best economics with lowest combined ratio
items.quote: But one thing clear that digital is having better economics, lower combined ratio. That's something I can tell you with certainty.
